conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Root Cause Tracing Method for Industrial Process Systems Based on Extended Convergent Cross Mapping
conference_papers.summary: With the continuous advancement of automation and intelligent operation and maintenance, process industrial systems are gradually evolving toward high-dimensional nonlinearity, multi-agent deep coupling, and strong dynamic interactions. This evolution renders fault propagation increasingly complex, exhibiting cross-unit, cross-level, and even cross-link characteristics. Accurately tracing abnormal propagation paths and precisely locating root causes has thus become a critical prerequisite for ensuring the safe and stable operation of industrial processes. To address these challenges, this study proposes a root cause tracing and diagnostic framework based on Extended Convergent Cross Mapping (ECCM). The framework first constructs a univariate equivalent intervention evaluation model to efficiently screen candidate variables closely associated with faults from high-dimensional data. It then employs ECCM to quantitatively analyze causal relationships among variables, thereby establishing a causal graph under abnormal conditions to reveal the propagation mechanisms and pathways of anomalies. In addition, a set of root cause identification criteria is proposed and combined with a tracing algorithm to recognize key driving variables, enhancing both the accuracy and interpretability of diagnostic results. Finally, experimental validation on the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process demonstrates that, compared with other root cause tracing methods, the proposed approach is more effective in identifying root variables and abnormal propagation paths in strongly coupled systems.
institutions: Ministry of Emergency Management of the People's Republic of China

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Respiratory Rate Estimation from ECG-Derived Respiration and Accelerometer Signals Using Deep Learning in Dynamic Movement Environments
conference_papers.summary: This study aimed to develop a foundational technology for a real-time biosignal monitoring system applicable to the daily lives of older adults by achieving functional light-weighting through the minimization of sensor configurations. To this end, two deep learning-based regression models were implemented to estimate respiratory rate using EDR spectrograms derived from ECG signals, three HRV-based features (RMSSD, SDNN, and Mean RR interval), and ACC data. The experiment was conducted on 210 participants who performed 15 types of daily movements, and the collected biosignals were used to evaluate model performance. Accuracy was defined as the proportion of predictions whose absolute error from the ground truth respiratory rate fell within ±0.05 Hz, ±0.10 Hz, and ±0.20 Hz error margins. As a result, the model using EDR spectrograms and HRV features showed the highest accuracy for fall movements, while the model using EDR and ACC inputs showed relatively high accuracy for daily life movements. This study demonstrates the potential to estimate respiratory rate in dynamic environments without the need for dedicated respiratory sensors. Future work will focus on expanding input data types and enhancing model architectures to further improve prediction accuracy and practical applicability.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on the Digitalization Construction of Quality Spot-check for Nuclear Engineering Design Products
conference_papers.summary: Quality spot checks on design products are a means of supervising the quality of design documents published by design units, and they are a crucial component of the process control in engineering design. With the rapid development of computer networks and information technology, informatization and digitalization have become effective tools for enterprises to reduce management costs and improve management levels. To enhance the efficiency of quality spot checks on design products and the accuracy of design quality evaluations, and to ensure that issues identified during spot checks are effectively resolved, thus improving design quality, there is a necessity for the digitalization of quality spot checks on design products. This paper explores the necessity, current status, key technologies, and implementation strategies of digitalization in quality spot checks of nuclear engineering design products, aiming to improve the efficiency and accuracy of quality evaluations through digital means, thereby supporting the high-quality development of design units.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on the Coal-Fired Boiler Blending Model Optimized by BP Neural Network
conference_papers.summary: With the global energy demand growth and the environmental protection concern, improving the efficiency of coal-fired boilers, reducing pollution emissions, and ensuring the stability of energy supply have become the current focus of energy technology research. This study aims to optimize the blending process of coal-fired boilers through data analysis techniques. A model for studying the blending characteristics of coal-fired boilers based on machine learning has been established. This model employs the DBO-BP neural network algorithm and integrates multiple technical links such as data collection, data preprocessing, establishment and optimization of machine learning models, aiming to deeply analyze and predict the performance of boilers under different blending conditions. Through simulation experiments, the conclusion is drawn: This prediction model can accurately predict the power generation of thermal power plants, with a correlation coefficient of 0.9999, indicating a good fitting degree and high prediction accuracy. A visual interface for the model was realized. The interface not only displays the prediction results, but also shows the input parameters and output parameters of the model, enabling users to intuitively understand the operating status of the boiler. The research provides a solution for improving environmental quality and promoting the development of clean energy.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on the Application of Automatic Loading System for Cartons on Gooseneck Trailers
conference_papers.summary: For the cartonized cargo loading of the gooseneck trailers, an automatic loading system has been studied. Its key technologies include the equipment architecture, the design of the loading vehicle for the adaptive gooseneck platform, using laser radar for the positioning of the vehicle, using a combination of fuzzy control and PID control for the path tracking and deviation correction of the vehicle, the automatic loading control system, and the loading process. After experimental application, the failure rate of the system is 7.96%, and the loading efficiency reaches 642 pc/h, which basically meets the user's requirements. The application of the automatic loading system has played a positive role in reducing manual operations and lowering logistics costs.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Wind Speed Monitoring and Alarm Software Along Songhua River
conference_papers.summary: To ensure the safety of summer ferries along the Songhua River in Harbin, Harbin Meteorological Bureau has deployed meteorological monitoring facilities at key points along the Songhua River. In order to ensure the normal operation of meteorological monitoring facilities, stable transmission of meteorological data, real-time grasp of wind speed data, and timely discuss with the Municipal Transportation Bureau and the municipal Maritime Safety Bureau on countermeasures when the wind speed is too high, business backbones are required to be on duty, causing greater personnel pressure in the manpower intensive flood season. Therefore, this paper studies the wind speed data monitoring and alarm software. When meteorological facilities have problems, meteorological data transmission is abnormal, and the wind speed exceeds the alarm threshold, SMS alarms are sent to business personnel to improve the timeliness of wind speed monitoring, save manpower and material resources in flood season, and effectively improve the automation and intelligent level of wind condition monitoring along the Songhua River.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Underwater Image Enhancement in Complex Scenes
conference_papers.summary: This paper addresses underwater image regression due to factors like light attenuation, colour distortion, scattering, and low contrast, proposing an innovative enhancement model. Traditional techniques, such as histogram equalisation and white balance adjustment, struggle in dynamic underwater environments. We introduce a degradation classification model for detecting issues like colour bias, blurring, and low illumination, combining the grey world hypothesis, Laplace edge detection, and grey-level histogram analysis. A scene degradation model based on the Jaffe-McGlamery framework simulates underwater environmental impacts. To correct chromatic aberration, we propose a model integrating bilateral filtering and reinforcement learning. Lastly, a comprehensive enhancement model combines adaptive gamma correction, blue-optimised histogram equalisation, and super-resolution reconstruction, tailored for complex underwater scenes. Quantitative evaluation shows that the blue-optimised histogram equalisation (BOHE) outperforms alternatives in both UCIQE (128.57) and UIQM (919.61), achieving improvements of 14.80% and 13.61% respectively. These advancements offer significant tools for underwater exploration, marine biology, and autonomous navigation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Trajectory Planning for Industrial Robotic Sorting Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
conference_papers.summary: To the trade-off between cycle time reduction and vibration suppression in high-speed sorting industrial robots, this study proposes an improved particle swarm optimization algorithmSA-PSO integrating nonlinear inertia weight, dynamic learning factors, and simulated annealingSA mechanisms for time-jerk dual-objective trajectory optimization. A two-stage planning framework is established for theUBO-i6 six-degree-of-freedom robot: key sorting path points are defined in Cartesian space, and a C2-continuous joint-space trajectory is generated via quintic B-spline interpolation. The improved algorithm employs a nonlinear exponential decreasing inertia weight strategy and dynamically adjusts learning factors using a sine-square function to balance global exploration and local exploitation. The SA mechanism, which accepts inferior solutions via the Metropolis criterion, enhances global convergence. Matlab simulations demonstrate that under ±0.5 mm positioning accuracy constraints, the proposed method reduces the sorting cycle time from 3.77 s to 3.07 s18.7% reduction and decreases the mean maximum jerk all joints from 14.73°/s3to 7.34°/s3(50.2%) reduction. This significantly improves sorting efficiency while suppressing mechanical vibrations, offering a novel approach for high-speed sorting robot trajectory optimization that balances performance and reliability.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Dynamic Path Planning and Obstacle Avoidance Methods for Low-Power Robots
conference_papers.summary: This paper addresses prevalent challenges faced by contemporary competition robots, including limited computational capacity on low-power computing systems, poor real-time performance in dynamic environment perception, and difficulties in coordinating global path planning with local obstacle avoidance. A hierarchical fusion-based approach for dynamic path planning and obstacle avoidance is proposed. First, at the global planning layer, an improved lightweight algorithm is introduced that significantly reduces node expansion during global path search by preprocessing map topological structures, thereby lowering computational overhead. Second, at the local obstacle avoidance layer, an optimized dynamic window approach integrating temporal difference prediction is designed, enhancing the robot's proactive avoidance capabilities through short-term forecasting of dynamic obstacle motion trends. Finally, an event-triggered replanning mechanism is developed to initiate global replanning only when significant environmental changes occur, avoiding unnecessary computational resource consumption. This method has been successfully implemented in competition robots, providing critical technical support for the research team to achieve outstanding results in high-level domestic and international robotics competitions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Disturbance Rejection Control of Four-Axis Turntable Based on Model Compensation and Variable-Gain Adaptive Control
conference_papers.summary: To address the challenge that four-axis flight simulation turntables, affected by multi-source disturbances such as multi-axis coupling and nonlinear friction, struggle to meet the requirements of "high dynamics, variable load, and coordinated anti-disturbance" for dynamic tracking tests of weaponry, this study proposes a coordinated anti-disturbance control method integrating model pre-compensation, finite-time disturbance observer (FTDOB), and variable-gain model reference adaptive control.The method leverages model precompensation to integrate known information for proactive mitigation of predictable disturbances, thereby reducing the observer burden and enhancing control accuracy. A finite-time disturbance observer incorporating a time-varying scaling function is designed to alleviate the issues of disturbance observation delay and slow anti-disturbance response. A variable-gain algorithm is adopted to dynamically switch parameters, reconciling the trade-off between identification speed and precision. Ultimately, a closed-loop anti-disturbance framework of "model pre-compensation- finite-time observation of residual disturbances - self-optimization of rotational inertia" is established. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the dynamic stability and robustness of the system, enabling high-precision tracking under multi-disturbance conditions. This work provides a reliable technical support for hardware-in-the-loop simulation tests of advanced weaponry.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Data-Driven Abnormal Identification Methods for Coal Mine Gas Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Gas hazards represent a critical safety concern in coal mine operations. To address the limitations of low detection accuracy and inefficient response in existing anomaly identification systems for massive gas time-series data, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional feature fusion-based method for anomaly detection. By constructing a four-dimensional feature profile comprising volatility features, mean-level features, micro-variation features, and trend features, the proposed approach enables automatic localization, identification, and early warning of gas anomalies across extensive monitoring networks. Furthermore, leveraging the Spark Streaming framework, we develop a big data-driven software platform for dynamic feature construction and real-time anomaly detection in coal mine gas monitoring. Field validation demonstrates that this methodology rapidly identifies both early-stage and recent gas anomalies, significantly enhancing the efficiency of anomaly response and management.
institutions: China Coal Technology and Engineering Group Corp (China)

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research of Environmental Risk Assessment Power Grid Construction Stage using Analytic Hierarchy Process
conference_papers.summary: In order to quantitatively assess the environmental risks of power grid enterprises and provide a basis for the control of safety risk sources and the construction of safety production risk management systems, this paper uses the Analytic Hierarchy Process - Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method to conduct environmental risk assessment during the engineering construction stage of power grid enterprises. Based on this, source control is carried out. Firstly, combined with the business process of power grid enterprise project construction during the engineering stage, an environmental risk assessment index system for the power grid enterprise project construction stage is constructed; Secondly, an environmental risk assessment method based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation is established; Finally, through case analysis of power grid enterprises, the quantitative assessment of environmental risks during the engineering construction stage of power grid enterprises is realized, and the source control methods are proposed. The risk assessment scheme and source control methods proposed in this paper have guiding significance for the environmental risk assessment during the power grid engineering construction stage, and also have important reference value for the environmental risk assessment in other business stages of power grid enterprises.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research and Implementation Analysis of Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Health Management Technology for Nuclear Power Plant Equipment
conference_papers.summary: Prognostics Health Management (PHM) technology provides a solution for the transformation of nuclear power plant equipment from "planned maintenance" to "condition-based maintenance." This paper reviews recent research advances in PHM and examined fault classification method and FMECA for various types of nuclear power equipment. It also addresses key technical approaches for implementing PHM within a system engineering framework, with a focus on challenges and solutions encountered during system deployment. The study aims to guide further applied research and engineering implementation of PHM technology in the nuclear power plant. As an equipment-level intelligent system, PHM will serve as a critical foundation for achieving fully intelligent nuclear power plants.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Recognition Technology of Crew Behavioral Errors in Civil Aircraft Cockpits
conference_papers.summary: This study examined the recognition mechanism of pilot behavioral errors in civil aircraft to enhance aviation safety. The occurrence of such errors was first analyzed as the outcome of interactions among multidimensional "human– machine – environment – management" factors. Relevant recognition technologies were then detailed, covering image recognition, speech recognition and natural language processing, task standardization, and scenario database construction. Based on these components, a pilot behavioral error detection and analysis system was developed. The verification results indicated that the system accurately identified pilot behavioral errors, enabled real-time monitoring and early warning, and provided scientific and technical support for aviation safety.
institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Real-Time Robot Perception and Response for Luggage Carrying Service
conference_papers.summary: Service robots are increasingly being developed to assist humans in various environments. However, in public environments, identifying individuals who require luggage handling assistance remains an underexplored area in service robotics. While existing studies focus on surveillance or object tracking, few address perception-driven interaction for assisting people with their belongings. This paper presents the integration and implementation of vision and speech models on a ROS-based mobile robot to identify individuals who may require help with luggage carrying. The proposed system integrates a YOLOv8 object detection model trained on five classes: person, backpack, handbag, paper bag, and suitcase, with an RGB-D camera to obtain depth-based distance measurements. The robot applies specific proximity-based rules to identify a Person of Interest (POI). It initiates interaction with the user through a touchscreen interface. Experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to accurately detect both individuals and luggage, while enabling real-time interaction. Future work will aim to improve detection accuracy in crowded environments, integrate voice-based interaction and enable the robot to identify individuals who genuinely need assistance through behavioural cues.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Real-Time Faulty Wiring Detection in Aircraft Using YOLO Framework with IoT-Enabled Thermal Infrared Imaging and Graph Algorithm for Shortest-Path Analysis
conference_papers.summary: Faulty wiring remains a critical source of electrical failure and fire hazards in aircraft systems. This study presents a real-time dual risk faulty wiring detection that combines IoT-enabled thermal infrared (IR) imaging, a YOLO based architecture for fault-classification model, and a graph-based shortest-path algorithm for spatial risk mapping. Initially, IoT thermal sensors embedded in sensitive aircraft zones capture baseline infrared signatures of healthy wiring. The collected dataset is used to train a YOLO model capable of differentiating normal and faulty heat patterns. During operation, thermal frames are streamed continuously to the onboard system, which detects anomalies and quantifies wiring health on a$0-100 {\%}$scale. Detected faults are then analyzed through a graph algorithm that traces the shortest-path endpoints to identify the most probable propagation routes of thermal or electrical risk. The integrated framework delivers autonomous early warning, fault localization, and health visualization through a cloud dashboard. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high precision in anomaly detection and accurate localization of affected nodes, establishing a reliable foundation for predictive maintenance in aviation systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Radar Operating Mode Classification Method Based on Improved ResNet
conference_papers.summary: In this study, a classification method based on an improved ResNet was proposed to address the limitations of traditional temporal feature extraction methods in the radar operating mode classification task. The one-dimensional signal was first converted to a two-dimensional image using a Gramian Angular Field to preserve periodic and temporal features. To address the problems of insufficient local/global feature differentiation and loss of multiscale frequency information in GAF conversion, this study proposes three improvements. First, Octave Convolution was used instead of standard convolution, which enhances multiscale feature extraction through the separation of high- and low-frequency features and interactions. Second, the Squeeze-and-Excitation Attention Mechanism module was integrated into the residual structure, which strengthened the expression of the key features using adaptive adjustments of the weights of the high- and low-frequency feature channels. Finally, a novel multilayer perceptron architecture was designed to integrate Depthwise Separable Convolution and residual linkage to optimize gradient propagation, and dropout was used to enhance the generalization performance. The experimental results demonstrated that the improved method achieved a classification accuracy of 89.8%, which provides a novel approach for intelligent radar signal processing, offering significant application value. e Self-built dataset, representing a 4.1 percentage point improvement over the benchmark. Furthermore, the AUC for each operating mode showed an enhancement ranging from 4.04% to 4.72%, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the proposed method.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Radar Odometry Using 3D Feature-Assisted ICP
conference_papers.summary: In this study, we propose a radar odometry method based on iterative closest point (ICP) that incorporates 3D feature information. Radar-based localization has been actively studied due to the robust perception capabilities of radar, even under adverse environments. However, radar point clouds are typically sparse, noisy, and contain numerous outliers, which can degrade the accuracy of data association. To address this limitation, our registration method leverages local geometric structure in ICP through 3D feature descriptors. The method utilizes fast point feature histograms to establish initial correspondences between point clouds and integrates feature-based association into the registration process. This enables ICP registration to benefit from geometric structure, even in sparse radar point clouds. Experimental results on public radar datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves improved localization accuracy compared to standard ICP approaches.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Layer-Wise Bias Weight Sensitivity Across Activation Functions in Deep Neural Networks
conference_papers.summary: Bias parameters in deep neural networks critically influence activation function outputs and gradient propagation, yet systematic quantification of their layer-wise sensitivity across different activation functions remains unexplored. This research addresses the fundamental challenge of measuring how bias weight perturbations propagate through network hierarchies and affect model predictions under ReLU, Sigmoid, and TanH activations. A dual-phase analytical framework is implemented that trains sequential networks with exponentially decreasing layer dimensions on three synthetic datasets and applies controlled bias perturbations to quantify layer-specific gradient stability. Experimental results reveal that ReLU maintains consistent 4253% monotonic sensitivity decay across layers, Sigmoid exhibits severe middle-layer suppression (68-76% reduction), and TanH demonstrates steep exponential attenuation (71-85% reduction), establishing that activation function topology fundamentally governs gradient distribution patterns independent of dataset scale along with direct implications for architecture selection and training optimization strategies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Q-Learning-Based Gripper Orientation Correction for a 6-DoF Robotic Manipulator
conference_papers.summary: Accurate end-effector orientation is essential for reliable robotic grasping and manipulation. This paper presents a Q-learning-based approach for autonomous gripper orientation correction of a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) robotic manipulator. The proposed method enables the robot to learn an optimal orientation adjustment policy through interaction with its environment using discrete angular actions on the$6{ }^{\text{th }}$joint (gripper). The approach does not rely on explicit kinematic or dynamic modeling and instead improves performance through trial-anderror learning. The method is implemented and evaluated on a real robotic platform (UFactory-Lite 6). Experimental results demonstrate reliable convergence within approximately 1500 training episodes, achieving accurate alignment between the gripper and the target object. These findings indicate that tabular Q-learning can provide an effective and computationally efficient solution for discrete gripper orientation correction tasks in robotic manipulation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Privacy Impact on AI Classifiers: Paper on Data Perturbation Feedback
conference_papers.summary: This paper investigates the behaviour of Artificial Intelligence (AI) classifiers when exposed to perturbed datasets, reflecting a crucial modelling feedback mechanism for privacyaware Machine Learning (ML). It delves into the challenges presented by the “right to be forgotten” regulations, exploring how the deletion or alteration of significant data points impacts the performance of various ML Algorithms. Through extended experimentation, this paper analyses how classifier accuracy and robustness are affected by different anonymisation and perturbation techniques. The findings provide critical feedback on the trade-offs between data utility for statistical analysis and the imperative of individual privacy protection, guiding the development of more resilient AI systems capable of operating effectively on evolving and privacy-constrained datasets.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Portable Measurement of Catenary Geometry Parameters
conference_papers.summary: Detecting catenary geometric parameters is essential in railway maintenance and operation. Key parameters include contact wire height, stagger at the locator, and steady arm orientation angle, along with automatic number plate recognition for rapid fault localization and improved maintenance workflows. This paper presents a portable detection device that integrates LiDAR and image recognition for automated, high-precision measurement of these parameters. The system simultaneously captures height, stagger, and locator angle while recognizing catenary mast identification numbers. Experimental validation confirms outstanding performance, measurement error within 3%, and recognition accuracy over 90% for both locator angles and number plates. These results demonstrate the device’s reliability and practicality for field deployment in railway systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Policy Real-Time Execution of Reinforcement Learning for Peg-in-Hole Assembly on Resource-Constrained System
conference_papers.summary: The policy of reinforcement learning model exists in neural networks, its execution often requires a certain amount of processing time and computing resource. It is difficult to deploy the reinforcement learning model on the real-time system with limited computing resources. This article proposes a policy real-time execution method of reinforcement learning for peg-inhole assembly on resource-constrained system. Its framework has two stages including a simulation training stage and a real-time assembly stage. In the simulation training stage, a reinforcement learning network is trained in a simulation environment and a state-action table is generated to store the policy. The state-action table replacing the neural network can reduce computational and storage cost and improve efficiency. In the real-time assembly stage, the assembly system queries the state-action table and calculates accurate assembly actions. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method, whose performance is very similar to the performance using neural networks.
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Phase-Shifted Interference Pattern Illumination and Saturation-Sensitive Fusion Imaging for High-Rotation Workpieces
conference_papers.summary: Specular highlights (glints) on highly reflective rotational parts (e.g., cylindrical shafts and rollers) often saturate camera pixels and conceal fine defects. We propose a geometry-aware stripe illumination with saturation-aware fusion for robust imaging under phase-shifted structured patterns. First, we orient the projected stripes perpendicular to the workpiece axis and set a small inclination angle (α) between the axis and the camera plane. This reduces the set of surface normals that satisfy the mirror reflection bisector toward the camera on a cylinder, thereby shrinking the glint region. Second, given a short sequence of phase-shifted stripe images, we perform saturation-aware weighted fusion, which down-weights locally overexposed pixels while preserving stripe fidelity for subsequent processing. Unlike feedback-based adaptive stripe systems that require online intensity modulation, our approach offers built-in glint suppression with a simple geometry setting and a lightweight fusion step, and is complementary to adaptive stripe illumination in prior work. Experiments on representative cylindrical parts demonstrate reduced saturated area and improved defect visibility compared with single-exposure stripes and conventional HDR exposure blending. Our method is motivated by established findings on illumination trade-offs for metallic surfaces and structured-highlight geometry on specular objects, while targeting large-scale rotational parts in practical inspection scenarios.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Personalized EEG-Based Passthought Authentication Using Custom-Fit Ear Devices: A Secure, Multi-Factor Approach
conference_papers.summary: This study investigates the feasibility of utilizing a single custom-fit earpiece equipped with embedded electroencephalogram (EEG) electrodes for authentication based on userspecific mental tasks, termed passthoughts. Passthoughts represent a novel biometric solution that enhances security while ensuring user-friendliness by leveraging unique brainwave patterns associated with individual cognitive activities. In our experiments, We achieved an impressive authentication accuracy of 99.82% using three small electrodes integrated into a custom earpiece, which significantly surpasses the performance of existing EEG-based authentication methods. Our system effectively combines both inherence factors, represented by the individual's unique brain activity, and knowledge factors, derived from the cognitive tasks that users voluntarily perform. Furthermore, our authentication method has demonstrated robustness against various spoofing attempts, as attackers faced substantial challenges in attempting to replicate the specific passthoughts associated with individuals. This highlights the inherent security advantages of our approach. Although the study's sample size is relatively small, the results strongly suggest the potential of ear-EEG systems for practical everyday authentication applications, showcasing favorable outcomes in terms of task memorability and user satisfaction. We also critically examine several limitations of our study, including the need for greater sample diversity and the constraints imposed by controlled experimental settings. To address these limitations, we propose future research directions that include testing our authentication system in a wider range of real-world environments, expanding the sample size to enhance generalizability, and improving usability through the development of dry electrode technology. Ultimately, our work lays the groundwork for a robust and discreet authentication method, particularly wellsuited for high-security applications as well as those requiring enhanced accessibility for users. The integration of personalized EEG readings with a practical form factor presents an innovative avenue for advancing secure authentication in an increasingly digital world.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Person of Interest Detection Using Deep Learning in a Real-Time Faculty Receptionist Robot
conference_papers.summary: New students often turn to faculty receptionists for information related to their studies or about the faculty. Sometimes students will come alone to ask questions, while at other times they will come in pairs or groups. During an interaction, the receptionist will identify the person of interest (POI) and focus on that person. In this work, we are exploring a perception module for receptionist robots to detect the POI, which can help to improve human-robot interaction (HRI). YOLOv8 and Support Vector Regression (SVR) are used to train the POI detection model. The model includes three modules: face detection, hand raise detection, and head pose estimation. The models are tested and evaluated to determine their performance level. The mean average precision (mAP50) for face detection and hand raise detection are 96.3% and 99.4% respectively. Meanwhile, the head pose estimation has achieved a mean average error (MAE) of 3.58°.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Path Departure Risk Assessment and Hierarchical Longitudinal Control for Autonomous Mining Trucks
conference_papers.summary: Autonomous Mining Trucks (AMT) are extensively deployed in open-pit mining areas. When AMT experience path departure, collisions with road boundaries or obstacles may occur, leading to severe consequences. This necessitates specialized path departure risk assessment and safety control strategies. In this paper, an enhanced Time to Lane Crossing (TLC)-based departure risk quantification method and a collision detection-based collision risk quantification method are proposed, and a hierarchical longitudinal control strategy is developed building upon these quantifications. Experiments using actual AMT operational data from mining sites demonstrate that the proposed safety protection control strategy computes appropriate deceleration commands based on risk quantification results, enabling timely safety interventions before path departure or collisions occur, thereby ensuring AMT operational safety.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Partitioned EEG Model for Emotion Recognition and Lightweight Deployment
conference_papers.summary: Mental health disorders, especially depression, pose a growing challenge to global public health. However, early detection of depression remains difficult because current diagnostic approaches largely rely on subjective assessments. In this context, electroencephalogram (EEG) signals have attracted considerable attention, as they provide objective and quantifiable neural biomarkers that can capture subtle brain activity patterns associated with emotional states. Different emotions generated by the human brain can, to a large extent, be represented by the distinct characteristics of EEG signals. The aim of this study was to design neuronetworks to recognize brain emotions, in particular three types including positive, neutral and negative emotions, then applying it to the microcontroller (Rasberry Pi) after model optimization. A three partitioned model was constructed to capture the corresponding three types of emotions. A ONNX model was created with the use of dynamic quantization method to help run the model in a light devices as easy as possible. The accuracy of 99.65 % with only 0.83 ms inference latency tested on the microcontroller has shown model's great capability in lightweight devices deployment. This indicates that there is a possibility of achieving real-time emotion recognition in resource-constrained environments, making it possible for preventing the bad impact of negative feeling in a early time.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Optimizing EEG Signal Quality and Streaming Performance in BCIs Using ADS1299EEG-FE
conference_papers.summary: Reliable and noise-free electroencephalography (EEG) acquisition is a key factor in building effective braincomputer interface (BCI) systems. This paper presents an evaluation of methods for optimizing EEG signal quality and realtime streaming performance using the ADS1299EEG-FE platform. The study compares hardware-based noise reduction strategiessuch as active shielding and grounding-with software-level filtering and adaptive preprocessing techniques to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) under varying environmental conditions. In addition, an edge-based streaming setup using a Raspberry Pi was implemented to test the performance of realtime EEG data transmission to a cloud analytics platform. Experimental results showed that the optimized configuration achieved up to a 35% reduction in power line noise and a 40% improvement in signal stability during continuous recording, while maintaining low data latency suitable for BCI feedback applications. The outcomes demonstrate that ADS1299EEG-FE can serve as a reliable, low-cost, and scalable solution for EEG data acquisition in both research and educational environments. These findings contribute to ongoing efforts to make EEG-driven intelligent systems more accessible and efficient for neurotechnology applications.
institutions: Oguz Han Engineering and Technology University of Turkmenistan

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Optimization of Ciliary Magnetic-Driven Soft Robot Based on Gradient Magnetization
conference_papers.summary: Inspired by ciliate microorganisms such as Paramecium, this study designs and optimizes a cilia-driven magnetic soft robot based on gradient magnetization. The robot is primarily composed of a non-magnetic body and magnetic ciliary legs embedded with hard magnetic particles, aiming to achieve efficient and controllable locomotion. Finite element simulation was employed to systematically analyze the influence of external magnetic field parameters and the connection method of the hinge-like structure on the robot's leg deformation and locomotion efficiency. Through experimental optimization of the driving magnetic field parameters, the optimal driving conditions were determined to be$7 \text{mT}, 20 \text{Hz}$, and a duty cycle of 0.6, under which the robot's locomotion speed increased by approximately 40%. Furthermore, trajectory planning experiments verified that the robot can achieve stable and controllable movement at the air-liquid interface under these optimized conditions, with a mean trajectory tracking error of$429.8 \pm 289.2 \mu \mathrm{m}$. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the structural optimization and magnetic field control methods.
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Robotics and Systems

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Multi-Directional Cursor Control via Motor Imagery-Based BCI Using Scalp EEG: A Comparative Machine Learning Approach
conference_papers.summary: A brain-computer interface (BCI) is a system that acquires, processes, and converts neural impulses into computer commands. The brain undergoes recurrent, rhythmic electrical fluctuations induced by these activities, characterized by a minimal voltage of merely a few microvolts (μV). The word electroencephalogram (EEG) denotes the non-invasive capture of electrical activity from the scalp. The signals are subsequently processed by a computer to determine the intended action following signal capture. This study develops a Motor Imagery-based BCI system for multi-directional mouse cursor control using EEG data from the Emotiv EPOC+ headset, analyzed through a custom MATLAB algorithm. Although analogous studies exist, the majority concentrate on certain facets of data processing, such as classification. This study established an experimental paradigm for data recording, involving approximately 18 healthy participants in the data collection process. After the exploration of signal processing algorithms and feature extraction techniques, a comparative analysis of machine learning algorithms was performed. Moreover, accuracy was evaluated across various frequency bands, with the FineTree algorithm attaining the best accuracy of 85.56% on the offline dataset.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Modeling and Parameter Estimation of Spastic Torque for Upper Limb Rehabilitation Robots
conference_papers.summary: This study addresses the challenge of muscle spasticity commonly observed during upper limb rehabilitation in stroke patients. A dynamic model of the upper limb rehabilitation robot is developed, incorporating spastic torque disturbances. Based on the anatomical and physiological properties of human musculoskeletal structures, a bio¬mechanical model of major elbow muscles is constructed using the classical Hill model to describe both active and passive muscle forces. A time-varying spastic torque disturbance model is then proposed, characterizing the influence of training duration and spasticity intensity. To estimate the uncertain parameters in real time, an empirical Bayesian estimation algorithm is designed, and its convergence and asymptotic optimality are mathematically proven. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively tracks the spastic torque parameters with high accuracy. This work provides a theoretical foundation for enhancing the adaptive capability of rehabilitation robots in handling spastic disturbances and contributes to the development of personalized and intelligent rehabilitation training strategies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Magnetometer-Aided Proprioceptive Factor Graph for Legged Robot Localization
conference_papers.summary: The state-of-the-art legged robot localization algorithms typically rely on both proprioceptive data and exteroceptive systems such as LiDAR, vision, and GNSS, fused using smoothing or filtering methods like Factor Graph Optimization or the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). However, such methods are limited to environments with distinct features or robots containing specific hardware, specifically high quality GNSS receiver. This paper presents a Factor-graph-based localization framework that uses only proprioceptive sensing IMU and motor encoder kinematics - augmented with magnetometer yaw observations. The method is implemented on a Unitree Go2 quadrupedal robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and evaluated across five trajectories. The results show that the proposed approach achieves stable, drift-minimized localization, with a maximum deviation of less than 4% of the total trajectory length.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: MVOD - A Multi-View Fusion Network for 3D Obstacle Detection with Point Clouds and Images
conference_papers.summary: In environmental perception for autonomous driving, LiDAR-camera fusion is crucial for accurate obstacle detection. However, single-level fusion methods have limitations: data-level projection loses 3D point cloud features; feature-level fusion struggles with heterogeneous data; and decision-level fusion fails in high-conflict scenarios. To address these, we propose MVOD, a multi-level fusion network cascading data-, feature-, and decisionlevel fusion. At the data level, we generate depth maps while preserving point cloud side and bird's-eye views, constructing a multi-view feature carrier to retain 3D information. At the feature level, we build a fusion module with dedicated extractors for different views, unified under the bird's-eye view (BEV) perspective. At the decision level, inputs combine feature-level fusion results and point cloud side-view detections, with improved Dempster-Shafer(D-S) evidence theory resolving traditional conflict misjudgements. On the KITTI dataset, MVOD achieves$81.57 \% \text{mAP}$, surpassing the baseline by 9.81 %, demonstrating substantial accuracy improvement. With short single-frame processing time, it enables inference on low-power embedded devices and meets real-time autonomous driving requirements.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: ML-Based Early Warning Systems for ERP-Integrated Loan Portfolios
conference_papers.summary: The paper is targeted at the application of the machine learning (ML) when constructing the early warning system (EWS) to the lending book to the enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems directly. There is an assumption that it would raise credit risks on a perfect level in the first stage and helping to make superior financial decisions. The accuracy and the reliability between the various ML models with respect to one another comprised random forest, the Gradient boosting and bi LSTM under qualitative literature review and analysis in the previous. The results show that the offered integrated ML systems deployed in the ERP can, in addition, add value to both the monitoring and delays to the accuracy with which prediction is possible. The article mentions the newly increasing importance of AI and ML in terms of risk management of the banking industry under the present circumstances.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Linear Time-Varying Model Predictive Control for Emergency Collision Avoidance of Four-Wheel-Steering Vehicles
conference_papers.summary: Emergency collision-avoidance maneuvers demand rapid and coordinated vehicle responses, especially when both longitudinal and lateral dynamics become highly coupled. Conventional trajectory tracking controllers-typically based on simplified single-track or constant-speed models-often neglect these coupling effects, resulting in degraded control accuracy and stability under high-speed evasive conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a linear time-varying model predictive control (LTV-MPC) framework for emergency collision avoidance and trajectory tracking of four-wheel-steering (4WS) vehicles. The controller is derived from a nonlinear seven-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamics model and linearized around the current operating point to ensure real-time solvability. It jointly regulates longitudinal driving force and steering angle to minimize tracking errors along a preplanned evasive trajectory. A closed-loop simulation platform based on Carsim and MATLAB/Simulink is established to validate the control performance under double lane-change and sudden obstacleavoidance scenarios. Results demonstrate that the proposed LTVMPC achieves superior trajectory tracking accuracy, stability, and computational efficiency compared with conventional DPID-LQR and DPID-MPC controllers, providing a feasible real-time solution for safety-critical vehicle maneuvers.
institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Malicious Packet Generation in Simulated V2X Frameworks
conference_papers.summary: With the rapid development of Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies, real-time interactions among vehicles, roadside units, pedestrians, and communication networks have become a vital component of intelligent transportation systems (ITS). However, the high connectivity and complexity of V2X systems also introduce significant cybersecurity risks. Attackers who can manipulate packets or mislead system decisions pose considerable threats to vehicle safety. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in natural language processing and code generation, showing potential for generating adversarial attacks. This study develops a simulation framework based on Taiwan's TCROS standard and Eclipse-MOSAIC, integrating LLMs to automate the generation of malicious packets. By utilizing prompt engineering and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the framework enables LLMs to comprehend and alter legitimate TCROS packets for adversarial purposes. Four attack scenarios are designed to evaluate the LLMs' ability to modify packets, recover from errors, achieve success rates, and assess their impact on simulated traffic. Results indicate that, with appropriate prompt design and domain knowledge, LLMs can effectively generate structurally valid attack packets that disrupt system behavior. This research validates the potential of LLMs as cybersecurity threats in V2X systems and offers new insights and datasets for designing future defense mechanisms.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Latency Analysis in Internal Layers of Shared Memory Communication in ROS2
conference_papers.summary: Inter-process communication is essential for autonomous mobile robots that process large amounts of sensor data at high frequencies. Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) provides various communication methods, including shared memory communication using Data Distribution Service (DDS). However, detailed analysis of latency in the internal layers has not been sufficiently conducted. In this study, we investigated the latency of internal layers in shared memory communication using iceoryx. By modifying RMW (ROS MiddleWare) and adding timestamp recording at the boundaries between ROS2 and DDS, the sources of the overall latency were separated into ROS2 and DDS components. Latency was evaluated for data sizes from 1 KB to 10 MB. The results showed that the overall latency was reduced to less than half compared to socket communication. Most of the difference was attributed to DDS. The parts performing input and output from DDS were significantly reduced through zero-copy implementation. Based on these findings, we discussed improvement strategies and the methodology for selecting measurement positions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: LCDTwin: LLM-Driven Contextual Digital Twin for Actuator-Sensor Correlation in ICS
conference_papers.summary: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) suffer from a lack of explainability in anomaly detection due to reliance on scarce domain expertise and opaque models. To address this, we propose LCDTwin, an LLM-Driven Contextual Digital Twin, which is a reasoning framework for interpretable anomaly detection. LCDTwin uses a frozen LLM to infer and maintain humanreadable rules that describe normal sensor-actuator logic, which are continuously updated through a similarity-based mechanism without retraining. During inference, the LLM performs contextual reasoning to detect logical deviations from these learned rules. Evaluated on the SWaT dataset's P1 process, LCDTwin achieved robust performance, with GPT-5-mini showing the best balance (F1-score 0.67, Recall 1.00). Crucially, the lightweight models like GPT-5-nano offer cost-efficient operation (0.24 USD per 6h) with low latency. LCDTwin's approach grounds every detection in an explicit rule violation, providing human-readable explanations that significantly enhance operational transparency and trustworthiness.
institutions: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Power Supply Management System
conference_papers.summary: The structure of the intelligent energy supply management system is given. The functioning of the intelligent energy supply management system is described to ensure the required level of user comfort, taking into account the minimization of financial costs for electrical energy. A mechanism for energy maneuvering of electricity consumption volumes and intelligent control of the energy supply system is proposed in the article.
institutions: National Technical University of Ukraine “Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute”

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Multi-Operational RADAR (IMOR)-Based Soft Landing of UAVs on Unknown Terrain
conference_papers.summary: For the safe and efficient real-time operation of micro and small-class Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), functionalities such as precise altitude measurement, flat terrain detection for emergency landings, and soft landing capabilities are essential. This paper introduces a lightweight RADAR powered sensing platform, Intelligent Multi-Operational RADAR (IMOR) designed for UAV applications. With dynamically configurable chirp settings, IMOR independently supports both high-altitude measurement and flat terrain detection, while also enabling soft landing on identified flat surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate that IMOR outperforms some existing sensors in terms of size, weight, power consumption, versatility, and computational efficiency, thereby enhancing the safety and reliability of micro and small-class UAV operations.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Arc Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Principal Component Analysis and Decision Tree
conference_papers.summary: Arc faults pose significant hazards in low-voltage electrical systems, often leading to fires and equipment damage. Their current signatures vary widely with load conditions, making conventional amplitude- or threshold-based methods insufficient for accurate detection. This paper proposes an intelligent arc fault diagnosis method that integrates Principal Component Analysis with a Decision Tree classifier. Eight time-domain features are extracted from current waveforms, and Principal Component Analysis is employed to generate three principal components that capture the dominant characteristics while reducing redundancy. A Decision Tree constructed using the Classification and Regression Tree algorithm is then applied for rapid classification under diverse load scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves more than 95% identification accuracy, improving by roughly 15% compared with models without dimensionality reduction. The method offers high efficiency, strong real-time performance, and reliable stability, demonstrating its potential for enhancing protection and control in electrical systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Integrated Decision Making and Planning for Autonomous Driving Based on the Prediction of Ego Vehicle
conference_papers.summary: Decision making and planning are critical components of Autonomous Driving (AD) systems. The integrated decision making and planning approach captures the coupling between these two modules, offering enhanced interpretability and intelligence. However, in highly dynamic complex driving environments, existing integrated modeling approaches suffer from high time complexity or poor applicability. In this article, we present a soluble and intelligent framework called Integrated Decision Making and Planning (IDMP), which decompose the AD decision making and planning problem into two layers: optimal trajectory selection layer and optimal trajectory tracking layer. The optimal trajectory selection layer leverages historical planning information to predict the ego vehicle’s trajectory and employs a fast decision making strategy based on the predicted trajectory to select the optimal path, which is subsequently tracked to achieve a tightly coupled decision making and planning module. Based on these, we designed a closed-loop structure composed of upper-layer decision guidance and lower layer planning feedback. Finally, we validated the proposed framework through comparative experiments using the CARLA-SUMO simulation. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method has advantages in a series of complex autonomous driving scenarios.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Industrial Process Root Cause Analysis Method Based on Graph Neural Networks and Knowledge Graphs
conference_papers.summary: Root cause analysis in industrial processes is crucial for ensuring production safety and improving system reliability. Existing methods suffer from limitations in effectively combining domain knowledge with industrial data, making it challenging to provide accurate online root cause diagnosis. This paper proposes a Graph Neural Network and Knowledge Graph-based Root Cause Analysis framework (GNN-RCA) that leverages graph neural networks to learn fault features and incorporates knowledge graphs for fault propagation reasoning. Specifically, we construct a prior industrial knowledge graph to represent physical relationships among equipment, design a temporal graph autoencoder to extract fault contribution scores, and implement root cause reasoning through a fault propagation algorithm. Experimental results on the Tennessee Eastman Process dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in root cause identification accuracy while maintaining good interpretability and real-time performance.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Implementing Real-Time Retail Shelf Monitoring via YOLOv8 on a ROS-Based Mobile Robot
conference_papers.summary: Maintaining optimal shelf inventory and product availability is critical in the contemporary retail landscape to maximise sales and customer satisfaction. The demand for service robots is increasing, but few existing works have explored retail product detection, classification, and counting on a robotic platform. This paper presents an automated, real-time system for monitoring retail products. The primary goal is to detect, classify, and count retail products on shelves to streamline inventory management and minimise stockouts. This work utilised the YOLOv8 object detection model, selected for its superior balance of speed and accuracy, and trained it on the Freiburg Groceries Dataset. The system was implemented on a robot based on ROS. The model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 88.3%, and completed detection within 3 seconds, showcasing a robust and scalable solution for automated retail product management.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Implementation of Speech Processing using Whisper AI and GPT in Real-Time Faculty Receptionist Robot
conference_papers.summary: The increasing number of students being admitted to the university often leads to long queues at the faculty reception counters. Meanwhile, receptionists are forced to address repetitive inquiries. This study presents the development and integration of a speech-based receptionist robot designed to ease the workload of faculty receptionists by automating interactions with students and visitors. The proposed system integrates the Whisper AI model for speech recognition and a customised GPT-based module for context-aware question answering. The Google Text-to-Speech (gTTS) library is used to synthesise responses into natural speech, which is deployed on a ROS platform for enhanced human-robot interaction (HRI). Experimental results demonstrated that the speech recognition module achieved a Word Error Rate (WER) accuracy of 82% while the GPT-based question-answering module obtained an F1-score of 86.96%. The system successfully responded within 10 seconds on average, demonstrating its robustness and practicality in real-world environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Implementation of Real-Time Proctoring Assistant Robot Route Planning for Exam Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Academic dishonesty has risen following the return to in-person examinations after the COVID-19 pandemic, with students adopting increasingly sophisticated methods to evade supervision. Existing proctoring robots are typically limited to online environments or fixed monitoring setups, making them unsuitable for dynamic, crowded examination halls. Safe navigation in classroom settings is further complicated by narrow desk layouts, occlusions, and low-profile obstacles that conventional LiDAR sensors often fail to detect. This paper presents a SLAM-based proctoring assistant robot designed to support human invigilators during physical examinations. The system integrates real-time SLAM navigation, enhanced obstacle detection, and dynamic waypoint-based path planning to enable autonomous patrolling in constrained classroom environments. A randomised zig-zag patrol strategy ensures full-area coverage while reducing route predictability. To compensate for LiDAR's limitations, a YOLOv8n-based vision module was incorporated, achieving a detection accuracy of 83.33% despite the limited training data. The waypoint navigation module demonstrated reliable performance, completing all$\mathbf{5} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{5}$trials without collision. Experimental results indicate that the proposed system offers a safe, efficient, and effective automated proctoring solution for modern examination settings.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Imagining the Rare: Diffusion-Augmented and Few-Shot Learning Approaches for Severely Imbalanced Mushroom Species Classification
conference_papers.summary: Fine-grained species recognition faces critical challenges from extreme class imbalance, where rare species essential for biodiversity monitoring often have fewer than 10 training samples. We present a comprehensive study comparing two complementary approaches for automated mushroom classification: diffusion-based synthetic augmentation with multi-stage quality control, and prototypical few-shot learning with balanced sampling. Using the Danish Fungi 2020 Mini dataset (182 species, 38.5:1 imbalance ratio), we demonstrate that diffusion augmentation excels at moderately rare classes ($10-50$samples), improving balanced accuracy to 53.01% and macro F1 to 52.88%, while few-shot learning achieves 72.68% accuracy on extremely rare species ($<10$samples) through rapid adaptation. Our novel hybrid framework combining both approaches reaches 76.34% episode accuracy. Critical to success is our two-stage quality control pipeline using CLIP semantic verification (threshold 0.75) and FID distributional filtering (threshold 30), which proves essential, gated augmentation outperforms ungated by 5.78 percentage points while maintaining 74.8% sample acceptance. For the 46 rarest species, our methods achieve substantial F1-score improvements:$\mathbf{1 7. 3 {\%}}$(diffusion),$\mathbf{2 2. 6 {\%}}$(few-shot), and 26.8% (hybrid). All implementations, models, and synthetic datasets are publicly available to advance ecological computer vision research.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Identification and Tracking of Multiple Objects on a Peristaltic Conveyor System
conference_papers.summary: The courier express parcel industry has demonstrated considerable volumetric growth in shipment activity throughout the preceding years. In order to enhance the performance and throughput of the material flow technology without compromising on space requirements at distribution centers, various methods are being developed, and their feasibility is being investigated. One such method includes the development of a robust object identification system that is able to identify and track objects for longer duration. Artificial intelligence based methods that utilize You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning architecture have been shown to reliably detect and identify objects in several applications provided that there is enough highquality training data. The aim of this work is to detect and track multiple objects on the Peristaltic Conveyor System (PCS) using YOLO-based detection along with existing tracking algorithms, and to estimate the real-time location and dimensions of these objects. The reliability of the detection and tracking approaches is evaluated by comparing their performance using appropriate detection and tracking metrics.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: ISOCAL-DDMR - Isostatic Calibration Platform for Differential Drive Mobile Robots
conference_papers.summary: Odometric accuracy remains a key limitation in Differential Drive Mobile Robots (DDMRs), as small structural inaccuracies or wheel slippage accumulate and cause localization errors. Traditional calibration methods, such as the UMBmark procedure, are reliable but demand large physical spaces and controlled conditions rarely available in research or educational settings. To overcome these constraints, this paper presents ISOCAL-DDMR - a novel controlled experimental platform integrating isostatic structural principles for dynamic wheelbase measurement. Unlike conventional static methods, ISOCAL-DDMR continuously estimates the wheel separation in real time, ensuring greater physical consistency of odometric parameters. Built upon open-source hardware and software, it employs an ESP32 microcontroller interfaced with LS7366R counters and HX711 strain-gauge converters for deterministic pulse acquisition and structural monitoring. Experiments with the DN2 robotic base show that the proposed method reduces systematic errors and achieves statistical equivalence with real-environment displacements, as verified through Welch's t-tests ($p > 0.05$). To the best of the authors' knowledge, ISOCAL-DDMR provides a novel and accessible solution for reproducible odometry calibration, bridging the gap between theory and experimental practice.
