conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Hyper-AI–Driven Acceleration of Multi-Database Integrated Genomic Analysis for Infectious Disease Response
conference_papers.summary: Rapid identification of emerging pathogens is essential for preserving the epidemiological golden time during infectious disease outbreaks. This paper presents a Hyper-AI-driven framework that accelerates multi-database integrated genomic analysis to support real-time epidemic response. The system links heterogeneous genomic repositories (including NCBI, GISAID, and K-Genome) through a federated interface and employs an AI-accelerated pipeline combining transformer-based sequence encoders with graph neural networks for relational genomic inference [4], [5]. By optimizing key stages of NextGeneration Sequencing (NGS) analysis and deploying adaptive GPU scheduling across cloud–edge–HPC infrastructures, the proposed platform reduces total processing time by up to$4.5 \times$while maintaining 96.8% accuracy in variant detection. Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency relative to conventional BWA+GATK pipelines and non-AI GPU baselines. Designed as part of the broader HYPER-AI continuum, the framework functions as the cognitive layer of an embodied, robotics-enabled epidemicresponse infrastructure, enabling near–real-time genomic interpretation, rapid identification of viral mutations, and crossdatabase surveillance. These findings highlight the feasibility of AIorchestrated, distributed genomic analytics for next-generation public-health preparedness and lay the foundation for extensions into autonomous laboratory systems, continual learning for emerging strains, and multi-omics fusion.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Hydraulic Soft Gripper for Human-Safe Manipulation: Design, Modeling, and Validation
conference_papers.summary: Soft robotic grippers enable safe, adaptable manipulation of irregular and fragile objects, yet achieving precise force control and repeatable performance remains challenging. This paper presents a hydraulically actuated soft finger composed of a TPU kerf-patterned elastomer base and four soft actuators, each formed by a silicone tube laterally constrained by a linear spring. A continuum mechanics model based on incompressible Mooney-Rivlin theory is developed to relate internal pressure to actuator stretch, enabling controlled elongation via a linear slider. By tuning the relative length of opposing filaments, the finger achieves desired bending angles. The model demonstrates strong agreement with experimental results (average$\mathbf{R}^{2}=0.9912$) and is further validated through Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Finally, strategies for precise configuration control of the gripper and its potential applications are discussed.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Hybrid-based Movie Recommendation System Using Machine Learning Techniques
conference_papers.summary: The necessity for sophisticated recommender systems in movie recommendation sphere has become particularly pronounced to generate a more personalized movie recommendation due to people nowadays like to watch movies online. This paper aims to fill this gap by developing a hybrid recommender system to provide better movie recommendation that matches user preferences. The first proposed hybrid model combines Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Cosine Similarity, and Random Forest Regressor (RFR). The second hybrid-based movie recommender system is the combination of Logistic Regression (LR) and Decision Tree (DT). Evaluation results indicated that the LR+DT hybrid outperforms the other model. The significance of this output lies in its potential to revolutionize the movie recommendation landscape by offering personalized movie watching experiences that could lead to higher user satisfaction.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sensor Fusion for Accurate and Real-Time Smart Grid Current Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Cyber-Physical Systems depend on precise, reliable, and real-time sensing to enable advanced monitoring, secure operations, and safety. While classical sensors are characterized by high responsiveness, they are limited to noise and drift faults. Whereas, quantum sensors offer high precision, yet suffer from slow update rates, expensive, and real-time implementation. Existing studies have highlighted the superior accuracy and stability of quantum sensors over classical sensors. However, the integration of classical and quantum sensors is vital to tackle the limitation of individual sensing technologies and to develop more resilient sensing systems. To address this gap, this article proposes a hybrid quantum-classical data fusion framework based on a Kalman filter. The Kalman filter efficiently handles heterogeneous signals with different dynamics and sampling rates, combining the rapid responsiveness of classical sensors with the accuracy of quantum devices. Furthermore, a smart grid system is presented as a proof of concept to demonstrate the practical methodology for the deployment of the proposed framework. Finally, experimental validation is performed to evaluate the performance of the hybrid fusion approach, achieving real-time, robust measurements with an accuracy of up to 94%.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Human Motion Capture with Sparse IMUs and a Single RGB Camera: A Confidence-Based Fusion Framework with Physical Constraints
conference_papers.summary: Motion capture systems that rely on visual tracking or inertial sensing often face challenges regarding accuracy, robustness, and adaptability in diverse environments. Integrating multiple modalities offers a promising solution for lightweight human motion capture, but it introduces challenges such as sensor-skeleton alignment, fusion of sparse and noisy data, and ensuring consistent performance across diverse motion patterns and environmental conditions. To address these limitations, we propose a novel two-stage optimization framework that combines data from a single RGB camera and sparse inertial measurements. In the first stage, we integrate 2D keypoints and silhouettes extracted from a pretrained visual motion capture model with 3D poses in SMPL format from a sparse inertial motion capture model. A unified skeleton and sensor calibration method is introduced to align the visual and inertial coordinate systems. Confidence models evaluate pose estimation errors dynamically, and a joint optimization minimizes weighted mean squared error (MSE) terms. In the second stage, inverse dynamics optimization incorporates physical constraints, such as contact points, to refine motion reconstruction for physically plausible results. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior pose estimation accuracy compared to existing works, making it suitable for a wide range of human motion capture applications.
institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: High-Precision Measurement of Load Position and Speed in Harmonic Servo Drives with Dual-Side Resolvers
conference_papers.summary: To achieve accurate motor commutation and highprecision load-side control, resolvers are typically mounted on both the motor side and the load side in harmonic servo drives. However, the measurement accuracy of load-side motion information is limited by the intrinsic accuracy of resolver. Meanwhile, the motor-side resolver can not provide effective auxiliary information for load-side measurement due to inherent kinematic errors of harmonic reducer. In this paper, a highprecision measurement scheme for load-side motion information using dual-side resolvers is proposed. Firstly, a kinematic error estimator is designed using both motor-side and load-side measurements. Then, the estimated kinematic errors are used to compensate the indirect measurement values based on motorside resolver to suppress the effect of kinematic errors. Finally, the proposed strategy can fully exploit dual-side resolver data to enhance the detection accuracy of load-side motion information and overcome the precision limits of resolver. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: HEART-Bot: A Human-Following Elderly Assistance Mobile Robot with Health Monitoring and Tracking
conference_papers.summary: The rising demand for assistance solutions for elderly people motivates the creation of intelligent robotic systems that combine mobility assistance and services such as continuous heart rate monitoring. This research describes a human-following mobile robot that combines mobility support and real-time heart rate monitoring to improve safety, independence, and quality of life of the elderly. The developed robotic system uses a Raspberry Pi-based controller with a vision-driven human detection module for reliable person-following and ultrasonic sensors for obstacle avoidance in dynamic situations. In parallel, a wearable healthmonitoring device built using NodeMCU and the MQTT protocol continuously monitors the user's heart rate and sends data to the robot for real time monitoring. Experimental validation demonstrates the robot's capacity to smoothly follow a user, safely navigate around obstacles, and reliably monitor heart rate. Design criteria are convenience, compactness, and adaptability with mobility assistance and integrated health monitoring, serving as functional requirements.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Guaranteed Cost Consensus for Multi-Agent Systems Under Event/Self-Triggered Mechanism
conference_papers.summary: This paper studies the event/self-triggered consensus problem for multi-agent systems in terms of saving control costs and communication resources. Based on the dynamic eventtriggered mechanism, a designed weighting matrix is integrated into the triggering condition for better consensus performance and fewer triggering times such that a Zeno-free event-triggered control strategy is established, as well as the corresponding selftriggered mechanism is also given. By setting a control cost index composed of the relative neighboring errors and control signals, the consensus is reached with a guaranteed overall cost. Numerical simulation validates the given method.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Graph Your Way to Inspiration: Integrating Co-Author Graphs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Model Based Scientific Idea Generation
conference_papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate potential in the field of scientific idea generation. However, the generated results often lack controllable academic context and traceable inspiration pathways. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a scientific idea generation system called GYWI, which combines author knowledge graphs with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to form an external knowledge base to provide controllable context and trace of inspiration path for LLMs to generate new scientific ideas. We first propose an author-centered knowledge graph construction method and inspiration source sampling algorithms to construct external knowledge base. Then, we propose a hybrid retrieval mechanism that is composed of both RAG and GraphRAG to retrieve content with both depth and breadth knowledge. It forms a hybrid context. Thirdly, we propose a Prompt optimization strategy incorporating reinforcement learning principles to automatically guide LLMs optimizing the results based on the hybrid context. To evaluate the proposed approaches, we constructed an evaluation dataset based on arXiv (2018-2023). This paper also develops a comprehensive evaluation method including empirical automatic assessment in multiplechoice question task, LLM-based scoring, human evaluation, and semantic space visualization analysis. The generated ideas are evaluated from the following five dimensions: novelty, feasibility, clarity, relevance, and significance. We conducted experiments on different LLMs including GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-8B, and Gemini 2.5. Experimental results show that GYWI significantly outperforms mainstream LLMs in multiple metrics such as novelty, reliability, and relevance.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Generating Third-Person View from First-Person View in Driving
conference_papers.summary: This study aims to evaluate a driver's usual driving situation using driving footage, such as that from a dashcam. The dashcam provides a first-person image depicting the front view of the driver's seat. However, to evaluate your own driving, a thirdperson perspective taken from behind the vehicle can give you a more accurate picture of your car's movements. This requires the cooperation of the car driving behind, which is impossible with a car alone. To resolve this, pix2pix, a generative adversarial network (GAN) model, was used to generate third-person viewpoint images from first-person images captured using a dashcam. For the evaluation, we used third-person perspective images generated using the model and first-person and thirdperson perspective images created using a simulator. The experiments using footage captured in an actual dashcam was also conducted.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: From Ranking to Exact Prediction in Multi-Label Learning with Bipolar Networks
conference_papers.summary: Real-world images often contain multiple objects, and applications such as medical image tagging, autonomous driving, and scene understanding require accurate identification of the exact set of labels present. Such applications demand optimization for threshold-based metrics such as the F1-score. However, most existing multi-label learning (MLL) methods focus on optimizing ranking-based metrics such as mean Average Precision (mAP), often at the expense of exact label prediction quality. To address this gap, we investigate bipolar networks, an architecture that assigns labels by comparing parallel positive and negative outputs, thereby embedding the classification threshold directly into the model. We show that standard singleoutput losses, including Binary Cross-Entropy, Focal Loss, and Two-Way Loss, can be reformulated in bipolar form to operate on the bipolar margin. Experiments on benchmark datasets (VOC, COCO, NUS-WIDE, VISPR) demonstrate that bipolar networks achieve significant improvements in F1-score while maintaining competitive mAP, with additional results validating robustness to data imbalance on benchmark vector multi-label datasets.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Feedback-Driven AI Workload Emulation for Big Data Cloud Systems
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces a novel methodology for emulating complex computational workloads in Big Data Cloud environments. We present a framework for constructing synthetic AI-driven application models that accurately mirror the performance characteristics of real-world Big Data processes. A core element is the integrated feedback mechanism, allowing iterative refinement of these models to explore system behaviors, identify optimization opportunities, and validate resilience strategies. By enabling precise, controlled experimentation and a continuous feedback loop for system design, this approach significantly simplifies the development and testing of robust and efficient Big Data Cloud AI infrastructures.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Feasibility of Robotic-Assisted Echocardiography in Patients: Reducing Sonographer Strain without Compromising Image Quality
conference_papers.summary: Echocardiography remains a widely used imaging modality for the evaluation of cardiac structure and function. Despite its diagnostic value, conventional manual scanning techniques require sonographers to maintain repetitive postures and apply sustained pressure over extended periods, increasing the risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. In recent years, collaborative robots, or cobots, have emerged as a promising solution for applications requiring robots to operate safely alongside human operators. Modern cobot systems are often equipped with integrated force and torque sensors, enabling precise control of contact forces during patient scanning to ensure both safety and comfort. This study investigates the feasibility of a robotic-assisted echocardiography system in a clinical setting, focusing on its potential to reduce physical strain on sonographers while maintaining diagnostic image quality. A patient-based evaluation over 24 participants was conducted to assess system performance, force control accuracy, and image quality compared to conventional manual scanning. The findings aim to provide insights into the integration of robotic assistance in echocardiography workflows, with implications for improving operator ergonomics, patient safety, and imaging quality.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Eyes on Target: Gaze-Aware Object Detection in Egocentric Video
conference_papers.summary: Human gaze offers rich supervisory signals for understanding visual attention in complex visual environments. In this paper, we propose Eyes on Target, a novel depth-aware and gaze-guided object detection framework designed for egocentric videos. Our approach injects gaze-derived features into the attention mechanism of a Vision Transformer (ViT), effectively biasing spatial feature selection toward human-attended regions. Unlike traditional object detectors that treat all regions equally, our method emphasises viewer-prioritised areas to enhance object detection. We validate our method on an egocentric simulator dataset where human visual attention is critical for task assessment, illustrating its potential in evaluating human performance in simulation scenarios. We evaluate the effectiveness of our gazeintegrated model through extensive experiments and ablation studies, demonstrating consistent gains in detection accuracy over gaze-agnostic baselines on both the custom simulator dataset and public benchmarks, including Ego4D Ego-Motion and Ego-CHGaze datasets. To interpret model behaviour, we also introduce a gaze-aware attention head importance metric, revealing how gaze cues modulate transformer attention dynamics.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Exploring the Relationship between Automated Essay Scoring System Functionality, Student Innovativeness, Reflective Thinking, and Exploratory Usage: A PLS-SEM Approach
conference_papers.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has accessed in modern life through web search engines and mobile apps. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) is playing a significant role in educational field. The research studied relationship between system functionality of AES and students’ individual innovativeness of AES, as well as their reflective thinking, and how these variables impact students’ exploratory usage of AES. Partial Least Squares - Structural Equation Modeling (PLS - SEM) was used for data analysis. The valid data was gathered from 442 students. The findings indicate that system function of AES positively influences students’ individual innovativeness, reflective thinking, and exploratory usage; individual innovativeness positively affects reflective thinking. Moreover, students’ exploratory usage of AES positively influences students’ individual innovativeness and reflective thinking. These insights shed light on students’ attitude on technological tool and also offering aid in improving teaching.
institutions: Shandong Vocational College of Special Education

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Exploring the Influence of Multiscale Urban Road Network Centrality on Cycling Behavior: A Case Study of Shenzhen Longgang District
conference_papers.summary: Cycling is widely recognized as a low-carbon, equitable, and space-efficient mode of urban transport, contributing to traffic demand management and enhancing multimodal connectivity—especially for short trips and first-/last-kilometer access. However, there has been relatively little research on how urban roads affect cycling frequency, even though the roads themselves are closely related to such behavior. This study implements a multiscale street network analysis framework to characterize the spatial configuration of urban centrality in Longgang District, Shenzhen. Monthly trajectory data from shared bikes in Longgang, Shenzhen, are chosen for spatial distribution analysis. In this study, a multivariate regression model was constructed to examine the determinants of cycling frequency. The model incorporates cycling frequency as the dependent variable, while three key independent variables were considered: shared bicycle supply, road network centrality, and street environmental characteristics. This analytical framework enables a comprehensive assessment of the factors influencing cycling behavior in urban contexts. Several interesting observations are revealed. The centrality metrics of road networks at multiple spatial scales exhibit significant associations with cycling frequency, with varying degrees of influence. Combining the analysis results, optimization strategies for urban street cycling are proposed from three perspectives: matching supply and demand, constructing a cycling network, and optimizing the cycling environment to promote cycling trips.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Explainable AI for Predictive Maintenance in Manufacturing Process Using RTDB Sensor Data
conference_papers.summary: Predictive maintenance in continuous manufacturing processes is a critical challenge for smart factories. Papermaking, with its high energy demand and sensitivity to equipment failures, requires early and reliable anomaly detection methods. This paper presents a framework leveraging Real-Time Database (RTDB) sensor data from a papermaking process to predict binary alarm events before they occur. Using Random Forest models trained with lead-time shifted labels, we achieve reliable performance with an ROC AUC of 0.78 and an F1-score of 0.62 at a 5 -step horizon. Explainable AI techniques, including feature importance analysis and partial dependence plots, visualize the impact of key process variables such as steam pressure (PR001), basis weight (WT001), and moisture (MO001) on model predictions, providing interpretability for operators. We further propose a dynamic multi-level warning strategy based on optimal thresholds to provide actionable alerts. The proposed approach demonstrates both academic contributions to explainable predictive maintenance and industrial relevance for smart manufacturing in papermaking.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Enhanced Robotic Framework for Object Recognition, Grasping, and Drawer Operation
conference_papers.summary: Social Robotics is a fast emerging and favorite research area for many robotic researchers. If robots are living with us and helping us (particularly assisting our elderly, disabled or ill) in our daily activities then they must be equipped with human like identification and manipulations capabilities with greater safety and efficiency. For instance, identifying and grasping objects and putting objects in the drawers and cupboards etc. without collision and damaging objects or harming humans. For robots to autonomously manipulate objects in unstructured environments presents significant challenges due to variations in object shape, orientation, lighting conditions, and dynamic environmental interactions. This paper presents an intelligent robotic framework for autonomous object recognition, grasping, and drawer operation in unstructured environments. To address the challenges of precise manipulation, the system integrates a dual-model perception pipeline. YOLOv8 is employed for robust drawer handle detection, while YOLOv11, enhanced with oriented bounding box (OBB) prediction, is utilized for accurate detection and orientation estimation of objects. The framework executes a complete sequence of tasks: detecting the drawer state, opening it if closed, recognizing and grasping the target object, placing it inside, and finally closing the drawer. Experimental validation on a MyCobot robotic arm demonstrated a 100% detection accuracy, 90% grasping success, and 70% placement success, confirming the system's robustness in performing complex, multi-stage manipulation tasks.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Enhanced Redundant Measurement and Innovation-Based Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter for INS/GNSS Integrated Navigation
conference_papers.summary: Adaptive Kalman filters play a vital role in the inertial navigation system/global navigation satellite system (INS/GNSS) integrated navigation system. However, when the GNSS measurement accuracy degrades or the system model biases exist, the positioning performance deteriorates significantly. In this paper, an improved adaptive Kalman filter based on redundant measurements and innovation is developed to enhance filtering performance. The proposed algorithm first determines the probability distribution of measurement noise by kernel density estimation (KDE) and then adaptively selects the secondorder mutual difference (SOMD) or autoregressive correction algorithm for measurement noise covariance estimation. With an accurate estimate of the measurement noise covariance obtained, an innovation-based model-bias detector is introduced to adaptively adjust the state-error covariance. Finally, a real-world experiment is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Energy-Saving Control Method for Fully Electro-Hydraulic Positive Flow Excavators Based on Optimal Flow Distribution
conference_papers.summary: To enhance the operational efficiency of fully electronically controlled constant flow control excavator electrohydraulic systems, this study investigates dual-pump flow distribution strategies for energy conservation, targeting maximum pump efficiency. Firstly, a high-precision pump efficiency model for plunger pumps was developed using machine learning methods. Experimental validation demonstrated that the model's predicted efficiency values exhibited a relative error of merely 3.98% compared to experimental measurements, significantly outperforming the computational accuracy of traditional theoretical models. Subsequently, an optimisation function targeting minimal system input power was formulated based on this pump efficiency model. The influence of different flow distribution patterns on system input power under varying pressure, rotational speed, and flow conditions was analysed, yielding the most energy-efficient dual-pump flow distribution strategy for each operating scenario. Finally, following validation of the experimental simulation model's accuracy, dynamic response characteristics of the hydraulic system under different flow distribution schemes were simulated. The research findings indicate that: when the system's total flow demand does not exceed the maximum flow capacity of a single pump, independent oil supply from a single pump is the most energy-efficient approach; when the system's total flow demand exceeds the supply capacity of a single pump, equal flow distribution between both pumps is more energy-efficient; the flow distribution strategy has negligible impact on the system's response characteristics. Consequently, the proposed flow distribution strategy is applicable to the control systems of existing excavators.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Energy-Efficient Quadrotor Missions Using Sliding Mode Control
conference_papers.summary: This paper proposes a method for executing quadrotor missions with minimal energy consumption. While trajectory planning is a common strategy to improve the inherently low energy efficiency of quadrotors, most existing approaches rely on open-loop designs and overlook the impact of closed-loop tracking, making actual energy usage unknown. To address this, we present a two-fold solution: (i) a Least Energy Trajectory (LET) generation framework based on solving an Optimal Control Problem (OCP) that incorporates all practical quadrotor constraints to ensure flyable trajectories, and (ii) a Sliding Mode Control (SMC) architecture with bounded inputs to accurately track these trajectories. Simulation results show that the proposed SMC achieves highfidelity tracking of LETs, with energy consumption up to 19% above the theoretical minimum-substantially better than the PX4-autopilot-based PID controller, which can deviate by over 40%.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Enabling Contextual Awareness for Automated Systems through Machine Learning on Electromagnetic Emissions
conference_papers.summary: Effectively sensing device states from complex electromagnetic EM emissions often relies on computationally expensive black box models. This paper proposes a systematic framework that prioritizes efficiency and interpretability over algorithmic complexity. Instead of deploying complex algorithms, this work demonstrates that the most critical factor is optimal feature selection. The framework begins by extracting 30 candidate features from raw EM signals and then employs Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) to identify a minimal optimal subset. The analysis reveals that a compact set of just 10 features is sufficient for peak performance. When trained on this subset, a classical Support Vector Machine (SVM) delivers exceptional accuracy and robust generalizability across different devices. The results clearly show smart feature selection is more important than model complexity. This principle offers a blueprint for building lightweight, efficient, and interpretable monitoring systems for future AI and automation applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: EdgeFlame: A Physics-Inspired Framework for Zero-Shot Fire and Smoke Recognition
conference_papers.summary: Wildfires and smoke pose serious threats that demand rapid and reliable detection, especially on autonomous platforms operating under limited resources. We present EdgeFlame, a physics-inspired cross-modal learning framework for zero-shot fire and smoke classification on drones and IoT devices. It combines 3D CWT features with a Stationary Action Principle–guided architecture to link physical signal dynamics with lightweight AI inference. The model is highly efficient, requiring only 0.12 MB of parameters and achieving 3,281 frames per second with a latency of just 0.30 milliseconds. It outperforms conventional baselines such as CLIP, YOLOv12, and ResNet50 in both speed and efficiency. Tested on three diverse datasets—Kaggle Fire, YouTube wildfire videos, and the RGBIR FLAME2 drone dataset—EdgeFlame consistently achieves 94–98% accuracy across different environments. Designed for onboard edge deployment, it enables real-time wildfire perception on autonomous UAVs without relying on large-scale retraining, offering a practical and scalable solution for disaster response robotics.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Edge-Cloud Collaborative Fault Classification of Mechanical Equipment Using Lightweight Deep Learning Models
conference_papers.summary: In the context of the intelligent transformation of the equipment manufacturing industry, traditional mechanical equipment condition monitoring methods based on deep learning often rely on cloud or server-side deployment, which suffers from issues such as high data transmission latency, strong dependence on network bandwidth, and inability to meet the requirements of low-latency application scenarios. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes an edge-cloud collaborative fault classification method of mechanical equipment based on lightweight deep learning models. The model training and quantization are performed in the cloud using historical data, generating a lightweight model tailored for edge devices, which is then deployed for real-time edge inference and fault classification. At the edge, feature extraction and preprocessing based on the Hilbert transform are conducted prior to inference to enhance signal quality and reduce computational overhead. Using motor condition monitoring as an example, the results demonstrate that this method achieves an inference time of 0.846 seconds and a classification accuracy rate exceeding 97% in the edge computing environment, significantly reducing latency while maintaining high precision. Furthermore, under the proposed framework, various types of deep learning models demonstrate high classification accuracy and inference efficiency, further validating the method's versatility and engineering applicability.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: EEG-Based Multi-Level Stress Screening Using Machine Learning
conference_papers.summary: Stress is a common mental health condition affecting millions, often manifesting in both emotional and physical symptoms. Severe stress can further contribute to depression and, in extreme cases, may lead to sudden death. Accurate assessment of stress levels is crucial for enabling timely interventions and preventing serious outcomes. This study examines a machine learning-based approach for classifying multi-level stress among university students using EEG signals. Participants were initially assessed and categorized into different stress severity groups using the PSS-10 screening tool. EEG data were then recorded, filtered into several frequency bands, and segmented into non-overlapping intervals of 1,2,3,4, and 5 seconds to examine the effect of segment duration on classification performance. Feature extraction encompassed eight time and frequency domain features, and the Bagged Trees classifier was employed to classify stress levels. The results demonstrate the potential of EEG-based systems as non-invasive tools for stress monitoring, offering valuable support for mental health diagnosis.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Event-Based Model Predictive Control for Networked Systems with Hybrid Cyber Attacks
conference_papers.summary: This paper studies the dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM)-based model predictive control (MPC) problem for networked systems with false data injection (FDI) attacks and denial of service (DoS) attacks. A DETM is used to save network resources. To reflect the impact of both FDI and DoS attacks on networked systems, a new model describing hybrid cyber attacks is proposed based on indicator functions. A solvable auxiliary optimization problem is designed to get the control gain. The DETM-based MPC algorithm is presented and the recursive feasibility of this algorithm is ensured. The mean-square input-to-state stability of the closed-loop system is guaranteed. The validity of the developed DETM-based MPC algorithm is illustrated by a case study of a networked two-area smart grid.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Analysis and Control of a Segmented Mirror Telescope Prototype Model
conference_papers.summary: This paper reports the initial progress on the design of a segmented mirror telescope mechanism using the combination of the system kinematic model and actuator dynamic model to achieve desired focus angle. A feedback control system based on the PID design framework is particularly developed based on the dynamic model of the actuator that is represented as a mass spring damper system. The proposed approach initially formulates the focus angle of the telescope mechanism with respect to the desired point and the center of the mirror. To ensure that the mirror can achieve the desired angle, the PID controller is introduced into the actuator to minimize the error on the required actuator lengths to achieve the desired value. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving the desired focus angle.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Discrete Functional Geometry of ReLU Networks via ReLU Transition Graphs
conference_papers.summary: We extend the ReLU Transition Graph (RTG) framework into a comprehensive graph-theoretic model for understanding deep ReLU networks. In this model, each node represents a linear activation region, and edges connect regions that differ by a single ReLU activation flip, forming a discrete geometric structure over the network's functional behavior. We prove that RTGs at random initialization exhibit strong expansion, binomial degree distributions, and spectral properties that tightly govern generalization. These structural insights enable new bounds on capacity via region entropy and on generalization via spectral gap and edge-wise KL divergence. Empirically, we construct RTGs for small networks, measure their smoothness and connectivity properties, and validate theoretical predictions. Our results show that region entropy saturates under overparameterization, spectral gap correlates with generalization, and KL divergence across adjacent regions reflects functional smoothness. This work provides a unified framework for analyzing ReLU networks through the lens of discrete functional geometry, offering new tools to understand, diagnose, and improve generalization.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: DexMapGrasp: Dexterous Grasp Generation via Contact Map
conference_papers.summary: Dexterous grasping is becoming increasingly widespread in its applications. Existing methods for generating dexterous grasp poses often require a fixed robotic hand configuration, which significantly increases the training cost associated with using new robotic hands. To address this issue, we propose DexMapGrasp, a contact map based grasp pose generation method that is suitable for different robotic hands. Our method introduces a single-input, multi-output contact map prediction network architecture that can be trained on multiple different robotic hands simultaneously, accounting for both the differences and commonality among their respective contact maps. Furthermore, we propose a novel grasp pose optimization method based on the contact map that considers the influence of the normal vectors of both the robotic hand and the object, which enables the robotic hands to gradually approach the object in an appropriate position and orientation. The experiments conducted in Isaac Sim validated the grasp success rate of the poses generated by DexMapGrasp and its generalizability to different robotic hands.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Development of an Autonomous Posture Controlled Robot for Assisting Water-Skipping
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces a device designed to make the activity of stone skipping accessible to anyone, regardless of skill level. Unlike approaches that assist a user's throwing motion, this research focuses on developing a throwable object that autonomously controls its posture to maintain the optimal angle for effective skipping on water. We developed a prototype equipped with a rotation control mechanism and onboard sensors, and conducted experiments under various throwing conditions to evaluate flight stability and the number of successful skips. The results demonstrated that the posture-controlled device significantly improved both stability and skipping performance compared to uncontrolled objects. This indicates that autonomous posture control in thrown objects not only enhances the enjoyment and accessibility of stone skipping as a recreational activity, but also suggests broader applications for self-stabilizing flight technologies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Development of an Automatic Scraping Method Based on Disk Milling Cutter Technology
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents an automatic scraping method based on a disk milling cutter, aiming to replace the traditional manual scraping operation. The system utilizes a three-degree-offreedom CNC machine platform, combined with disc milling cutter processing technology. By adjusting the milling parameters, the milling cutter marks are used to simulate the cutter mark of manual scraping in different stages. The theoretical and simulation calculations of the cutting force generated during the machining process were carried out, which is consistent with the force required for manual scraping. The experimental results show that the number of high points (6,13, and 21 points/square inch, respectively) of this method in the rough scraping, fine scraping, and precision scraping phases meets the standard of manual scraping, and the processing efficiency is significantly improved. The study verifies the feasibility of scraping with disc milling cutters and provides an efficient solution for the automated scraping of guideways for machine tool.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Development and Application of a Graphical Automatic Programming System for Multi-Groove Shaft CNC Machining
conference_papers.summary: To solve the problems of low programming efficiency and cumbersome parameter verification caused by variable dimensions in the batch processing of multi-groove shafts, a graphical automatic programming system was built based on the Fanuc 31i CNC system and Fanuc Picture development environment, integrating macro program compilation and parametric interface technologies. By extracting variable parameters of multi-groove shafts to design the interface, associating controls with macro variables via read-write functions, compiling and integrating part family macro programs, and importing data files through parameter configuration, the system enables programming and processing of dedicated shaft part families by inputting parameters graphically on the CNC interface. Practical application shows it shortens setup and debugging time, improves efficiency and safety. This technical approach provides a feasible solution for the development of dedicated CNC programming functions and is suitable for batch processing of similar parts.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Designing a Scalable RPA-Based Methodology for Automating HR Operations in Manufacturing
conference_papers.summary: In the context of Industry 4.0, where digital transformation is restructuring industrial operations through technologies such as IoT, AI, and cyber-physical systems, the need to modernize and streamline administrative functions has become increasingly relevant. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) has emerged as a strategic tool for automating repetitive, rule-based, and structured tasks through software bots, without altering existing systems. In response to these evolving demands, this study proposes a scalable methodology for automating Human Resources (HR) administrative processes in manufacturing organizations through RPA. The objective is to enhance operational efficiency, minimize manual errors, and support the digital evolution of HR departments. The methodology is organized into five phases: Process Diagnosis and Prioritization, Process Modeling, Prototype Development and Implementation, Change Management, and Continuous Monitoring. To ensure scalability, it integrates standardized templates, reusable components, centralized orchestration infrastructure, and a feedback-driven improvement cycle based on performance metrics. This work presents a structured and practical methodology intended to guide future HR automation initiatives. The proposal is in its early implementation phase and will be validated through application in a real-world HR process at a manufacturing company in Mexico, establishing a foundation for future evaluation and refinement.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design of a Real-Time System for Detecting Tire Trajectory Elevation Based on LiDAR-IMU Fusion
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents a real-time system for detecting tire trajectory elevation information through tightly-coupled LiDAR-IMU fusion based on the FAST-LIO2 SLAM algorithm. The system integrates motion-adaptive filtering with the Patchwork ++ ground segmentation algorithm to extract road surface information, while constructing a Kd-Tree-based dynamic map management system that provides$O(\log n)$query complexity for efficient elevation retrieval. Vehicle trajectory prediction employs an Extended Kalman Filter combined with kinematic models, utilizing odometry outputs from FAST-LIO2, followed by Catmull-Rom spline interpolation to generate smooth tire trajectories. Elevation extraction uses tire trajectory points as query seeds, performing rapid Kd-Tree radius searches within the map to obtain elevation data along the driving path, with statistical filtering and weighted averaging applied to enhance measurement accuracy. Experimental validation demonstrates that at vehicle speeds below$20 \text{km} / \mathrm{h}$, the system achieves an elevation measurement accuracy of$\pm 2.6 \text{cm}$, with a mean processing latency of 6.5 ms and a maximum delay of less than 17 ms at a 10 Hz update rate, thereby meeting the real-time requirements for autonomous driving applications.
institutions: Hunan University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of a LiDAR 3D Mapping System Based on a Modular UAV
conference_papers.summary: With technology increasingly empowering modern industries, unmanned mapping is poised to become a primary form of environmental perception. Addressing the detection, perception, 3D mapping, and trajectory planning requirements for lightweight Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) platforms, this study proposes a modular UAV system. The system integrates a comprehensive hardware and software solution, with a particular emphasis on environmental perception and fiber optic communication technologies for complex environments. Experimental validation confirms the feasibility of the proposed design, highlighting its potential for broader application.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of Transformer Fault Diagnosis Model Based on Multimodal Sensor Fusion and Edge Computing
conference_papers.summary: Power transformers are critical assets in power grids; their unexpected failure can lead to substantial economic loss and power outages. Traditional single-sensor diagnostic approaches struggle with the complex, non-linear, and non-stationary nature of fault signatures. This paper proposes a comprehensive multimodal sensor-fusion fault-diagnosis model that combines vibration, acoustic emission, dissolved gas analysis (DGA), and partial-discharge (PD) measurements within a transformer-tailored Vision-Transformer (ViT) architecture and deploys the model on edge devices for real-time inference. The contributions are fourfold: (1) a unified preprocessing pipeline converting heterogeneous signals into a common time-frequency representation; (2) a modality-specific embedding scheme enabling early-stage fusion through a cross-modal attention mechanism; (3) an optimized lightweight ViT network with knowledge distillation for edge deployment; and (4) an extensive evaluation on a 3-year, 58-TB industry dataset showing a 97.6 % F1-score and 23.4 ms end-to-end inference latency at the substation edge. Comparative studies demonstrate a 12.3 % improvement over state-of-the-art CNN-based methods. These results suggest the feasibility of multimodal transformer models in practical, resource-constrained environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design of Gaze Evaluation System in Driving Using Eye Tracking and Object Detection
conference_papers.summary: This paper proposes a gaze evaluation and training system for beginner drivers, implemented using Unity and You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8x for real-time object detection. Objects that could not be recognized by YOLOv8x were annotated manually. The system automatically identifies regions to be observed as must-see areas and regions that should be avoided as must-not-see areas. The must-see areas are marked with green bounding boxes, whereas the must-not-see areas are marked with red bounding boxes. Two experiments were conducted to assess YOLO accuracy and score comparison (manual counting) respectively. The manual score comparison was then updated to automatic scoring system which helps to calculate the automatic score when the subject looks at the system under the surveillance of an eye tracking sensor. Experiments with beginner and experienced drivers revealed significant differences in gaze patterns, with experienced drivers exhibiting wider gaze movements. In contrast, beginner drivers normally focusing straight on the road, showing insufficient hazard checks while driving. Finally, comparative score evaluation with two different approaches were performed with beginner and experienced drivers. The findings of this paper support the development of training mechanisms to improve driving skill in beginners and to enhance safe driving.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Validation of an End-Effector for a Surgical Robot with an Automatic Multi-Tool Switching Function
conference_papers.summary: Surgical robots are crucial to modern precision surgery, yet the working efficiency of tool switching in existing end-effectors remains a major challenge. In a conventional robot-assisted surgery (RAS), manually replacing surgical tools may disrupt the surgical workflow, reducing both working smoothness and the level of automation. To address current limitations, this paper presents the design and implementation of a novel surgical end-effector with an automatic multi-tool switching function. The core mechanism employs a dual-motor architecture: a distal motor drives a six-station rotating turntable via a planetary gearbox for rapid tool selection, while a proximal motor converts rotational motion into linear propulsion using a trapezoidal lead screw. An incomplete rack and pinion mechanism automatically locks and rotates the selected tool to the optimal working angle during forward propulsion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed design achieves rapid, stable, and accurate automatic tool switching without human involvement. This end-effector shows promising potential for high-precision surgical scenarios, such as oral and maxillofacial surgery, offering a novel solution to enhance the accuracy and automate the workflow of surgical robots.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Validation of an Autonomous IoT Collar for Bovine Monitoring in the Bolivian Altiplano
conference_papers.summary: This work presents the design and validation of an autonomous IoT collar for livestock monitoring in the Bolivian Altiplano. The device integrates motion, temperature, and environmental sensors into a compact platform powered by a solar energy system. A low-power wireless link enables continuous data transmission to a local gateway for remote visualization. The mechanical enclosure was 3D-printed with a bio-inspired internal pattern that improves impact resistance and overall durability. Compression, vibration, and water-resistance tests confirmed the structural reliability of the collar, while field trials demonstrated stable operation under real conditions. The embedded motionanalysis algorithm achieved a mean absolute error of 1.5 steps$(\mathbf{1. 1 {\%}})$and a correlation of$r=0.969\left(R^{2}=0.939\right)$, effectively distinguishing locomotion from non-advance movements. These results confirm the system's robustness and accuracy, which provides a low-cost solution for continuous livestock monitoring in remote rural areas.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Motion Analysis of a Novel 12-DOF Bionic Lower Limb Exoskeleton
conference_papers.summary: Current lower-limb exoskeletons mainly focus on sagittal-plane gait training, which leads to incomplete jointfunction recovery and unnatural overall gait. To address this issue, this study designs a novel bionic lower-limb exoskeleton with 12 degrees of freedom. Through an innovative bionic joint structure, the rotation axis of each joint is aligned with that of the corresponding human joint. The leg actuators are mounted proximally, and Bowden-cable transmission is used to achieve low inertia and high torque. A modified Denavit-Hartenberg method was employed to establish the forward kinematic model and obtain the foot workspace, while numerical method was used to derive the inverse kinematics. A virtual prototype was constructed for dynamic simulation to evaluate its performance under different modes. Finally, a physical prototype was built to verify wearing comfort and movement feasibility. The results showed that the exoskeleton provided a wide three-dimensional workspace, colud replicate natural human gait, and offered excellent humanmachine compatibility and a comfortable user experience. The dynamic simulation results served as a basis for actuator selection. This study provides an innovative design approach for lower-limb exoskeletons and is expected to advance the development of bionic exoskeleton systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of a Stereo Perception and Intelligent Interpretation System for Orbiting Satellites
conference_papers.summary: With the advancement of modern aerospace technology, novel space situational awareness methods are emerging as key innovations for future space exploration. Addressing the urgent need for efficient detection of space targets by orbiting satellites, this paper designs an integrated system combining stereo vision with intelligent interpretation. By integrating a 100° wide-field stereo camera with the Nvidia Orin edge computing platform, the system achieves four core functions: target detection and tracking, stereo ranging, parameter measurement, and 360° panoramic image reconstruction. The YOLOv8 detection model was enhanced by integrating the C2f_Faster module and attention mechanisms, enabling effective detection and tracking of rotating targets. This resulted in a lightweight model with parameters reduced to 26MB (a 20% reduction from the original). Through stereo vision calibration and matching, the system was successfully demonstrated. Conversion based on aperture relationships yielded a ranging accuracy better than 1% within 5 meters and a target size measurement error of less than 3%. Further leveraging depth information and off-target correction, the system achieved gaze-stabilized imaging with uniform resolution across the entire orbital plane and three-dimensional target reconstruction. Simulation testing and experimental validation confirm the system's feasibility for high-precision perception and intelligent interpretation, enabling broader application prospects.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Development of a Human-Evaluation Platform for Large Language Model-Generated Datasets
conference_papers.summary: This study aims to design and develop a human evaluation platform for assessing educational question-answer (QA) datasets generated by closed-source large language models (LLMs). As the use of generative AI expands in educational settings, there is a growing need for structured review systems capable of verifying the reliability and curricular alignment of high-quality datasets. The proposed platform enables experts to evaluate QA datasets by uploading data, ranking multiple responses, and providing qualitative feedback. To support this process, a web-based system was implemented, incorporating features such as metadata management, expert account creation and assignment, and rank-based evaluation. By introducing a practical tool that supplements human involvement in dataset validation, this study lays the groundwork for the evaluation and refinement of educational language models.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Deepfake Video Detection Using Swin Transformer and LSTM: A Hybrid Approach for Facial Feature Analysis
conference_papers.summary: Deepfake technology raises major challenges in digital authenticity, privacy, and trust in society. Although detection techniques based on deep learning, like CNNs, are common, they tend to be less generalizable across datasets and are sometimes incapable of identifying temporal inconsistencies. This indicates the necessity for stronger and more flexible solutions. In return, this paper investigates a hybrid deepfake detection mechanism leveraging Swin Transformer for feature learning and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for classification. The hierarchical self-attention mechanism of the Swin Transformer well learns multi-scale spatial features, while LSTM can model temporal dependencies to identify inconsistencies in deepfake videos. By using the solution, i.e., Swin-LSTM, generalizability, detection accuracy, and robustness against sophisticated deepfake manipulation techniques are enhanced. Furthermore, the paper considers effective preprocessing methods, including face detection and video frame grabbing, to gain the best out of feature representation. Our experiments demonstrate that combining transformer-based feature extraction with sequential learning highly improves deepfake classification accuracy to$\mathbf{8 5. 7 1 \%}$in testing.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Deep Temporal Causal Discovery: A Framework for Uncovering Nonlinear and Time-Lagged Dynamics
conference_papers.summary: Understanding causal mechanisms underlying sealevel variability is essential for environmental forecasting and coastal resilience planning. Traditional statistical and machine learning approaches often capture associations but fail to model nonlinear, time-lagged dependencies or provide interpretability. This paper investigates the Temporal Causal Discovery Framework (TCDF), a deep learning-based method for uncovering nonlinear and lagged causal relationships in multivariate climate time series. The framework is enhanced with configurable hyperparameters, attention-based visualizations, and efficient caching mechanisms, all integrated within a modular, web-based causal discovery platform. Comparative experiments with baseline methods, such as Granger Causality, PCMCI, ICALiNGAM, and GES, demonstrate TCDF's unique capability to reveal hidden nonlinear dependencies and adaptive lag structures in real-world datasets. Results show that TCDF consistently identifies robust causal drivers of Sea Level Anomalies (SLA) and Water Level (WL), validated through noise, permutation, and placebo-based refutation tests. Overall, TCDF provides a practical, interpretable, and scalable framework for causal-aware environmental forecasting.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Data Driven Evasion Policy for Repeated Pursuit Evasion Problem with Unknown Imperfect Pursuer
conference_papers.summary: A novel repeated pursuit-evasion (PE) problem with unknown imperfect pursuer is proposed and addressed using model based reinforcement learning. Grounded in aerospace applications, the problem adopts a repeated game formulation, where the evader engages repeatedly with the pursuer with unknown imperfect policy for multiple rounds, and the objective for the evader is to optimize the evasion policy based on data of preceding rounds so that evasion is achieved with minimum number of rounds. Unlike previous works that rely on prior knowledge of the pursuer's policy, our approach focus on efficient data exploitation in each round. Specifically, we adopt the probabilistic inference for learning control (PILCO) method, where a Gaussian process is adopted to model the unknown imperfect pursuer. This allows for efficient data exploitation and transforms the problem into the deterministic pay-off optimization with analytical gradients, enabling successive policy optimization in each round. Numerical results on a typical aerospace application demonstrate that the proposed method achieves successful evasion in remarkably few rounds, with the optimized policy aligning closely with the analytical optimal solution assuming complete knowledge of the pursuer.
