conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Control-Oriented Modeling for Thermal Management of Fuel Cell Vehicles in High-Temperature Environments Based on Physics-Informed Neural Network
conference_papers.summary: To ensure the stable operation and passenger comfort of fuel cell vehicles, vehicle-level thermal management plays a vital role. Under high-temperature conditions, the control of air-conditioning compressor speed and chiller valve opening is particularly important, as these actuators directly affect both the cabin temperature for passenger comfort and the battery temperature for system safety and durability. Integrated thermal management systems can improve efficiency and thermal performance in such scenarios, yet the strong coupling among subsystems significantly increases the difficulty of accurate modeling and control design. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a control-oriented modeling framework based on a physics-informed neural network. First, conventional state-space models of the high-temperature thermal management system are obtained. Then, the Gated-Recurrent-Unit (GRU) based encoder-decoder neural network is trained in a physics-informed manner, allowing it to capture the underlying dynamics of the system. This hybrid approach improves modeling accuracy while preserving the interpretability. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed model achieves better input–output accuracy compared with both traditional neural networks and conventional state-space models. With a relatively small number of network parameters, the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of the step-by-step prediction for the cabin and the battery are only 0.030 K and 0.023 K respectively, and the maximum errors are 0.916 K and 0.629 K respectively. The developed model therefore establishes a solid foundation for advanced thermal management strategies, such as neural network-based model predictive control, in the future development of fuel cell vehicles.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predictive Modeling of Truck Cycle Time in Open-Pit Mining Operations
conference_papers.summary: Truck cycle time is a critical performance indicator in open-pit mining operations, directly impacting productivity, fleet management efficiency, and operational costs. Accurate real time prediction of truck cycle time allows for dynamic dispatching and scheduling optimization, which is essential for maximizing material handling throughput. This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of eight distinct machine learning algorithms for the predictive modelling of truck cycle time in a real-world open-pit mine environment. The investigation leverages a robust dataset of truck movement and operational parameters to train and validate the performance of the following models: Artificial Neural Network, Bayesian Network, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Logistic Regression,$k$-Nearest Neighbors$(k$-NN), Decision Tree, and Linear Regression. The models are rigorously assessed based on key performance metrics, including Root Mean Square Error, Mean Absolute Error, and$R^{2}$score, to determine their accuracy and reliability in estimating future truck cycle time. Results indicate significant variability in predictive power across the algorithms, highlighting the necessity of an informed model selection process for this specific industrial application. Specifically, the Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network models generally demonstrated superior predictive performance due to their capacity to capture complex, non-linear relationships within the haulage data. Conversely, simpler linear models exhibited lower accuracy. The main contribution of this research paper is the provision of a clear methodology and empirical evidence for selecting the most appropriate machine learning algorithm, offering a crucial contribution towards developing highly efficient, data-driven truck dispatching and management systems that enhance overall mine profitability

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Comparative Analysis of JPDA and GM-PHD Methods for Dense Group Target Tracking
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the result of simulation modeling of motion, detection and tracking of a group in the presence of measurement noise, a comparative analysis of two common methods of group target tracking: the Joint Probabilistic Data Association (JPDA) filter and the Gaussian Mixture Probability Hypothesis Density (GM-PHD) filter. The GOSPA metric and the average calculation time per scan are used to evaluate the quality of the modeling. The results demonstrate that while JPDA correctly estimates the number of trajectories, its computational load increases exponentially with the number of objects in the group. In contrast, GM-PHD exhibits a linear increase in computation with data volume but fails to provide a consistent estimate of the number of closely spaced objects. Based on these findings, the study proposes a hybrid approach, leveraging GM-PHD for initial group detection and position estimation in cluttered environments, and JPDA for subsequent precise tracking of individual trajectories.
institutions: Moscow Automobile and Road Construction State Technical University

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Gel and NiCu Textile Electrodes for Non-Invasive Fetal ECG Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Accurate monitoring of fetal heart activity is essential for early detection of congenital abnormalities and ensuring maternal-fetal well-being. While conventional noninvasive methods such as cardiotocography and Doppler ultrasound provide only indirect mechanical assessments, noninvasive fetal electrocardiography (NIFECG) offers a more direct, electrical measurement of fetal cardiac activity. However, its reliability depends strongly on electrode quality and skinelectrode contact. Standard$\mathbf{A g} / \mathbf{A g C l}$gel electrodes, though capable of capturing high-fidelity signals, are unsuitable for longterm or wearable monitoring due to skin irritation and gel drying. This study presents a comparative evaluation of traditional$\text{Ag} / \text{AgCl}$gel electrodes and nickel-copper (NiCu) textile electrodes for fetal ECG acquisition. Data were recorded from a pregnant and a non-pregnant subject using a uniform setup, and signals were processed through a standardized pipeline consisting of bandpass filtering, notch filtering, maternal ECG suppression, and fetal QRS detection combined with the multi stage false positive rejection stratergy. Performance was assessed using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), R-peak detection, heart rate estimation, and waveform correlation. The NiCu textile electrodes produced a comparable SNR to gel electrodes, indicating equivalent signal quality. However, textile electrodes yielded a higher number of detected QRS peaks, suggesting greater sensitivity but also a tendency toward over-detection. The correlation between the two electrode types was low, reflecting differences in material conductivity and signal morphology. Overall, NiCu textile electrodes demonstrated potential for comfortable, gel-free, and prolonged fetal monitoring, though further optimization of signal detection algorithms and electrode placement is needed to enhance accuracy. The findings contribute to ongoing efforts to develop reliable, wearable, and patientfriendly fetal monitoring systems suitable for clinical and home settings.
institutions: General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University
Indian Institute of Information Technology, Design and Manufacturing, Kancheepuram

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Comparative Analysis of 2D Deep Neural Network Architectures for Lung Nodule Detection
conference_papers.summary: Cancer remains a substantial global health burden and the leading cause of death worldwide. Early detection is critical to improving patient survival rates. Deep Learning (DL) has emerged as a transformative force in medical image analysis, particularly for tasks involving Computed Tomography (CT) scans, the optimal architectural choice for specific tasks remains a critical area of investigation. The best Deep Neural Network (DNN) architecture for real-world deployment in medical image processing is primarily determined by the trade-off between operational efficiency (inference speed) and detection accuracy. This research aims to analytical compare of four major 2D Deep Neural Network (DNN) object detection architectures, which are SSD-VGG16, EfficientDet, and YOLO, to provide empirically supported insights for model selection in high-stakes diagnostic tasks. The most impactful finding challenges standard evaluation protocols by analyzing model stability and learning dynamics. The training loss analysis demonstrates that mAP scores acquired at an arbitrary, fixed checkpoint are a poor reflection of an architecture's true potential. Such a framework is critical for assisting medical experts in accurately detecting and tracking nodule changes, resulting in better diagnosis and assessment of treatment response.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Collaborative Optimization of Speed Limits and Lighting in Urban Tunnels
conference_papers.summary: This paper focuses on the collaborative optimization of driving safety and energy efficiency in urban tunnels. By establishing a driver visual adaptation model, conducting driving simulation experiments, designing a multi-objective optimization algorithm, and performing dynamic simulation verification, a collaborative control strategy for dynamic matching of tunnel lighting and speed limits is proposed. By simulating tunnel scenarios, quantitatively analyze the impact of different lighting schemes and speed limit strategies on drivers' eye movement characteristics, physiological stress and operational behaviors, and achieve the construction and improvement of a multi-objective collaborative optimization model. With the goal of minimizing lighting energy consumption and accident risk index, a dynamic coupling solution for "brightness - speed - reaction time" has been achieved. The research results show that the collaborative solution has a lower rear-end collision rate during peak hours compared to the traditional solution, reduces lighting energy consumption, shortens the standard deviation of vehicle speed, and significantly enhances the safety and efficiency of tunnel operations.
institutions: Shandong University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Coherent Signal DOA Estimation for Coprime EMVS Array via TNN Minimization
conference_papers.summary: In this paper, we suggest a direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm for coherent sources with coprime electromagnetic vector sensor (EMVS) array. Firstly, the array interpolation is performed on the output of the coprime EMVS array, and a tensor nuclear norm (TNN) minimization problem is constructed to recover the corresponding third-order tensor. Based on the reconstructed tensor, the DOA estimates can be obtained by exploiting the MUISC searching. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method can offer enhanced DOA estimation accuracy. Experimental results validate the performance superiority of the proposed algorithm over the state-of-the-art methods.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Co-attention Autoencoder for Reinforcement Learning in High-Dimensional Environments
conference_papers.summary: We propose a framework, termed Co-attention Autoencoder for Reinforcement Learning (CARL), which exploits temporal dynamics among consecutive observations while mitigating information redundancy. As an unsupervised and model-agnostic module, CARL can be seamlessly integrated into existing RL algorithms, improving both training stability and performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CARL outperforms baselines in all environments, achieving an average improvement rate of 10.68%, which highlight its potential as a general framework in high-dimensional decision-making tasks.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Cloud-Based Smart Toilet System with an Integrated Soft Robotic Hand for Post-Defecation Anus Cleaning in Elderly Nursing Bed
conference_papers.summary: The growing global aging population has significantly increased the demand for intelligent healthcare solutions, particularly for elderly bedridden individuals in nursing beds who require assistance with personal hygiene. However, modern nursing bed toilets still lack automation and require caregiver assistance for cleaning the anus after defecation. Relying on others for such a personal task can leave elderly patients feeling vulnerable and stripped of their dignity, potentially leading to anxiety and depression. Researchers are now focused on developing solutions that are both cost-effective and efficient to tackle these challenges. Automatic toilets are a promising option, but most existing models remain inefficient. This paper proposes a novel cloud-based smart toilet system integrated with a soft robotic hand, specifically designed for post-defecation anus cleaning in nursing bed environments. The smart toilet system comprises a robotic arm with a soft robotic hand for cleaning, and an RGB-D camera connected to a cloud system for data collection. Additionally, cloud computing is integrated to handle data processing and storage. The processed data is then transmitted to the robot for the detection and localization of stool around the anus. In the experiment, the system's effectiveness was demonstrated using a plastic model simulating human buttocks. The results showed that the system successfully collected stool data and transmitted it to the cloud server. The data was then processed and stored in the cloud database, taking only 2.853 seconds. These results illustrate a promising direction for integrating robots in smart toilets with cloud technologies to improve hygiene and dignity in elderly care.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Cascade Disturbance Estimator for Disturbance Suppression in Spacecraft with Flywheels
conference_papers.summary: In the spacecraft with flywheels, there are multiplesource disturbances from flywheels, flexible appendages, and external space environment. Complex disturbances can degrade the attitude control performance of spacecraft and are usually suppressed by using disturbance estimation and feedforward compensation. However, flywheel rotor dynamic imbalance disturbance is difficult to suppress since it exhibits both time-varying frequency and amplitude characteristics. In this paper, a cascade disturbance estimator is proposed to estimate all disturbances. Firstly, a gradient estimator constructs novel basis functions to describe the flywheel rotor dynamic imbalance disturbance. Thus, it can accurately estimate this dynamic imbalance disturbance based on precise model information. Secondly, an extended disturbance observer is designed to further estimate residual disturbances with unknown model information to improve robustness. The proposed estimator can precisely estimate the total disturbances with a limited bandwidth. Afterwards, a composite controller based on the proposed estimator is designed to achieve high-performance spacecraft attitude control. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: CNN with Transfer Learning on RGB and Thermal Imaging for Epoxy Spill and Crack Detection in Glass Fiber Composites
conference_papers.summary: The disposal of composite materials, particularly glass fiber components, poses significant environmental and economic challenges, as many discarded parts still contain reusable epoxy. This study proposes a RGB thermal vision framework for detecting three key surface conditions in cured glass fiber composites: single epoxy dosage, double epoxy dosage, and cracks. Two lightweight CNN models (RGB and thermal) were trained independently using modality specific augmentation strategies to maximize robustness under varying visual conditions. The two models operate in parallel, and an alert is raised if either detects a potential defect, providing detection redundancy and reducing the risk of missed epoxy regions. The experimental results demonstrate that RGB and thermal modalities offer complementary strengths RGB excels in high contrast regions, while thermal imaging provides superior detection under low contrast or visually ambiguous conditions. Combined, the dual modality system enhances detection reliability and supports real-time application. This work contributes a practical and energy efficient vision solution that supports sustainable composite reuse within circular-economy manufacturing workflows, and it provides a foundation for future smart recycling and automated inspection systems in industrial environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Building Resilience to Out-of-Distribution Visual Data via Learned Input Preprocessing
conference_papers.summary: A major challenge in machine learning is resilience to out-of-distribution (OOD) data, that is data that exists outside of the distribution represented within a model's training data. Training is often performed using limited, carefully curated datasets leading to significant distribution shift during real-world deployment as edge cases and anomalies not included in the training data are encountered. This work seeks to address this through a learned input preprocessing pipeline whereby a dedicated preprocessing model learns to optimise input data for a specific target vision model. We investigate several out-ofdistribution scenarios in the context of semantic segmentation for autonomous vehicles, an application area where OOD scenarios pose a major challenge. We compare our learned preprocessing approach to a finetuned target model with augmented training data and demonstrate that our approach can enable performance comparable or better than that of such a finetuned model, and subsequently that a combined approach, whereby a preprocessing model is optimised to target a finetuned model, delivers superior performance to either method in isolation. Finally, we propose a joint optimisation approach, in which preprocessing and target models are trained simultaneously, which we demonstrate achieves significant further performance gains, particularly in challenging edge-case scenarios. We also demonstrate that our architecture can be reduced to a relatively compact size without a significant performance impact, potentially facilitating real time embedded applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Bipolar Joint Energy: Energy-Based Multi-Label OOD Detection with Bipolar Networks
conference_papers.summary: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is essential for deploying vision systems safely, since test-time inputs may not follow the training distribution. In real-world settings, inputs are inherently multi-labeled containing multiple correlated and overlapping concepts, which makes OOD detection particularly challenging across interdependent label spaces with single output layered networks. Despite its practical importance, OOD research has primarily addressed single labeled classification, only recently turning to multi-label settings by designing energy based OOD measures like Joint Energy (JE) for single output layered networks. On the other hand, bipolar networks have shown better multi-labeled classification performance over single output layered networks by encoding both positive and negative evidence for each label, yielding well-separated margins for in-distribution inputs. This raises the question - can bipolar networks improve multi-label OOD detection performance? This work addresses this research gap by proposing Bipolar Joint Energy (BJE), an energy-based scoring function that operates on bipolar margins for better OOD detection in multi-labeled settings. Experiments on PASCAL-VOC, MS-COCO, and NUS-WIDE show that BJE improves AUROC by up to 2.5 % and reduces FPR95 by up to 39 % compared to existing methods, demonstrating the advantage of bipolar architectures for multi-label OOD detection.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Benchmarking Offensive AI Agents Through the Autonomous Attack Chain
conference_papers.summary: This study presents the first empirical validation of the Autonomous Attack Chain (AAC), a cognitive-behavioural framework designed to model offensive operations of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents. Existing human-centric models, such as the Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK, and ATLAS, lack the granularity to capture machine-driven offensive autonomy. To address this gap, controlled experiments were conducted with two distinct AI agents: a stateless, single-tool agent (Agent Y) and a stateful, multi-tool agent with planning and memory (Agent X). Operating in a sandboxed environment, both agents' behaviours were systematically logged and evaluated against the AAC's five phases: Planning Initiation, Data/Tool Acquisition, Execution and Adaptation, Persistence/Propagation, and Impact Optimisation. Results confirm that the AAC successfully captured and differentiated the agents' behavioural lifecycles, revealing Agent Y's linear progression versus Agent X's multi-tool interactions and adaptive behaviours. The AAC, therefore, provides a foundation for understanding and profiling threats by AI agents, enabling the design of phase-aware defensive strategies that anticipate autonomous decision-making. All experimental artefacts are archived in a controlled repository at: https://github.com/malatm1/Autogen_Project_312/tree/main/results.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Bat-Grid SLAM: Bio-Inspired Active SLAM Approach Using Neural Grid Cells for Autonomous Navigation
conference_papers.summary: Active Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) systems face significant computational bottlenecks due to frontier-based exploration strategies requiring extensive environmental analysis for path planning. Drawing inspiration from the hexagonal firing patterns of grid cells in the mammalian entorhinal cortex, we present a bio-inspired active SLAM framework, Bat-Grid SLAM, that transforms spatial exploration into an efficient tessellated navigation problem. Our approach replaces computationally expensive frontier detection with a structured hexagonal grid representation that mimics the spatial encoding mechanisms observed in rodents. Grid cells and the Laplacian of Gaussian algorithm create an optimal scanning zone, with fewer exploration points, resulting in 16 percent faster mapping performance compared to conventional active SLAM techniques.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: BA Hand: A Novel Gripper Based on Object Adaptability and Plane Environment Adaptability
conference_papers.summary: Aiming at the problems of poor adaptability of traditional industrial grippers in unstructured scenarios, high cost of high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hands, and grasping limitations of traditional underactuated hands, this paper proposes the design of the “BA Hand” underactuated robotic hand. This design integrates the advantages of the Omega Hand and the KoreaTech-BLT Hand. It adopts the Co-terminal Dualshaft Link - Long Slot Structure to achieve plane environment adaptation and scooping function, and uses a belt to realize surface-contact adaptive grasping. The structure is simplified and can be 3D-printed to reduce costs. Through kinematic analysis, key parameters such as the tilt angle range of the hand are determined. Combined with force analysis, the boundary of state switching is quantified. Simulation verifies the rationality of the theory, and experiments demonstrate its multi-mode grasping ability, showing excellent grasping performance for objects of different shapes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Autonomous Cleaning of Solar Panels in Floating Photovoltaic Systems
conference_papers.summary: This research presents an autonomous robot for cleaning solar panels in floating photovoltaic systems. The robot uses a dual-track mechanism to maintain stability on flexible platforms, while two RPLiDAR S3 sensors generate point clouds for real-time edge detection. A segmentation algorithm extracts panel boundaries, and a feedback controller adjusts track speeds to maintain alignment with the detected edge. Cleaning is performed by a single cylindrical brush with height adjustment regulated by dual load cells to ensure consistent contact pressure. A water-spray system is also implemented to enhance debris removal. Laboratory experiments demonstrate reliable autonomous motion with 89.1 % tracking efficiency. The dust removal performance is within 1 % in the restoring condition, while the dirty panel performance is reduced by 5-9%. These results confirm the system's capability to provide stable navigation and high cleaning performance for floating photovoltaic installations.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Autonomous Astronomical Positioning Method of Lunar Satellite with Error Analysis Based on Moon Phase Characteristics
conference_papers.summary: This study focuses on moon phase characteristics observed by lunar satellite and proposes an autonomous astronomical positioning method with error analysis. Based on the orbital mechanics theory and astronomical almanac, the comprehensive orbit model of the Sun-Earth-Moon system together with lunar satellite is established. Through moon phase analysis, the limb feature point and terminator feature point on the imaging array of lunar sensor can be identified and extracted, thus obtaining lunar centroid by existing image processing algorithms. With precise attitude reference provided by star sensor, the positioning method by 2 cases corresponding to double feature types is presented accompanied by error derivation. The simulation compares the 2 cases through a 12-hour circumlunar satellite orbit with performance assessment based on reference centroiding precision, and verifies their applicabilities in positioning during moon phase variation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Autonomous Agent (AutoAgent) for Self Driving through Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: Recent advances in maneuver planning for autonomous vehicles leverage expert driving behavior but struggle to balance safety and comfort. We introduce AutoAgent, a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based framework that aligns with human driving behavior while optimizing for safety and comfort. AutoAgent combines a predictive model and RL: the predictive model, trained on historical data, forecasts surrounding vehicles' positions and embeds them in context-aware grid maps for the RL agent. Evaluations on simulated RL environments derived from real-world datasets show that AutoAgent consistently improves driving experience, achieving safe, comfortable, and humanaligned maneuvers. Compared to a state-of-the-art imitation learning model in unseen scenarios, AutoAgent demonstrates superior performance in handling complex situations. An ablation study highlights the predictive model's critical role.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Automatic Debugging and Testing Strategy for Power Equipment PCB Based on Multi-modal UAV Inspection Data
conference_papers.summary: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are critical to power equipment, as faults like overheating, broken traces, or loose components can disrupt the entire power system. Traditional manual debugging and testing are inefficient, high-risk in harsh environments, and inaccurate in fault localization. To address these issues, this paper proposes an automatic debugging method for power equipment PCBs using multi-modal Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) inspection data. A UAV system with multiple sensors collects visible light, thermal imaging, and vibration data, which is processed via a fusion model integrating deep learning and classic computer vision. An automated workflow for fault detection, localization, and debugging is developed, verified through laboratory and on-site tests. This strategy enhances automation and fault detection accuracy, filling the gap of integrating UAV remote sensing, multi-modal data processing, and PCB-specific debugging.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Automated Capsicum Grading Using Color-Edge Analysis and Machine Learning
conference_papers.summary: The object detection and classification of images has improved tremendously within critical areas of compute vision ranging from autonomous driving to agricultural monitoring. This study will focus on the YOLOv5 model for detection and classification of capsicum (bell pepper) in images taken from the Bachata variety grown in Karnataka, India. YOLOv5, which is highly accurate and real-time detector, was trained to detect capsicum and Image processing techniques were then employed to assess quality; edge detection, color analysis, and segmentation and classify into health (healthy and spoil), ripeness (ripe/unripe/unknown), and quality grade (A/B/C). The model produced the following results precision: 0.887, recall: 0.891, mAP@50: 0.929. The proposed system was designed as an easy to use android application so that farmers could utilize the app to assess quality in just few taps. Improving agricultural productivity through automation of quality assessment adds to the decision-making process of capsicum farming.
