conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Art2Music: Generating Music for Art Images with Multi-Modal Feeling Alignment
conference_papers.summary: With the rise of AI-generated content (AIGC), generating perceptually natural and feeling-aligned music from multimodal inputs remains challenging. However, existing approaches often depend on explicit emotion labels, which require costly manual annotation, highlighting the need for more flexible, feeling-aligned methods. In this paper, we propose Art2Music, a lightweight, feeling-aligned cross-modal music framework that synthesizes expressive music from artistic images and viewer comments or descriptions. The framework has two stages: (1) visual and textual cues are encoded into Mel-spectrograms using OpenCLIP, gated residual fusion, and a bidirectional LSTM optimized with a frequency-weighted L1 loss to enhance high-frequency fidelity, and (2) a fine-tuned HiFi-GAN vocoder reconstructs the spectrograms into high-quality audio waveforms. We conducted experiments on ArtiCaps, a pseudo feeling-aligned multi-modal (i.e., image, music, text) artwork dataset proposed in this work. Experiments demonstrate that Art2Music can improves the quality of generated music from the aspects of Mel-Cepstral Distortion, Fréchet Audio Distance, Log-Spectral Distance and cosine similarity. Also, A small-scale LLM-based case study for feeling alignment furtherqualitatively verified that Art2Music achieves consistent cross-modal feeling alignment and interpretability of matches and mismatches across modalities.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Analysis of Emotional Evolution for Public Opinion in Sudden Events Based on Big Data
conference_papers.summary: In the context of emergencies, accurately and reasonably analyzing netizens' attention and emotional attitudes in the emergency management of online public opinion is one of the important reference means to control the development of public opinion, guide the development of public opinion, and ensure social stability. Taking the "Typhoon Capricorn" emergency as an example, Python is first used for data collection; secondly, TF-IDF (term frequency–inverse document frequency) is used to eliminate duplicate data of public opinion texts and extract key data; then the sentiment analysis module of the third-party Python library (i.e. SnowNLP) is used to perform sentiment analysis of online comments. By analyzing the public opinion hotspots, public opinion stages, and public opinion emotions of netizens' comments, suggestions for responding to online public opinion are explored from the aspects of public opinion monitoring, precise response to public opinion, netizens' emotional tendencies, public emotional guidance, and media influence, in order to provide the government with a more accurate, detailed, and humanized situation analysis reference in the handling of public opinion emotions in emergencies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: An Underactuated Dual-Slide Adaptive Robotic Hand with Strong Environmental Adaptability*
conference_papers.summary: This paper proposes a grasping system based on a linear slide rail mechanism, characterized by strong environmental interaction and high adaptability. Its core concept involves coupling the linear slide rail with the finger plate of the robotic hand through a slot mechanism to achieve robust environmental adaptability and stable gripping during the grasping process. Through unique innovation, we have designed the DS Hand as its concrete implementation. Compared to other robotic hands with different complex mechanisms, this robotic hand features a simpler structure while possessing exceptional capabilities in passive adaptation, multi-mode grasping, and clamping. Theoretical analysis verifies its strong self-adaptability and experimental results demonstrate that the system can achieve stable grasping and holding of objects with various shapes and surface roughness. The proposed linear mechanism offers significant industrial applicability and low manufacturing cost. It does not rely on complex linkage-based linearization mechanisms and enables large-scale adaptive grasping. This work provides a low-cost and efficient solution for robotic grasping and clamping systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: An LLM-Enabled Interactive Knowledge Check System for Personalised E-Learning
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the design and implementation of an interactive knowledge check system powered by large language models (LLMs), aimed at enhancing digital education through personalized assessments and explainable feedback. The system retrieves questions from a structured question bank and employs Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide context-aware, tailored explanations to learners. Built as a secure full-stack web application integrated with AWS Bedrock, the platform supports role-based access control, learner performance dashboards, and structured learning progression. By addressing limitations in conventional e-learning platforms-such as the absence of intelligent feedback and adaptive content delivery, this work delivers an AI-driven solution emphasizing structured progression, responsible AI design, and meaningful analytics. Key technical innovations include an intelligent off-topic detection engine with high classification accuracy and an optimized LLM prompt structure that reduced average response latency by 45%, a caching mechanism that significantly lowered inference costs by minimizing repeated API calls. This suggests a potential approach for enabling more interpretable and adaptive AI-assisted assessments in digital learning environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: An Introduction to Reinforcement Learning Methods for Strategic Decisions in Competitive and Cooperative Multi-Agent Games
conference_papers.summary: This study introduces reinforcement learning methods to multiple agents with uncertain actions to be taken. The system describes interactions between agents (or groups of them) and their shared environment. Some parameter estimates need the use of reinforcement learning techniques. Each agent, or a network of which he could take part, acts on the environment of which it changes the previous state. This new observation is notified to the agent or networked agents. Their received reward relates to the quality or performance of their action. It can be shown that the repeated interactions through time always converge towards an optimal solution of discounted cumulated revise returns obtained by experiences alone without any model. This study aims to develop a comprehensive modeling chain comprising the theoretical foundations, developments and implementation. However, it is not approaching the most recent successful deep learning using an artificial neural network. Modeling applied to a single agent may be enough to explain and study basic concepts and techniques, as in this study. However multiple agent system allows to approach the organization of agents and the nature of their individual or collective behaviors. Thus, a controller can intervene to collect information and initiate joint actions. Agent behavior can be either cooperative, competitive, or mixed strategies. We then prove the interest of using the game-theoretic concepts to avoid non-stationary environment and partially observability issues from the action of multiple agents in MARL system. The implementation of the algorithms operates around the Bellman equation. A description compares the Q-learning and RL-learning approaches. The complete implementation of Q-learning is shown by using the known example of the shortest route between two points of a frozen lake broken by water holes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: An Improved Machine Learning Framework for Heart Disease Risk Prediction with Personalized Health Recommendations
conference_papers.summary: This study proposes an interpretable machine learning framework for heart disease risk prediction, integrating elastic-net logistic regression with interaction-only polynomial features and SMOTE-based class rebalancing. The model was developed on a stratified clinical dataset$(n=1,025)$using an$80: 20$split, with hyperparameters optimized through$\mathbf{1 0}$-fold crossvalidation. On the held-out cohort$(n=205)$, the framework achieved robust performance with 96% accuracy, a macro-F1 of 0.96, and balanced precision-recall metrics. Beyond predictive accuracy, the approach emphasizes probability calibration, interpretability, and methodological transparency, ensuring that calibrated risk estimates can inform physician assessment and guide personalized lifestyle recommendations. This calibrationaware, sparsity-promoting design demonstrates practical potential for transparent cardiovascular risk stratification and decision support in resource-constrained healthcare environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: An Idle-Stroke Underactuated Gripper with Independent Double-Parallelogram Linkages for Pinching and Adaptive Grasping*
conference_papers.summary: Traditional parallel grippers often require repeated pose adjustments of the robot arm when grasping objects lying on a table, which complicates reliable handling of planar objects with varying sizes. This difficulty mainly arises from the circular fingertip trajectories generated during conventional parallel motion. To overcome this limitation, this paper presents an underactuated idle-stroke gripper that integrates linear parallel and adaptive grasping modes in a single design, called the GPL hand (Grasshopper Link Gripper). A grasshopper-inspired linkage is employed to linearize the fingertip motion, while an independent two-stage parallel four-bar double-parallelogram linkage mechanism constrains the terminal finger segments to maintain a constant orientation during pinching. Furthermore, an idle-stroke transmission with delayed engagement enables a smooth transition from precision pinching to self-adaptive enveloping grasp once contact is established. Both theoretical analysis and experimental validation demonstrate that the proposed gripper achieves robust planar object grasping, wide size adaptability, and reliable performance, making it suitable for industrial grasping applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: An Edge-Cloud Collaborative Anomaly Detection Method for Rotating Machinery Based on Perceptual Vibration Hashing and Autoencoder
conference_papers.summary: Condition monitoring of machinery health is essential for ensuring operational safety and maintaining production efficiency. To address the challenge of delayed anomaly detection caused by high data throughput during realtime, high-frequency vibration monitoring, this paper proposes an edge-cloud collaborative anomaly detection method based on perceptual vibration hashing and autoencoder. On the edge side, a perceptual vibration hashing algorithm is employed to compress raw vibration signals into fixed-length machine condition hashes, thereby enabling compact feature representation. On the cloud side, an autoencoder is utilized to compute the reconstruction error of the machine condition hashes, which is then processed using a Kalman filter to construct a health indicator for degradation assessment. Furthermore, a residual contribution analysis is introduced to identify the parameters responsible for detected anomalies. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments on a benchmark bearing dataset, demonstrating its capability for timely and accurate anomaly detection in high-throughput monitoring scenarios.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: An EEG Controlled Artificial Hand Based on α Wave
conference_papers.summary: Artificial hands controlled by electroencephalograph (EEG) can bring a lot of help to the disabled. However, most of the EEG sampling equipments are expensive and the system design is always very complicated. All these bring limitations in the application of EEG controlled equipment in practice. This work has designed a low cost EEG controlled artificial hand that the control commands were generated by an α based brain-computer interface (BCI). The BCI designed in this work sampled EEG through an inexpensive wireless EEG device EMOTIV EPOC+. The system can output control commands to grasp and release objects by detecting α wave generated by users. The local controller can not only receive the control commands from BCI but also can control the detail movements of artificial hand based on current feedback, which makes the artificial hand can grasp objects of any shapes. By combining these two parts, the artificial hand can control and grasp things well according to the user's will by EEG. The experiment results show that the success rate of each subject finishing the experiments reached greater than or equal to 90%. This verifies that the artificial hand can be controlled well by the system designed in this work.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Advanced Robotic Object Slip Detection for Neuromorphic GelSight Tactile Sensor
conference_papers.summary: Robotic manipulators' gripping actions still pose challenges to researchers and hinder the emulation of human hand dexterity and gripping capabilities. In particular, the challenge is in detecting and controlling the slippage of a gripped object. A plethora of vision-based tactile sensors are reported in the literature, with varying levels of effectiveness and accuracy. Among the popular, cost-effective, commercially available tactile sensors are GelSight sensors, which are used to complement many gripper designs across diverse applications. Unfortunately, in many of these designs, object slip detection and control are often demonstrated by reducing the gripping force, which is an unrealistic emulation of the human hand. This work introduces a novel object slip-based experiment using the GelSight neuromorphic tactile sensor and a custom-made pneumatic gripper that naturally emulates robotic object slip. Furthermore, the object slip robotic experiment results are verified and validated using a standard Convolutional Neural Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-GRU) architecture. The GelSight tactile sensor, in combination with its event camera, produces data that is inherently spatial, temporal, and sequential, making it wellsuited for deep learning models that can jointly capture spatial structures and temporal dependencies, such as the CNN-GRU network. The proposed architecture successfully enabled object slip detection by extracting full spatial features with the CNN, while the GRU unit efficiently modeled temporal dependencies with high accuracy, more than 98%.
institutions: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Adaptive Underactuated Robotic Gripper with Gear-Multi-Link Mechanism for Composite Grasping*
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces an adaptive finger mechanism suitable for environmental constraints, named the GML Gripper (Gear-Multi-Link Gripper). This mechanism is based on the coupling of a symmetric five-linkage mechanism and a two-stage parallelogram system and is actuated by a single actuator to achieve multiple composite grasping functions. Specifically, the GML Gripper utilizes the linear motion characteristics of the symmetric five-linkage to achieve compliance in the vertical direction and employs the two-stage parallelogram linkage system to ensure line contact at the fingertip. Parallel grasping achieves a firm hold on conventional objects through stable line contact, asymmetrical scooping can effectively grasp thin objects, and symmetrical scooping allows for the grasping of irregular or large-volume objects. After analyzing the working principle of the mechanism through kinematics and statics, a 3D-printed prototype was used for experimental validation of the gripper's grasping performance under environmental constraints. This research provides a new approach to the design of adaptive grippers and expands the potential applications of underactuated robotic grippers in complex environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Adaptive Rule Based Energy Management System (EMS) for Battery-Supercapacitor Electric Vehicles Minimizing Battery Stress
conference_papers.summary: In this work, an adaptive rule based Energy Management System (EMS) is proposed for Electric Vehicles (EVs) using Battery/Supercapacitor (SC) based Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS). Rules for the EMS are designed considering SC State Of Charge (SOC), vehicle acceleration and battery threshold power. A continuous power distribution factor which depends upon battery SOC is added to improve the performance of the rule based framework. The impact of practical uncertainties such as vehicle mass variation, road slope variation and variation in both mass and slope are also analysed to test the efficiency and practicality of the proposed controller. A battery State Of Health$(\text{SOH})$model is applied to test the ageing stress over battery under different uncertain conditions. A real time simulator OPAL-RT is used to implement the proposed EMS. Simulation results show reduction of battery current by the proposed EMS as compared to Filter based strategy and Battery only EV undergoing conditions of varying vehicle mass, varying road slope, varying vehicle mass and road slope both for US06 and SC03 drive cycle. Hence robustness of the proposed rule based EMS is established ensuring enhanced participation of the SC in HESS leading to improvement in battery life and vehicle performance.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: ARTEMIS2 & ARTEMIS2-Mini: From Full-Scale to Distilled Real-Time Animal Behavior Recognition in a Robotic Dog
conference_papers.summary: Recent progress in pre-trained vision-language models has greatly advanced multimodal learning by enabling robust and generalizable feature extraction. However, animal action recognition remains a challenging task due to high intraspecies variability, subtle motion cues, and the need for fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning. In this work, we present ARTEMIS2, an improved version of the ARTEMIS framework, featuring enhanced frame selection, more powerful visual and textual encoders, and a refined spatio-temporal captioning module for stronger alignment between visual content and textual descriptions. Evaluated on the Animal Kingdom benchmark, ARTEMIS2 achieves 82.4 mAP, setting a new state-of-the-art. To support real-time deployment on robotic platforms, we propose ARTEMIS2-Mini, a distilled unimodal variant based on the TimeSformer architecture. Despite relying solely on video input, it achieves 77.91 mAP and enables real-time inference onboard a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot. Field experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in recognizing feline behaviors across indoor and outdoor environments, showcasing its potential for embodied AI in animal monitoring and interaction tasks. The code of ARTEMIS2 is available at https://github.com/edofazza/artemis2.
institutions: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
Istituto di Scienza e Tecnologie dell'Informazione "Alessandro Faedo"

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: AI-Driven Real-Time Workplace Safety Monitoring System for Industrial Environments
conference_papers.summary: Pakistan's industrial sector, employing millions in manufacturing and construction, faces significant workplace safety challenges, with$\mathbf{1. 9}$million reported injuries in 2020-2021 alone. Inadequate labor regulations and limited safety oversight further exacerbate the risks, especially for low-wage workers. This project proposes an AI-driven real-time monitoring system utilizing computer vision and deep learning to enhance workplace safety at Dawlence's sheet metal plant in Karachi. The system will analyze live video footage from factory CCTV cameras to detect unsafe behaviors, such as the absence of protective gear and hazardous machinery operation. By issuing real-time alerts, it will help prevent accidents, ensuring both employee safety and regulatory compliance. Additionally, the system will generate insightful safety reports, aiding in refining Dawlence's safety protocols. Designed for scalability, this solution can be adapted to various industrial settings, contributing to a safer and more compliant work environment.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: AI-Driven Peripheral Neural Interfaces for Decoding Movement Intent from EMG Signals
conference_papers.summary: Non-invasive decoding of human motor intention remains a central challenge for neural interfacing and hu-man-robot integration. This paper presents an artificial intelligence framework for interpreting latent motor states from high-density surface electromyography (sEMG) recorded during a Go/No-Go paradigm, with emphasis placed on No-Go trials, in which movement is prepared but voluntarily cancelled. By analysing tibialis anterior muscle activity, we demonstrate that peripheral signals can reveal cortical processes beyond overt force generation, demonstrating the potential feasibility of wearable thought-controlled interfaces. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on preprocessed beta-band (13 – 30 Hz) EMG data achieved a mean accuracy of 76.8% across three states-Baseline, Preparation, and Cancellation-significantly exceeding Support Vector Machine, Recurrent Neural Network, and Long Short-Term Memory baselines. The analysis of class-activation mappings and temporal prediction windows indicated that motor intent could be inferred up to 300 ms before explicit movement onset. These findings extend peripheral brain-interfacing concepts and open routes toward real-time, muscle-driven control of robotic and prosthetic systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: AI-Driven Forecasting of Tourist Arrivals in Metro Manila: Limits of Aviation Operations and Seasonality
conference_papers.summary: This study examined the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in forecasting tourist arrivals in Metro Manila by incorporating airline and airport operational data with seasonality as a moderating factor. Quantitative design was employed with survey responses from 320 aviation and tourism stakeholders. Traditional regression models revealed weak and non-significant relationships, showing that operational and seasonal variables alone could not explain fluctuations in arrivals. These results highlight the limitations of conventional forecasting approaches in capturing the complexity of tourism demand. The study therefore emphasizes the value of AI -driven models, such as machine learning and neural networks, which offer greater capacity to detect nonlinear patterns and multifactorial influences. By reframing forecasting through AI applications, the research contributes to advancing smart tourism strategies and demonstrates the relevance of AI beyond traditional aviation operations.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: AFC Rule Check Framework for Construction Integrity of Semiconductor FAB MEP: Case Study
conference_papers.summary: This research addresses design-construction discrepancies in the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems of semiconductor fabrication facilities (FABs). Given that even minor inconsistencies during the design phase can precipitate substantial rework expenditures during construction, enhancing design-construction integrity prior to procurement and field execution is paramount. The proposed Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based Approval for Construction (AFC) rule framework represents a technological advancement toward data-driven, automated validation of construction integrity. This framework is specifically designed to address the inherent complexity and stringent quality requirements characteristic of semiconductor FAB MEP projects, thereby supporting the achievement of quality, cost, and schedule objectives.
institutions: Seoul National University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Wind Power Forecasting Paradigm Incorporating the Temporal-Frequency-Enhanced Training Strategy
conference_papers.summary: Multi-step wind power forecasting serves as a vital technique for maintaining a smart grid where wind energy is embedded. However, traditional direct forecasting paradigm suffers from a fundamental contradiction between label independence assumption and label autocorrelation in wind power. Therefore, this study proposes a novel wind power forecasting paradigm incorporating a Temporal-Frequency-enhanced training strategy. Specifically, a dual-component loss function incorporating temporal-domain accuracy and frequency-domain consistency is proposed for mitigating label autocorrelations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed forecasting paradigm significantly outperforms benchmark models in terms of forecasting accuracy. Furthermore, compared with traditional direct forecasting paradigm, the Temporal-Frequency-enhanced training strategy yields accuracy improvements of up to 7.73% and 6.06% in deep learning framework and transfer learning framework, respectively. The study provides a simple yet effective insight into improving multi-step wind power forecasting performance.
institutions: Anhui University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Variational Bayesian-Based Augmented State Joint Estimation Method for Heavy-Tailed Colored Noise
conference_papers.summary: The measurement of dynamic system is corrupted by colored noise and involved heavy-tailed characteristics simultaneously for target tracking in practice. Mostly existing work employs the the first-order measurement difference method to resolve the colored noise. In this paper, we augment the colored measurement noise onto the system state vector to whiten the colored noise. To handle the heavy-tailed noise in state model, we model it as the Student’s t distribution, and it is decomposed into a hierarchical Gaussian structure of Gaussian distribution and Gamma distribution. Subsequently, the variational Bayesian method combined with the inverse Wishart prior describing the uncertainty of the scale matrix, is used to achieve the joint posterior estimate of the system state. Then a variational Bayesian and augmented state (VB-AS) joint estimation algorithm is proposed for the state estimate of dynamic system with colored heavy-tailed noise. Illustrative examples verify the validness of the proposed algorithm.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A User Aware Indian Music Recommendation System
conference_papers.summary: The Hindustani music repertoire of the Indian subcontinent is a rich cultural legacy, renowned for its therapeutic properties and emotional depth. This work introduces an intelligent User-Aware Music Recommendation System that leverages the emotional and therapeutic richness of Hindustani classical music. In Hindustani music, a raga is a melodic framework of specific notes and rules for their arrangement, designed to evoke a particular mood or emotion, and is associated with therapeutic benefits. Building on this principle, the system is designed in three stages to provide culturally grounded, personalized recommendations. First, a specialized dataset is curated, combining attributes such as therapeutic benefits, emotional effects, and metadata derived from extensive studies on Hindustani ragas. Second, a Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) model, based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks trained on the RAVDESS dataset, is employed to identify user emotions, which are mapped to the emotional essence of ragas through a mood mapper. Finally, a content-based filtering algorithm integrates mood mappings and health conditions to recommend music that aligns with the user's current state. The SER model achieves high accuracy (up to 93.6%) across multiple emotion categories. By providing different combination of user queries, recommendations are evaluated using cosine similarity, a customized Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) algorithm, Precision@K, and Diversity metrics. Results demonstrate that the system effectively suggests ragas aligned with health conditions such as stress, insomnia, and headache, outperforming baseline Spotify recommendations in precision and complementing them in diversity. By blending cultural heritage with computational intelligence, this work highlights the potential of AI driven Hindustani music recommendation as an example of AI for Social Good.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Telemanipulation System with Constraint-Aware Shared-Control for Contact-Rich Robot Tasks
conference_papers.summary: This work introduces a robot telemanipulation with constraint-satisfying shared-control for robot tasks with both precision and contact force requirements. To enable a human operator to intuitively teleoperate a manipulator to perform contact-rich tasks, we introduce two novel features, namely i) a pose registration method to determine the object grasp pose with respect to the target environment, and ii) motion mapping to re-target input device motion to robot motion that satisfies geometric task constraints. Additionally, force-feedback compensation relative to the constraint geometries is employed to ease contact-rich teleoperation for the human. Experiments of human-robot co-assembly of IKEA furniture and Lego bricks have been conducted, and the results show that the system can quickly register the poses and allow the human operator to work with the robot to perform the assembly tasks with greater speed and success rate, and with reduced contact forces. Our approach provides means to telemanipulate the robot over different motion ranges, register key poses, and intuitively share the control of the task motion with the robot, which can be useful for many human-centered robotic applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Systolic Architecture for Deep Learning-Based Fall Detection
conference_papers.summary: One of the active research problems in intelligent healthcare monitoring systems is fall detection. As the elderly population is increasing day by day across the globe and there is an increase in assisted living environments, fall detection and timely medical intervention are crucial, which can reduce the severity of injuries and sometimes can even save their lives. A deep learning based model is proposed for fall detection, which is implemented on an FPGA. Initially, with the help of the background subtraction technique, a human silhouette is obtained. An optimised VLSI architecture, which is based on a systolic array, is designed so that the computations are done in parallel and the detection time is reduced. The designed architecture is tested with fall and non-fall videos, and simulation results show successful fall event detection.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A System for UAV Obstacle Avoidance Control via Haptic Interface and Optical Tracking
conference_papers.summary: This paper outlines the design and implementation of a full haptic feedback system developed to accomplish real-time teleoperation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The system allows the teleoperation of a drone within indoor environments rich with obstacles by using only haptic feedback and without visual feedback. Our system efficiently encompasses using Unity as the processing and visualization center, ROS2 as the communication and robot control system, Geomagic Touch as the haptic device and controller, and OptiTrack to provide real-time position tracking of both the UAV and surrounding obstacles. The force feedback is dynamically calculated within Unity based on the distance to obstacles and is transmitted to the Geomagic device to provide better intuitive spatial perception. Experimental results demonstrate the ability of teleoperators to safely traverse through obstacles without visual cues, demonstrating the system's responsiveness, low-latency system design, and precision of the real-time feedback. The developed framework provides a modular and efficient architecture to achieve intuitive teleoperation of a drone within confined environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Survey for Scene Graph Generation Based on Pre-Trained Model
conference_papers.summary: Scene Graph Generation (SGG) aims to represent image content as structured graphs consisting of objects and their pairwise relationships, serving as an important intermediate representation for downstream tasks such as visual question answering, image retrieval, and robotic perception. Despite significant progress achieved by classical approaches, they remain constrained by the closed-vocabulary assumption, long-tail distributions, and limited reasoning capabilities. Recently, the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) and VisionLanguage Models (VLMs) has opened up new opportunities for advancing SGG. With strong semantic understanding, commonsense reasoning, and cross-modal alignment, these pre-trained models enable SGG to move beyond discriminative classification towards generative reasoning, thereby demonstrating stronger generalization in open-vocabulary scenarios. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive review of SGG methods empowered by pre-trained models. We introduce a new taxonomy that categorizes existing approaches according to the distinct roles played by pre-trained models, offering a clearer understanding of their contributions to traditional pipelines. In addition, we systematically analyzed the datasets and their evaluation metrics. Finally, we discussed the main issues that currently exist and provided some insights into future research directions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Study of Visual-Language Model for Defect Detection in Manufacturing Industries
conference_papers.summary: Deep learning models such as YOLO and Faster R-CNN have improved defect detection but remain limited by data requirements and generalization challenges. Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual perception with natural language reasoning, offering interpretable, context-aware, and scalable solutions. It provides interpretability by generating natural-language outputs that can explain predictions to support decision-making. Fine-tuning also enables the VLMs to learn subtle distinctions between defective and non-defective products. These characteristics make fine-tuned VLMs a practical and efficient solution for intelligent and sustainable manufacturing systems. The model demonstrated a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5:0.95) of 0.69 indicating strong detection accuracy and precise localization. These capabilities make VLMs promising tools for achieving sustainable, intelligent, and zero-defect manufacturing.
authors: Nik Azimah Zainab Nik Mohd Rahimi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Autonomous Behavior Tree Construction in Door Traversal Tasks
conference_papers.summary: The intelligent decision-making behavior of autonomous systems has developed to adaptive and well-informedly interact with complicated environments but obtaining intelligent decision-making behavior often comes at the cost of difficulty in condition designing and complexity of the system. In this research, we aims to design and implement a decision-making framework that combines Behavior Tree (BT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL), allowing RL to autonomously construct BTs by learning from the environment and feedback signals from the BT. Additionally, we propose a reward function to address hierarchy problems in a door traversal task. The results presented in this paper demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and reward function in enhancing the performance of the policies and the constructed BTs.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Radar Working Mode Recognition Method Based on Fusion of Local and Global Correlations
conference_papers.summary: Working mode recognition is a crucial component for enhancing the comprehensive performance and intelligence level of electronic-warfare systems, for modern multifunction radars (MFR). To address the inability of existing methods to fully fuse the local and global dependencies of radar pulse signals, this paper proposed a parallel hybrid framework for MFR working mode recognition based on ResNet and Transformer. First, a deep residual convolutional and a multi-head self-attention mechanism were employed to respectively model local and global correlations; then, the two feature sets were combined through a learnable weighted fusion and fed into a classification layer; finally high-precision sorting of the radar pulse signals were achieved through Softmax. The simulation results show that the recognition accuracy reaches 99.80% at an SNR of 10 dB and remains around 86.97% even under a low SNR condition of -6dB. Even when the pulse-sequence loss rate and the false-pulse injection rate are 50% and 30%, the accuracy still respectively holds at around 90% and 95%. Thus, the proposed algorithm notably enhances recognition accuracy under challenging conditions such as low signal-to-noise ratios, high data loss, and elevated false alarm rates.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Obstacle Avoidance Method for UAV Based on Velocity Obstacle Model and Improved Artificial Potential Field
conference_papers.summary: To address the obstacle avoidance problem for unmanned aerial vehicle during flight, this study proposes an obstacle avoidance method based on the velocity obstacle model and an improved artificial potential field. The velocity obstacle model is introduced to assist obstacle avoidance maneuver decision-making within the artificial potential field framework. Improvements to the artificial potential field function include the implementation of an elastic obstacle avoidance distance and dynamic adjustment of the potential field size. An auxiliary obstacle avoidance force is further incorporated to enhance avoidance efficiency. A obstacle avoidance model was established, and strategies for both the conflict resolution and trajectory restoration phases were designed. Comparative analysis of obstacle avoidance maneuver simulations across four typical scenarios verifies the feasibility and high efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Novel Defect Detection Method Guided by Density Load Matrix for Regional Growth
conference_papers.summary: Defects on the rail surface severely affect train operations and passenger safety. Traditional manual inspection is inefficiency and risky. Therefore, a point cloud defect detection method based on density load matrix guided regional growth is proposed. First, we propose a manifold clustering algorithm constrained by the normal vector to perform coarse segmentation on rail point cloud data, effectively addressing the issue of missed detections caused by uneven point cloud density distribution. Then, based on the density parameters provided by the rough segmentation, a region growth algorithm guided by the density load matrix is proposed for fine segmentation, which solves the problems of missing detection, false detection and low detection efficiency caused by the complex rail surface defects and irregular shape. Finally, experiments were carried out on eight defect areas in three rail sections, The experimental results show that compared with traditional methods, our method improves the detection accuracy index by an average of 4.7% and the IoU index by an average of 3.2%.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Multimodal Biosensing System for Real-Time Driver Monitoring and Adaptive Feedback
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents a multimodal biosensing driver monitoring system for real-time detection of driver drowsiness and psychological stress. The system leverages facial expression recognition, simulated EEG signal analysis, and EMG-based stress detection to assess the driver's physical and mental state. Three different machine learning models are used: a CNN for facial emotion classification, a Random Forest classifier for EEG-based drowsiness detection, and an MLP for EMG-based stress recognition. Each model is developed with a robust preprocessing pipeline and trained using either real or simulated physiological data. The outputs are analyzed by a central decision-making engine that autonomously adjusts the vehicle's music playback via the Spotify Web API, enhancing driver alertness and comfort. This architecture exemplifies the use of affective computing to support road safety, offering an intelligent and adaptive vehicle environment. Experimental results demonstrate reliable performance across all modalities, highlighting the system's potential for practical deployment.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Multi-Object Tracking Approach Based on the Integration of Motion Information and Appearance Features
conference_papers.summary: Multi-object tracking technology plays a critical role in intelligent vehicle environmental perception. However, camera motion can introduce prediction errors in Kalman filtering for object tracking, while inadequate extraction of appearance features compromises the effectiveness of association matching. To address these challenges, this study proposes a camera motion compensation approach based on the LucasKanade (LK) optical flow method and FAST feature detection, which effectively corrects Kalman filter prediction inaccuracies. To enhance the capability of appearance feature extraction, it employs CSPResNet as the backbone network and integrates a channel attention mechanism to develop an improved feature extraction architecture. Furthermore, a novel method for constructing a cost matrix by fusing motion and appearance information is introduced. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly enhances the accuracy and robustness of target tracking on the MOT dataset.
institutions: Anhui University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Modified U-Net Based Approach for Human Contour Extraction and its Hardware Realization
conference_papers.summary: We present an approach for accurate extraction of human contours from an image in this paper. This is motivated by applications in computer graphics, medical diagnosis and robotics. The U-net architecture designed for image segmentation is studied. A variation of the architecture is developed which is lightweight and adequate for contour extraction amidst a non-empty background. Ablation studies are performed to establish the efficacy of the proposed solution. The architecture proposed is also studied for hardware realization. Preliminary results based on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) are reported.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Method of NEAR-FIELD SIMULATION and Analysis with FDTD Algorithm
conference_papers.summary: The Finite-Difference-in-Time-Domain (FDTD) method is a significant numerical analytical approach for electromagnetic field calculations, applicable across diverse scenarios. Some professional software has been developed to solve electromagnetic simulation question. However, some of aspects about the software should be considered. Software concentrates about shallow single-mediums by setting some simple parameters. The simulations may have other results cause of the properties’ differences between the interfaces of different kinds of medium such as complicated discrete media. When meeting some experiments designed for special conditions such as discrete medium area with many complicated reflective objects, parameters and environment of the software can’t be modified according to the experimental conditions either. It may need specific update packages, which will spend a large amount of cost. This paper proposes a method to simulate the propagation of electromagnetic wave in near-field area with some of experiments by digitizing necessary objects such as reflective objects and combination of medium. By comparing to some of results compiled by other codes, the experiments show fine results.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Mesh Processing Scheme for Higher-Order Split-Conformal Cases in Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Method
conference_papers.summary: A mesh processing scheme for handling higher- order split-conformal cases in the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is presented, addressing challenges in simulating complex geometries involving thin and random metallic structures. It introduces a comprehensive framework that includes identification, classification, and processing techniques to accurately handle higher-order split-conformal mesh facets. The effectiveness of the scheme is demonstrated through an example, showing improved modeling accuracy with sparser mesh lines and reduced computational complexity.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Light Reconnaissance and Strike UAV System Design
conference_papers.summary: With the empowerment of modern warfare by technology, unmanned combat will be the primary form of future warfare. This paper addresses the mission requirements for identifying, tracking, and striking targets using lightweight unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with ammunition and other mechanisms. A lightweight integrated UAV system for surveillance and strike is designed, proposing both software and hardware system functionalities, components, and implementation plans. The system mainly includes a software system with image recognition technology as a core component and a hardware system focusing on control and payload. The study emphasizes image processing technology and UAV control technology in complex battlefield environments. Simulation analysis and experimental verification of this technology demonstrate the feasibility of the design scheme, suggesting further application and promotion.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Improving Delayed Graduation Prediction Accuracy in Employed Postgraduate Students
conference_papers.summary: With the continuous expansion of China's graduate student enrollment, the contradiction between cultivation quality and cultivation scale has been highlighted, and the phenomenon of delayed graduation has become more and more common, among which the problem of delayed graduation of employed graduate students is particularly prominent. In order to identify students facing the risk of delayed graduation in advance, this paper firstly analyzes the influence of two features, "gender" and "job type", on the accuracy of delayed graduation prediction through experiments, so as to determine the feature set for delayed graduation prediction. Subsequently, this paper designs a prediction framework based on multiple prediction algorithms, which can realize the optimal matching of prediction methods, key parameters and prediction data. Through experimental validation on the MBA dataset of a western university, this framework significantly outperforms other methods in terms of accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 scores, which are improved by 9.68%, 76.99%, 26.05%, and 73.81%, respectively. The Friedman mean rank test and the significance level test further confirm the superiority of this framework.
institutions: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Hierarchical Autonomous Parking Method Based on Complexity-Adaptive Hybrid-Action Constrained Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: Autonomous parking in narrow, irregular urban environments is challenging, as current planning methods often yield non-smooth trajectories and low success rates in constrained scenarios. This paper proposes Complexity-Aware Hybrid-Action Constrained Reinforcement Learning (CHCRL), a hierarchical method to address these issues. CHCRL first quantifies scenario difficulty via a fuzzy complexity model and uses a Fuzzy Inference System for target pose estimation in unstructured areas. Second, it employs a Constrained Markov Decision Process with a hybrid action space (discrete intentions, continuous parameters) for smooth path generation. Crucially, a complexity-driven adaptive constraint mechanism dynamically adjusts safety thresholds based on the environmental score. Experimental results in parallel and perpendicular scenarios demonstrate that CHCRL significantly outperforms baselines (PPO, SAC), exhibiting superior robustness, safety, and efficiency, especially in complex parking tasks.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Framework for Human-Reason-Based Trajectory Evaluation in Automated Vehicles
conference_papers.summary: One major challenge for the adoption and acceptance of automated vehicles (AVs) is ensuring that they can make sound decisions in everyday situations that involve ethical tension. Much attention has focused on rare, high-stakes dilemmas such as trolley problems. Yet similar conflicts arise in routine driving when human considerations, such as legality, efficiency, and comfort, come into conflict. Current AV planning systems typically rely on rigid rules, which struggle to balance these competing considerations and often lead to behaviour that misaligns with human expectations. This paper introduces a reasons-based trajectory evaluation framework that operationalises the tracking condition of Meaningful Human Control (MHC). The framework represents human agents' reasons (e.g., regulatory compliance) as quantifiable functions and evaluates how well candidate trajectories align with them. It assigns adjustable weights to agent priorities and includes a balance function to discourage excluding any agent. To demonstrate the approach, we use a real-world-inspired overtaking scenario, which highlights tensions between compliance, efficiency, and comfort. Our results show that different trajectories emerge as preferable depending on how agents' reasons are weighted, and small shifts in priorities can lead to discrete changes in the selected action. This demonstrates that everyday ethical decisions in AV driving are highly sensitive to the weights assigned to the reasons of different human agents.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Cluster Head Election Mechanism for Industrial IoT Based on the Integration of Association Rules and Decision Trees
conference_papers.summary: In recent years, the rapid growth of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has placed increasing demands on Low-Power and Lossy Networks (LLNs) for data collection and communication in complex environments. As key nodes in clustered architectures, Cluster Heads (CHs) directly influence network lifetime and transmission efficiency. This paper proposes a lightweight rule-based two-stage CH selection mechanism that integrates association-rule filtering with a decision-tree–style logical evaluator that combines association rule mining with a decision tree, jointly evaluating features such as neighbor density, residual energy, and communication cost to improve candidate filtering and final election accuracy. The mechanism is implemented in Contiki and evaluated through Cooja simulations. Results show that the proposed approach significantly enhances energy efficiency and extends network lifetime, offering a promising direction for intelligent CH election and adaptive communication protocols in LLNs.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent System Driven by LLMs for Meal-Level Personalized Nutrition Management
conference_papers.summary: Personalized nutrition management aims to tailor dietary guidance to an individual's intake and phenotype, but most existing systems handle food logging, nutrient analysis and recommendation separately. We present a next-generation mobile nutrition assistant that combines image based meal logging with an LLM driven multi agent controller to provide meal level closed loop support. The system coordinates vision, dialogue and state management agents to estimate nutrients from photos and update a daily intake budget. It then adapts the next meal plan to user preferences and dietary constraints. Experiments with SNAPMe meal images and simulated users show competitive nutrient estimation, personalized menus and efficient task plans. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi agent LLM control for personalized nutrition and reveal open challenges in micronutrient estimation from images and in large scale real world studies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: 3D-Printed Hasel Actuators with Integrated Fluidic Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor for Cardiac Assist Applications
conference_papers.summary: This work presents a fully 3D printed Hydraulically Amplified Self-Healing Electrostatic (HASEL) actuator integrated with a soft piezoresistive force sensor for cardiac assist applications. The actuator is fabricated via direct ink write (DIW) 3D printing, enabling precise and personalizable construction of elastomer shells, soft electrodes, and liquid dielectric cavities. A fluidic piezoresistive sensor is integrated for monitoring of pressure output while preserving the actuator's compliant properties. The actuator achieves up to 87.9% strain with rapid response and repeatability up to 7.5 Hz. The sensor also demonstrates minimal hysteresis due to the fluidic reset mechanism, and it exhibits a clear correlation between applied force and resistance when coupled with the actuator. This self-sensing system enables closed-loop control through correlating voltage, resistance, and force and meets the performance requirements for mechanical support of the heart. Compared to existing VADs, this approach offers improved bio-compatibility, adaptability, and sensing. This work establishes a foundation for self-sensing soft robotic systems for future biomedical devices.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Using Pi Zero SBCs as a Low-Cost Driver Monitoring Solution
conference_papers.summary: Driver monitoring systems have become a vital component of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) for vehicle safety. According to the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, drowsy driving contributes to nearly 100,000 accidents annually. Early driver monitoring systems relied on vehicle sensor data, and current systems often use eye-tracking technology. Recently, there has been a rising interest in applying machine vision and deep learning to driver monitoring systems. Machine vision allows for advanced driver monitoring, such as detecting driver attention states, smartphone use, and seat belts, but machine vision systems typically require high processing power, which increases the device cost. This paper introduces a cost-effective driver monitoring system utilizing Pi Zero Single Board Computers (SBCs) like the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W board, and Radxa Zero 3 W board, combined with a deep learning CNN, the system is capable of identifying various driver states, including safe driving, distraction, drowsiness, and smartphone use.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Umbrella Reinforcement Learning - A Tool for Hard Problems
conference_papers.summary: We propose an approach for addressing Reinforcement Learning (RL) problems. It combines the ideas of umbrella sampling, borrowed from Monte Carlo technique of computational physics and chemistry, with optimal control methods, and is realized on the base of neural networks. This results in a powerful algorithm, designed to solve hard RL problems - the problems, with long-time delayed reward, state-traps sticking and a lack of terminal states. It outperforms the prominent algorithms, such as PPO, RND, iLQR and VI, which are among the most efficient for the hard problems. The new algorithm deals with a continuous ensemble of agents and expected return, that includes the ensemble entropy. This results in a quick and efficient search of the optimal policy in terms of “exploration-exploitation trade-off” in the state-action space.
institutions: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Towards Responsible and Ethical AI Chatbot in Education: A Guideline for Developers
conference_papers.summary: With the expansion of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the penetration of AI chatbots into every aspect of people's daily lives, discussions and issues related to AI ethics and responsibility began to arise simultaneously. A large portion of AI users remain ignorant of such ethical discussions, while a significant percentage of developers lack precautionary measures to prevent irresponsible AI behaviors. An increasing number of companies and organizations are taking action to address the problems. Despite the efforts, prominent issues still prevail. Most existing solutions are too general and theoretical; few are narrowed down to examine the specific application scenario of AI chatbots in education. In response, this study aims to address the arising concerns and the lack of a satisfying solution. After conducting an extensive literature review and performing a detailed analysis of survey data, this study develops a comprehensive guideline about AI ethics and responsible AI, which specifically targets undergraduate developers and guides them during their development of AI chatbots used in education. This guideline successfully bridges the knowledge gap, raises awareness about AI ethics, and acts as the first guideline for undergraduate students, influencing future development practices.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: TSHC-DTS: A Two Stages Semi-supervised Dialogue Topic Segmentation Based on Siamese Transformers and Hierarchical Clustering
conference_papers.summary: Dialogue segmentation is one of the fundamental tasks in natural language processing that involves partitioning a dialogue into coherent segments or topics. Previous methods often explore only the surface level of contextual features such as lexical features. The proposed method in this paper is a two-stage approach to dialogue segmentation. The first stage uses a Hierarchical Clustering algorithm to group semantically similar utterances based on the embeddings. The second stage uses a Siamese Transformer to calculate the similarity between the utterance pairs in each group. The proposed method can detect both broad and subtle transitions within the dialogue. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies segment boundaries compared with other methods.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Stable and Safe Navigation Scheme for Mobile Robots Under Moving Obstacle Presence
conference_papers.summary: This paper reports a controller design methodology for a differential drive wheeled mobile robot (DDWMR) model which considers both safety and stability properties of the robot's operation. The proposed methodology first constructs a stabilizing controller using Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) concept and then generates a polynomial function-type reference trajectory to seamlessly connect the initial and final poses of the DDWMR. Subsequently, a Control Barrier Function (CBF) based scheme is used to ensure the safety of the DDWMR movement in avoiding moving obstacles while driving on the constructed reference trajectory. By the proposed CLF-CBF integration, the proposed approach offers an efficient solution for autonomous navigation of DDWMR in the presence of moving obstacles while also addresses the challenges posed by its nonholonomic constraint. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is shown through simulations which demonstrate the robot's ability to perform safe and stable collision-free movement and navigation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Self-Recovery of Quadrupedal Robot Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: Quadruped robots are commonly used for navigating difficult terrains. However, they remain vulnerable to falls in unpredictable and unstructured environments. To ensure continuous operation, a self-recovery behavior is necessary. In this paper we present a self-recovery mechanism using Proximal Policy Optimization. This method eliminates the need for complex kinematic calculations. The proposed approach was trained and tested on the UnitreeA1 quadruped robot within the simulation environment to achieve effective self-recovery behavior. The results demonstrate the potential of this method as a reliable solution for self-recovery in quadruped robots.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: SATYA: Smart AI-driven Talent Yield Analyzer for Resume Screening and Recommendation Evaluation
conference_papers.summary: The hiring process is becoming increasingly complex, as HR departments are overwhelmed with large volumes of resumes and recommendations that require in-depth analysis. This paper presents SATYA (Smart AI-driven Talent Yield Analyzer), a comprehensive AI system that automates the resume screening process, validates recommendations, and enhances the accuracy of talent acquisition. By leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), and graph-based algorithms, SATYA assesses resumes, verifies skill claims, evaluates recommendation credibility, and generates final candidate scores. Trained on a dataset of 1000 resumes manually scored by HR experts, SATYA achieved an accuracy of 91.4%, significantly outperforming traditional resume screening methods. This paper describes the architecture of SATYA, detailing the resume scoring model, recommendation network analysis, skill validation process, and multi-objective candidate evaluation. The system's scalable design ensures that it can be integrated into existing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to improve talent acquisition efficiency.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Robotic Arm Design and Simulation for Remote Maintenance in the DTT Fusion Reactor
conference_papers.summary: The need for low-carbon, predictable, and reliable power has driven the European community to establish the EUROfusion project, aiming to provide grid electricity by the mid-21st century through nuclear fusion plants integrated with renewable energy sources. A key component of this initiative is the Divertor Tokamak Test facility (DTT) in Frascati, Italy, by ENEA, which will test reactor configurations and technologies for the future DEMOnstration (DEMO) reactor. Due to neutron-induced radioactivity, remote-controlled robots will perform maintenance on plasma-exposed components, operating during non-active periods. This paper proposes a robotic arm designed to perform pipe extraction and positioning in confined environments as part of the DTT's Divertor Handling subsystem. The robotic system described and its working environment are tested using a model of the system built in a multibody environment. Results allow to to evaluate joints motors specifications and the capability of the manipulator to achieve the task. The end effector trajectory is designed to avoid collision with the environment during the maneuver.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Robot for Solar Panel Cleaning with Sling-Based Mechanism
conference_papers.summary: This research focuses on the design and development of a solar panel cleaning robot system. The main objective is to provide flexibility for use in a variety of environments, including both solar rooftops and solar farms. This design can be install at the top corner of the panel area and the movement is designed into two motions. The vertical cleaning uses a wire rope drive module in the up and down direction, while cleaning with a rotating brush set. The robot moves horizontally using a horizontal drive module to move to the next area. The robot can be used with solar panels with an edge thickness of 3–4 centimeters and a vertical length of 1.5-4 meters. The robot can move on the solar panel and cross the gap between the panels up to 3 centimeters. The rope pulley driving set used for vertical movement has a distance sensor accuracy of 99.19%, while the robot is controlled via an RF wireless remote control.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Recognition Method of Tomato Ripeness Based on YOLOv7 and YOLOv8
conference_papers.summary: The increasing demand for efficient and accurate agricultural practices necessitates advanced technological solutions in crop management. One critical aspect is the accurate classification of tomato ripeness, essential for optimizing harvesting processes and ensuring product quality. Traditional methods are labor-intensive and prone to errors, emphasizing the need for automated systems. This research addresses this issue by exploring the application of advanced computer vision models, specifically YOLOv7 and YOLOv8, for tomato ripeness classification. The primary objectives were to develop and train YOLOv7 and YOLOv8 models, compare their performance, and evaluate YOLOv8's robustness under various simulated real-world conditions. Trained on a dataset of unripe, ripe, and rotten tomatoes, YOLOv8 demonstrated superior performance compared to YOLOv7, with higher precision, recall, and F1-scores across all categories of tomatoes. Further analysis included assessing YOLOv8's resilience to vary brightness, blurring, and noise addition. Results indicated that YOLOv8 maintained robust performance under these conditions, though slight declines in accuracy were observed. In conclusion, YOLOv8 proved to be a more effective and robust model for tomato ripeness classification, achieving higher true positive rates and overall better performance metrics than YOLOv7. These findings suggest that YOLOv8 is well-suited for practical deployment in agricultural settings, offering significant improvements in the accuracy and reliability of tomato classification.
institutions: Tun Hussein Onn University of Malaysia

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: ROS 2 Application to the Safety Monitoring of Collaborative Robots
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the application of a safety monitoring algorithm for collaborative robots (cobots). Cobots become increasingly common in various workplaces, such as manufacturing lines and even restaurant kitchens. The heavy-duty robots can assist human operators by handling heavy loads, reducing the physical strain of the job. However, safety concerns arise due to the close proximity and direct interaction between cobots and humans. To ensure real-time monitoring of potential accidents, this paper considers the use of a redundant fault detection algorithm. This algorithm relies on comparing outputs from redundant systems or sensor data with the actual robot's performance. Any significant discrepancy between these values signals a potential fault in the robot, triggering an accident alarm. In this study, the Gazebo simulator was employed as the redundant system. Gazebo is a widely-used, open-source 3D robotics simulator that integrates seamlessly with ROS (Robot Operating System). ROS 2, the next generation of ROS, serves as the middleware framework for building and executing robotic applications. The heavy-duty robot was modeled in Gazebo and controlled through ROS 2 nodes for communication and operation. A synthetic fault was introduced in one of the robot's joints, and another Gazebo simulation acted as the real system. Joint positions were monitored, and any deviation from normal operations signaled the presence of a fault. Consequently, integrating Gazebo with ROS 2 provides an effective analytical model to compare against real systems for safety monitoring purposes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Proposal of an Automated Feature Engineering Pipeline for High-Dimensional In-Vehicle Bus Data Using Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: The complexity of the communication between electronic control units in contemporary vehicles is increasing with the rising demand of customer functions such as automated driving and infotainment resulting in up to several thousand data elements (signals) per data bus. Consequently, engineers have no choice but to apply data science methods to extract meaningful insights from this high-dimensional communication data, particularly before training machine learning models. A critical step in this process is identifying the bus signals relevant for a specific data science task. Extracting them manually is not only time-consuming but it also demands a high degree of in-vehicle communication knowledge which is hard to obtain. To address this challenge, we propose an automated feature engineering approach that leverages reinforcement learning combined with state-of-the-art feature selection and engineering methods and a tunable sampling rate for the bus data. Due to the high degree of automation it requires little prior knowledge of how in-vehicle communication works. Our method enhances important key performance indicators for machine learning model quality for the task of energy consumption prognosis and significantly reduces the number of bus signals required for accurate model predictions. This approach does not only improve the understanding of relevant data but also reduces the model's size as less features are used for the prediction, leading to more efficient and interpretable machine learning solutions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Proposal for the Design of an Educational Robot to Enhance Learning and Support Children with attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder from the Fifth Year of Age at Low Cost-Nubox
conference_papers.summary: This research work presents the design of an educational robot that enhances learning in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder at low cost. The design of the educational robot aims to support learning through structured and focused interaction with games and activities that improve attention and memory, this enhances and keeps children engaged with immediate and positive feedback, it also has a striking mechanical design for the user being the PLA material, as well as a Raspberry Pi 3 controller that controls the educational robot with great efficiency and with enough memory to store and carry out the purpose for which it was designed, also mention about the 7″ touch screen that improves the interaction with the user and the speakers that produce white noise for the improvement of attention. A mixed methodology between VDI 2206 and MIT was used to meet the proposed objectives. The results of this research will improve attention and memory with a pleasant and practical design, a stable structure, intuitive mechanism and electronic components suitable for children with mild ADHD.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Proposal for the Design of a Mechatronic Intelligent Irrigation System with Spraying for Fruit Trees
conference_papers.summary: This research work presents the design of an intelligent mechatronic sprinkler irrigation system for fruit trees using IoT technology. The design aims to help with the irrigation process through technologies and optimize the agricultural system, the mechanical design has pipes that will help the irrigation of 2 planting lines per pipe line in this way we optimize irrigation, as well as the ESP32 DEVKIT 1 microcontroller, which by its characteristics of being able to connect to a Wifi network is the ideal for the IoT aspect, in addition to comment on the solenoid valves or solenoid valves, The Cayenne Mydevices platform was chosen for its easy distribution, creation and design of this interface, and also for being free, having a version for mobile devices that allows an improvement and good performance in their work, to meet the objectives the VDI 2206 methodology was used, designed especially for mechatronic systems. The results of this research will improve the method of irrigation of fruit trees with internet of things technology, facilitating management through an interface for the farmer.
