conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Prediction of Particulate Matter in a Mining Environment via Machine Learning
conference_papers.summary: The objective of this research work is to present an investigation in the application of machine learning algorithms in the prediction of particulate matter concentration in an open cast coal mine. Three types of neural networks, Long Short Term Memory, Gated Recurrent Unit and Recurrent Neural Networks are used to estimate and forecast the particulate concentration in the mine. The neural networks are bench-marked using Linear Regression and support vector machines. The results indicate that the Recurrent Neural Network performs well under conditions with short time lags, whereas both the Long Short Term Memory and Gated Recurrent Unit neural networks perform well over a wider range of lag times. Future work includes the implementation of these algorithms in early warning and intervention systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Optimizing Deep Reinforcement Learning Models for Stock Trading with Technical Indicators
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the development and optimization of a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent for stock trading, leveraging different technical indicator strategies to enhance decision-making process. The study tackles the challenges associated with using the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicators and proposes a robust DRL framework that integrates different technical indicators. Through comprehensive data acquisition, feature engineering, and model development processes, our proposed method demonstrates the potential of using DRL in predicting stock performance and executing profitable trades. The ensemble strategy emerged as the top performer, achieving up to 76% cumulative returns with a Sharpe ratio of 1.37 for the stock “AAPL.” These results indicate the effectiveness of the developed DRL models and their improvements over existing approaches in literature. The study concludes that DRL-based trading strategies offer significant advantages in profitability and risk management, paving the way for more advanced and reliable automated trading systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: OFVO: A Visual Odometry Designed for Motion Trajectory Estimation of Autonomous Vehicles
conference_papers.summary: Camera motion estimation is crucial for measuring the trajectory of moving objects. Fortunately, there is an odometry to help us solve this problem. Unlike other research works that primarily rely on odometry for indoor robots and drones, we aim to utilize visual odometry to enhance our autonomous driving perception system. The outstanding contributions of this paper are as follows: Firstly, by utilizing the feature point method in image processing, we explore various feature extraction and matching algorithms to develop a visual odometry system based on Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) and Fast Library for Approximate Nearest Neighbors (FLANN) for autonomous cars, which is named the ORB-FLANN Visual Odometry System (OFVO). Secondly, we validate our algorithm in the self-driving simulator Carla and achieve satisfactory results.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Next-Generation Diabetes Care: Robust Adaptive Optimal Glucose Control Using Machine Learning, Wearable Integration and Microwave Sensors
conference_papers.summary: Managing diabetes effectively is vital to prevent complications such as heart disease, nerve damage, and kidney issues. This research shows that weight control and tailored interventions can improve blood sugar and metabolic health. This paper reviews the microwave sensor for continuous, real-time glucose monitoring, designed for wearables like smartwatches. By integrating type-2 fuzzy-logic and machine learning, the sensors can offer accurate glucose readings and monitor additional physiological markers, optimizing personalized interventions for type-1 diabetes. This innovation will aim to advance diabetes management with reliable, user-friendly health monitoring.
institutions: National Yunlin University of Science and Technology
National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Multiple Model Based Online Surface Estimation During Collisions
conference_papers.summary: As modern robotic systems operate in dynamic and unpredictable environments, it is essential that they can handle impacts effectively. To ensure efficient and safe control, it is crucial to identify the physical properties of surfaces and their impact on the robot's dynamic response. However, identifying surfaces and applying a suitable control scheme remains a challenge. The proposed method uses a multi-model adaptive control approach that implements a bank of Kalman filters to form surface estimations. Numerical simulations demonstrate the method's effectiveness by simulating a robotic actuator impacting different surfaces when the system dynamics are unknown. Evaluations are presented where the correct model is included and excluded from the bank of Kalman filters and are considered. A demonstration of the physical robotic system is provided, showing that this method can identify the model and switch to the correct controller within one impact with a surface.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion Floor Location Method Based on Extended Kalman Algorithm
conference_papers.summary: This paper investigates an extended Kalman filter-based barometer and IMU fusion floor localization method, aiming to solve the problem of precise floor localization for mobile robots that need to take elevators. By establishing an index between spatial height and floor levels, the paper uses the extended Kalman algorithm to fuse filtered IMU acceleration data with barometric data optimized by the least squares method to obtain the robot's height data. Subsequently, the robot's floor data is obtained based on the floor index. Experiments show that the comprehensive height prediction error of this paper is within 0.10m, and the floor prediction accuracy reaches 98%. The research provides effective technical support for floor localization of mobile robots in elevator scenarios.
institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Motion Planning of Counterpoint Parallel Robot Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
conference_papers.summary: In order to realize the high-efficiency and high-precision operation of the counter-parallel robot in a limited motion space, a method based on the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm was proposed to solve the optimal running trajectory of the counter-parallel robot in time and joint energy consumption. In order to solve the problem that the starting and ending attitudes of the moving platform are very close to the given motion limit boundary, and the optimal path without collision cannot be found, a trajectory planning method based on task-space partitioning and joint-space segmentation interpolation is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Through comparison, it is concluded that IPSO is more suitable for the optimal motion planning of time energy consumption of parallel robots than general PSO, PSOGWO, GWO and IVY.
institutions: Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Modeling and Validation of a Single-Axis Tilting Quadrotor with Enhanced Attitude Control

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Measuring the Chatbot-User Interaction: Scale Development and Validation
conference_papers.summary: This study presents the development and rigorous validation of the Chatbot-User Interaction Scale (CUIS), following Churchill's (1979) scale development framework across four stages. As chatbots increasingly transcend basic task-oriented functions due to rapid advances in artificial intelligence and natural language processing, this research addresses a timely need for a comprehensive tool to measure key aspects of chatbot-user interaction (CUI). The scale evaluates three core dimensions–interoperability, affinity, and intelligence credibility–validated through 18 items demonstrating strong convergent, construct, and discriminant validity. Additionally, the study establishes a positive “CUI-satisfaction-continuance” framework, highlighting the scale's theoretical strength. The evidence presented may benefit further efforts in similar issues by offering in-depth insights for future research and making this paper a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to enhance chatbot functionality and user engagement.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Master Surgical Scheduling of Multi-Surgeon Surgical Schedules Using a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model and Genetic Algorithms
conference_papers.summary: The purpose of this work is to develop a master surgical scheduling for a case study of a large-scale public hospital in Thailand using a mixed-integer linear programming model (MILP) and a genetic algorithm (GA). Due to the high volume of operations that must be handled every day, our main objective is to create a schedule that maximizes OR utilization, minimizes room overtime, and reduces idle time between surgical patients. The data from Thammasat University Hospital were analyzed and simulated to generate a timetable from daily to weekly schedule. Our results show that an exact solution can be obtained by MILP for a simple problem while a large CPU run time is incurred for the complex problems. GA provided the optimal solution for a complex large-scale problem. The schedule generated by the proposed GA is more flexible and the staff can improve it to obtain more practical timetable in real-life situations, such as increasing the number of surgeries, setting a time block for specific surgical specialties, and handling emergency cases.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Machine Learning for Prognostication: Harnessing Chronic Wound Registry Data for Predicting Wound Healing Outcomes
conference_papers.summary: Chronic wounds have been a pressing concern worldwide, and the most significant issue is unnecessary amputations. It is made worse by delays in receiving suitable treatment which can be avoided. To address this, this paper introduces a pivotal algorithm that utilizes Gradient Boosting classifier to forecast the likelihood of wound healing within specific time frames. The wound healing predictions are made at three distinct intervals: 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months following the initial visit to the healthcare facility by the patient. The algorithm relies exclusively on the data gathered during the patient's initial visit and a systematically assembled chronic wound registry. The algorithm yields an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.80, 0.74, and 0.70 for the prediction at the 3 time-points using the baseline features. Additionally, this paper also yields an additional result of 0.76 and 0.73 for the prediction at the three-months and six-months using the baseline plus one-month data. The proposed prediction model uses mainly tabular data which are readily available to clinicians after the initial visit. This helps the clinicians to have a more accurate diagnosis of the wound healing time, therefore allowing the clinicians to intervene early to prevent unnecessary amputations that are very costly to the patients and to provide the appropriate treatment to prevent the loss of lives through chronic wound injuries.
institutions: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Machine Learning for Enhanced Underwriting: Predicting Premiums in Health Insurance
conference_papers.summary: In the evolving field of Insurance, Machine Learning (ML) has emerged as a transformative tool for enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of insurance underwriting, particularly in health insurance, a sector experiencing increased demand post-pandemic. This research develops an ML model aimed at improving premium prediction within this domain. Utilizing a health insurance database from Kaggle, we conducted a comparative analysis of several ML models—XGBoost, Random Forest, Neural Network Regression, and a baseline Linear Regression—to establish performance benchmarks. Our methodology included rigorous data analysis and application of ML model optimization techniques such as feature engineering and selection, hyperparameter tuning through Grid Search, Random Search, and Bayesian Optimization, as well as overfitting prevention strategies like Pruning and Early Stopping. The XGBoost model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2582.3, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 4625.0, and an R2 value of 86.59%. This research not only advances the application of ML in predictive premium pricing but also provides a structured approach for future studies in the insurance industry's underwriting processes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Machine Learning Implementation for Estimation of Earthquake Magnitude Using Strong-Motion Data
conference_papers.summary: Determining earthquake parameters in a short time presents a trade-off between speed and accuracy. To enhance both the accuracy and speed of magnitude determination after the arrival of the P-wave, we introduce a machine learning-based magnitude prediction model using the Random Forest Regression method (RFmag) for earthquake magnitude estimation. In this study, strong-motion data obtained from the Agency for Meteorology Climatology and Geophysics (BMKG) were used to calculate the input parameters for the RFmag model. The model utilizes 12 significant parameters extracted from 30 seconds of strong-motion data recorded after the P-wave arrival as input features. The results showed that the RFmag model achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 94.49% with a standard deviation of 0.36, indicating its capability to estimate earthquake magnitude effectively. Therefore, the RFmag model demonstrates significant potential for application in real-time Tsunami Early Warning (TEW) operations, offering a more efficient and reliable method for rapid magnitude estimation in Indonesia's seismically active regions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Enhancing Financial Compliance: A Focus on Anti-Money Laundering Applications
conference_papers.summary: Money laundering is dangerous to the world's finan-cial institutions, because it allows hiding illegal cash and supports various criminal activities. Due to reliance on manual procedures and rule-based systems, traditional Anti-Money Laundering (AML) techniques need assistance in managing the complexity and volume of contemporary financial transactions. This research explores how Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT-3 and BERT, can improve AML by utilizing cutting-edge natural language processing capabilities to provide more reliable and scalable money laundering detection and prevention solutions. By examining the transformational potential of LLMs in overcoming the drawbacks of conventional techniques, the research fills a significant vacuum in the present AML procedures. Enhancing transaction monitoring, refining client due diligence procedures, streamlining sanctions screening, and aiding in the production of precise suspicious activity notifications are among the primary study issues. The main assumption is that utilizing LLMs' capacity to handle unstructured data and spot complex patterns, AML accuracy and efficiency will significantly increase compared to traditional systems. The goals include implementing LLMs across AML functions, assessing their effectiveness with various datasets, as well as presenting empirical research and case studies to prove their superiority. By advancing our knowledge of and ability to use LLMs in financial compliance, this research is expected to strengthen the defenses against financial crimes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Optimization of Laser Marking Parameters Using Neural Networks and Genetic Algorithms
conference_papers.summary: Laser marking technology is essential in precision manufacturing, but optimizing its numerous parameters is com-plex and time-consuming with traditional methods. This study developed a fully automated laser marking system using the Draco series laser from Han's Laser, incorporating automatic loading and unloading mechanisms. By utilizing neural networks and genetic algorithms, we optimized laser marking on ABS materials. The research included COMSOL simulations of laser-material interactions, analysis of parameter variations on col-oration, temperature field distribution under laser irradiation, and prediction of marking effects for practical applications. The aim is to automate processes through algorithmic integration, providing an intelligent laser marking solution. The developed methodologies and algorithms are applicable to other manufac-turing optimizations, offering valuable insights for broader in-dustrial applications. Primary research focuses include COMSOL simulation and parameter analysis, developing an AI-integrated laser production line with color prediction, and exploring au-tomated laser marking on ABS material using neural networks and genetic algorithms.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Integration of Autonomous Mobile Robot with Elevators for Multi-Floor Transportation in Hospital Logistics
conference_papers.summary: Hospital logistics is another critical area where autonomous mobile robots play a vital role. In this research, autonomous mobile robots have been integrated with wireless devices based on Zigbee and Bluetooth protocols to test the interoperability of autonomous mobile robots and wireless devices when used with elevators. The success rates in four different formats between the AMR and wireless devices were found to be 85.71 %,94.29%,88.57%, and 91.43%. These results demonstrate a significant shift in the working capabilities of autonomous mobile robots, showing improved productivity when using wireless devices in conjunction with elevators. This integration highlights the potential for wireless devices to enhance the functionality of autonomous mobile robots in hospital settings.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Image-Based Game Quality Assurance Automation Process
conference_papers.summary: Traditional Quality Assurance (QA) practices often rely on manual testing, resulting in limiting efficiency and accuracy. To tackle these challenges, we propose an automated QA tool, utilizing Image AI technologies. The key difference from existing QA tools is that it is not dependent on specific engines or frameworks, such as web-based platforms. Instead, it can handle targets using only the name of the target process, offering the advantage of easily acquiring QA test images from dynamically changing target games. Our tool automatically detects in-game UI elements and images, extracting valuable information using built-in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) capabilities. By employing multi-scale template matching and a fine-tuned Vision Transformer (ViT) model, our system ensures reliable image detection across different screen resolutions and complex visual contexts.(Repo:https://github.com/eglabsid/AutonomousQA_Tool)

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Harnessing Diversity and Novelty Metrics in Evaluating Course Recommender Systems via a Machine Learning Approach
conference_papers.summary: This study analyses k-Nearest Neighbors, Matrix Factorisation, and Neural Collaborative Filtering (NCF) for developing a Course Recommendation System in higher education. Key metrics-Accuracy, Novelty, and Diversity-are used to evaluate trade-offs, particularly whether optimising for variety impacts Accuracy. Results indicate that N CF achieves the highest Accuracy while balancing Novelty and Diversity. Improvements in Novelty and Diversity are observed at specific cut-offs, though at some cost to Accuracy. These findings demonstrate the potential of NCF for balancing accuracy and variety in recommendations. Future work will explore algorithms like Gated Recurrent Units and Recurrent Neural Networks to enhance the system further.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Generating Spatial Binaural Environmental Audio Alert on a Personal Audio Device
conference_papers.summary: In this paper, we address the audio spatial alert, which aims to provide spatial binaural environmental audio alert on a personal audio device. Existing methods have achieved binaural sound reproduction in head mounted devices and relates to audio spatialization technique, but fails to teach the ability to determine the direction of environmental audio event producing source from the surrounding and generating a binaural sound alert by a virtual sound source in respect to current head direction of the user so that for that instant user can understand from which direction environmental sound is coming. To address these issues, we propose a method for providing spatial binaural environmental audio alert on a personal audio device. The proposed solution determines head direction and activity of a user in an environment in a time frame and, further includes capturing one or more audio events occurring in the environment in the time frame. This also includes Direction Estimation Model, which helps in determining direction of environmental audio event producing source. Hence, proposed PBAG (Personalized Binaural Alert Generator) localizes a virtual sound source for generating a spatial binaural audio alert with respect to current head direction of the user and providing the alert on the personal audio device.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Event-Triggered Moving Block Train Platooning Scheme Under Communication Loss Constraint
conference_papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenges of efficient coordination and safety assurance of moving block train platooning system. Conventional railway signaling method which relies on static block systems often fail to adapt to high frequency scenarios and thereby limiting the railway system's operational flexibility and scalability. The moving block signaling approach through communication-based train control (CBTC) technology has recently been proposed and viewed as a potential solution alternative to address such limitations. To enhance railway system opearational performance and safety, this paper proposes a control strategy combining sliding mode control (SMC) and event-triggered control (ETC) for a multi-agent system representation of train convoy operating under moving block signaling scheme. The proposed SMC is used to ensure robust tracking and coordination of the train convoy in the presence of inter-train communication loss, while ETC scheme is used to minimize communication and computation overhead in each train by updating the individual train's control actions only when deemed necessary. The proposed approach improves coordination, safety, and resource efficiency within complex, multi-agent train systems. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the combined control strategy in maintaining inter-train spacing even when data transmission loss/drop occur on several time instances.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Evaluation of Various Machine Learning Models in Forecasting Cricket Player Performance
conference_papers.summary: Predicting player performance is a critical aspect of sports analytics, aiding in decision-making and strategy development. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of multiple machine learning algorithms to forecast player performance in the dynamic sport of cricket. The research evaluates a range of algorithms, including Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Adaboost Regressor, XGBoost, and LightGBM, to predict both batting and bowling outcomes. Performance metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared (R2) scores are used to rigorously compare these models. The findings reveal that certain algorithms outperform others in predicting player success, offering valuable insights for team selection, strategy planning, and player development. A key contribution of this study is its in-depth examination of feature importance and hyperparameter optimization, which enhances the predictive power of the models. The study also highlights practical applications by exploring how these algorithms can be integrated with existing sports analytics platforms, bridging the gap between theoretical analysis and real-world implementation. Furthermore, the results provide a data-driven foundation for cricket teams, coaches, and analysts to leverage machine learning for more informed decisions, setting the stage for future research in sports analytics.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Evaluating the Impact of One-Shot Structured Pruning: A Noise Robustness Perspective
conference_papers.summary: The increasing complexity of neural networks in combination with the growing interest in edge computing has led to a surge in the development of neural network compression techniques. These methods aim to reduce the computational complexity of the networks while maintaining a high level of performance. However, the impact of compression on the robustness of the network is often overlooked. Therefore, in this work, we investigate the robustness of compressed neural networks by assessing the way a neural network behaves under different types and levels of noise. More specifically, we propose a robustness evaluation method that employs two different evaluation methodologies: a Multi-Level Monte Carlo simulation [1] and the CIFAR-100-C [2] dataset. We compare popular neural networks with their compressed versions, generated using an XAI-inspired one-shot structured channel pruning methodology. We systematically evaluate the robustness of the models pruned for different scenarios. Our results show that the pruned models can maintain their robustness properties in the presence of noise, and that specialization through pruning can improve a model's ability to handle corruptions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Evaluating Robustness of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Autonomous Shipping
conference_papers.summary: Recently, there has been growing interest in au-tonomous shipping due to its potential to improve maritime efficiency and safety. The use of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, can address the current navigational and operational challenges in autonomous shipping. In particular, inland waterway transport (IWT) presents a unique set of challenges, such as crowded waterways and variable environ-mental conditions. In such dynamic settings, the reliability and robustness of autonomous shipping solutions are critical factors for ensuring safe operations. This paper examines the robustness of benchmark deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, implemented for IWT within an autonomous shipping simulator, and their ability to generate effective motion planning policies. We demonstrate that a model-free approach can achieve an adequate policy in the simulator, successfully navigating port environments never encountered during training. We focus par-ticularly on Soft-Actor Critic (SAC), which we show to be inherently more robust to environmental disturbances compared to MuZero, a state-of-the-art model-based RL algorithm. In this paper, we take a significant step towards developing robust, applied RL frameworks that can be generalized to various vessel types and navigate complex port- and inland environments and scenarios.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Empathetic Variations Between Offensive Language and Sentiment in Kuwaiti Dialect
conference_papers.summary: Online user-generated content platforms offer a space for anyone to communicate with others and share their thoughts publicly online, with or without their identity being disclosed. This feature makes online conversations more depen-dent on users' empathetic attitudes. More offensive language is displayed in conversations when participants have negative empathy and less when they share positive empathy toward each other. Accordingly, this study aims to conduct a preliminary study for the first Kuwaiti offensive language and sentiment analysis dataset and provide a lexicon-based approach to analyzing the empathetic content of each task. Our results demonstrate the positive potential of our approach as it shows some valuable and noticeable empathetic patterns under each subset from the dataset based on their offensiveness and sentiment labels.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Automatic Chiptune Generation for Game Music
conference_papers.summary: This project investigates how artificial intelligence can be used to generate chiptune music that changes based on emotional cues in real-time. Utilising Long Short-Term Memory networks, the research aims to create emotionally impactful and musically unified chiptune music to increase players' involvement in video games. The YM2413-MDB dataset, which includes FM video game music from the 1980s with detailed emotional annotations, acts as the model's training data. Essential steps consist of preprocessing the Musical Instrument Digital Interface files into tokenized events, training the LSTM to recognise patterns and emotions, and creating a user-friendly interface for user input. The proposed solution includes generating music sequences that mirror chosen emotions, converting the sequences into sound and evaluating the model's success through automated and human evaluations. This study focuses on filling the void in emotion-based music creation in real-time with the goal of expanding interactive entertainment and enhancing game experiences using chiptune sound tracks that adapt to the gameplay.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Development of a Reconfigurable Holonomic Mobile Manipulation Cobot for Smart Factory 5.0
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the design, experimentation, and evaluation of a reconfigurable holonomic mobile cobot equipped with a Mecanum wheel base and a coupling locking mechanism to support versatile manipulation tasks in smart factory 5.0 environments. The system, designed for omnidirectional movement and dynamic adaptability, aims to enhance flexibility and precision in human-robot collaborative manufacturing. Through a series of experiments, we assessed the accuracy of the mobile base in loaded and unloaded conditions and evaluated the alignment and coupling success of the cobot with a detachable manipulator arm module. Results indicate that the Mecanum wheel base achieves an impressive 80% alignment success rate using ArUco marker tracking, demonstrating reliable mobility and tracking in dynamic environments. However, the coupling locking mechanism achieved only a 20% success rate, revealing limitations in the locking system's tolerance to minor misalignments. These findings highlight the cobot's strengths in adaptive navigation and tracking accuracy while underscoring the need for further development of the coupling mechanism for consistent operation. For future work, we will focuses on refining the coupling system, enhancing alignment feedback through additional visual markers, and optimizing control algorithms for load-bearing accuracy. This study provides a foundational step toward implementing reliable, reconfigurable robotic systems that meet the complex demands of next-generation manufacturing environments.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Development of a 3 DoF Underactuated Robotic Finger
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces the design and evaluation of a three-degree-of-freedom (3 DoF) underactuated robotic finger, inspired by the 3-Finger Adaptive Robot Gripper by ROBOTIQ. The proposed design utilizes a single DC servo motor to drive multiple joints, simplifying the actuation system while ensuring adaptability in diverse grasping scenarios. Its underactuated mechanism dynamically adjusts to object geometries, enabling versatile and efficient manipulation. The performance of the robotic finger was assessed through experimental testing using MATLAB Simulink. Calibration methods were implemented to align the system's response with desired input, significantly improving precision and reliability. The results demonstrate the system's potential applications in prosthetics, industrial automation, and robotics, offering a cost-effective and robust solution for tasks requiring adaptive manipulation. This work contributes to advancing robotic gripper technology by achieving a balance between simplicity, functionality, and adaptability.
institutions: Tun Hussein Onn University of Malaysia

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Development and Integration of an Autonomous In-House Manipulator Arm for Enhanced Object Interaction in Rescue Robotics
conference_papers.summary: Manipulator arms in rescue robots remain a challenge in both competitions and real-life situations. In this paper, we present an autonomous in-house manipulator system specifically engineered to enrich object interaction in rescue robotics for the RoboCup Rescue Robot Competition 2024 as a contestant under the iRAP Robot Team. The manipulator is equipped with an RGB-D camera, providing pose estimation of objects by leveraging 3D models generated through prior scanning. YOLOv8 2D object detection is employed to identify objects in the scene, and cropped depth images are used to subsequently generate object point clouds. Iterative Closest Point (ICP) techniques, including point-to-plane, point-to-point, and color registration, are utilized in conjunction to provide accurate alignment between the object's point cloud and the pre-scanned 3D models. These techniques work together to minimize Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) during the alignment process, ensuring reliability of pose estimation before executing robotic movement actions. The system also uses IMU data from the RGB-D camera for manipulator impact detection. The entire system is developed within the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework, utilizing MoveIt for motion planning and control. The methodologies and innovations introduced in this work are adapted for deployment in the challenging and unexpected environments of the RoboCup Rescue Robot Competition.
institutions: King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of a Hierarchical Motion Control Framework for Bipedal Robots on Various Structured Terrains
conference_papers.summary: The prevalence of structured terrains in human environments highlights the importance of developing a versatile controller adaptable to multiple terrain types. This paper presents a detailed implementation of a motion control framework that ensures dynamic and robust locomotion on various structured terrains. The framework adopts a hierarchical planning and control architecture, where the high-level module uses the inverted pendulum simplified model without constant height constraint to plan the three-dimensional center of mass (CoM) trajectory through model predictive control (MPC) and the low-level module employs optimization-based whole-body control (WBC) to track and execute the planned trajectories, utilizing the full-body kinematic and dynamic models. This framework is deployed on our self-developed 12-degree-of-freedom (DoF) bipedal robot. Extensive simulation tests demonstrate that the robot can achieve stable and dynamic omni-directional walking on flat ground and exhibit robust performance on other common structured terrains, including stairs and slopes. The results validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control framework.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Indoor Autonomous Drone: Navigation in Unknown Environment Based on Relative Position Decision
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents a new approach for indoor autonomous drone navigation using a deep reinforcement learning algorithm, specifically the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm with position-based action (relative position) decisionmaking. Real-world tests with a quadrotor drone demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in practical applications. The unmanned aerial vehicle can safely navigate from a starting point to a destination without prior map knowledge, achieving smooth movements through a position control loop. The results confirm the suitability of this approach for real-world deployment. Compared to traditional map-based path planning algorithms like the A-star algorithm, the paths generated by our method show similar trends. Using relative position as an action in our approach allows the model to adapt to different robot platforms without retraining it when the kinematic model changes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Deep Learning Based Smart Wheelchair Navigation Optimization for Multi-Lighting Conditions
conference_papers.summary: Smart wheelchairs have begun to be developed to help people with special disabilities in helping their independent mobility, including the use of head movement for the navigation. One of the major challenges in smart wheelchair navigation is low-light conditions, which poor image quality can interfere with automated navigation systems. The purpose of this study is to develop a smart wheelchair navigation system that is able to operate well in low-light conditions, thereby supporting the improvement of the performance in multi-lighting conditions. This study proposes the integration of the low-light enhancement method, RetinexNet, for the preprocessing stage applied to the EfficientNetv2 model to improve the quality of head movement image data in low-light conditions. The proposed approach successfully improves the performance of the classification process, which initially experienced overfitting on low-light images. In low-light conditions, the model evaluation metrics increase significantly with all metric values reaching 1.0 in all model versions (BO, B1, B2, B3), indicating overfitting. The highest performance produced on enhanced images was achieved by the EfficientNetv2 B2 variation, with precision, recall, and f1-score values of 0.735, and accuracy of 0.873. The use of the RetinexNet method for low-light enhancement has been proven to improve image quality, which also affects the classification performance of the EfficientNet model in multi-lighting conditions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Convolution on Honeycomb Structures with Three-axis Coordinate System
conference_papers.summary: This paper discusses convolution over two-dimensional regular tessellation. Convolution is one of the principal mathematical operations in engineering field. Tessellations are often referred to as “honeycombs,” and found in wide range of engineering objects, pixel structures in image data, for instance. In order to formulate the convolutional operation over a honeycomb structure, this paper applies a three-axis coordinate system for the honeycomb structure, named “HCP.” Along with convolution, accompanying operations such as stride and padding are also contrived to facilitate software implementation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Benchmarking a ROS 2-Based Indirect SLAM on Edge Devices
conference_papers.summary: This study provides insights into SLAM performance on embedded systems and introduces an unsupervised parameter tuning approach for enhanced localisation accuracy. Our paper benchmarks a ROS 2-based indirect Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) system across six NVIDIA Jetson devices: Orin Nano 4 GB, Orin Nano 8 GB, Orin NX 8 GB, Orin NX 16 GB, AGX Orin 32 GB Auvidea, and AGX Orin 32 GB Devkit, using sequences from the KITTI dataset. The edge devices differ significantly in GPU computing power, number of CPU cores, CPU clock frequency as well as memory. SLAM evaluations are conducted within Docker containers to ensure consistency, with feature detection parameters optimised using an unsupervised tuning approach for each device. In addition to localisation accuracy, hardware utilisation is analysed, revealing that less than a half of CPU capabilities and approximately 5– 10 % of GPU power are utilised. The results indicate that in the default configuration devices with lower computing power demonstrate higher fluctuation in SLAM localisation accuracy. However, optimising feature parameters improves accuracy stability, especially for less powerful edge devices, indicating that even lower-powered but more energy-saving devices can achieve similar performance when an optimised balance between feature quantity and runtime constraints is achieved.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Autonomous Docking for Underwater Drones Using ArUco Marker Based Localization
conference_papers.summary: Autonomous docking for underwater drones is crucial for various marine applications. This paper introduces an approach to autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) docking using ArUco marker-based localization, as demonstrated by Project MIRA, at the Tau Autonomy Center, Norway. The method combines a control system with dual-feed computer vision based perception to achieve autonomy. The control system is based on a cascaded PID controller fine-tuned using various external sensors and optimization techniques. The vision system utilizes ArUco markers for 3D positioning. Our method uses visual markers to help the drone navigate to a custom docking pad. We achieved stable and reliable docking by combining advanced control systems using visual-inertial sensors. This work highlights the potential of using visual markers and smart control systems for underwater drone operations.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Automatic Control of Drug Infusion and Spinal Fluid Drainage Through Data Collection and Look-Up Table Learning
conference_papers.summary: This paper builds and tests the performance of an automatic control algorithm for injecting drugs and draining spinal fluid during hospitalization after cancer surgery. Drug injection and spinal fluid drainage can detect pressure changes during the drug injection process and automatically control drug injection, interruption, and spinal fluid drainage according to pressure changes. To handle this process, data is collected, look-up tables are built, and data learning is performed. If the pressure rises to 15 mmHg during the drug injection process, the injection is stopped, and the spinal fluid is drained. If the pressure decreases to 5 mmHg during the spinal fluid drainage process, stop draining and inject the drug again. Through this repeated performance evaluation, accuracy and reliability of over 98% were achieved.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Automated Predictive Maintenance System of Lathe Machine Cutting Tool Through Combined Vibration and Sound Pressure Sensors with PLC
conference_papers.summary: The cutting tools used in a lathe machine are constantly subjected to loads and stresses which contribute to their deformation over time. This can greatly affect the quality of the machined product as well as the lifespan of the cutting tool. To provide a solution in maintaining the desired state of a lathe machine cutting tool used in turning operation, this study presents an automation solution for the predictive maintenance of a lathe machine cutting tool that integrates vibration and sound sensors using a programmable logic controller (PLC). Data was gathered from finite element analysis simulations, namely, modal analysis, harmonic response analysis, and harmonic acoustics analysis, and were used as the basis for the ladder logic programming implemented in the PLC considered, where maximum deformation for three different lathe parameters occurs at 1450 Hz and has amplitudes of 0.096 mm, 0.176 mm, and 0.135 mm, respectively. Results showed that the frequency of 7800 Hz, which is where the maximum vibration acceleration occurs, does not correspond to the frequency where maximum deformation occurs. However, the frequency of 1500 Hz, which is where the maximum acoustic pressure occurs, approximately corresponds to the frequency where maximum deformation occurs. The automation system was simulated and proved to generate the intended outputs according to the formulated ladder logic program. Simulation results show that it can be a reliable solution in predicting the potential deformation that the lathe machine cutting tool is being subjected to.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Attention Module in YOLO-Based Object Detection Method for Autonomous Smart Wheelchair Room Navigation System
conference_papers.summary: People with visual impairment have difficulty in navigating a room based on text in room nameplate. Recognizing room nameplate in real environments with computer vision approach is challenging, because the system has to detect the room nameplate objects. Detection result can be improved by adding attention module in deep learning architecture, however model complexity also need to be observed to prevent accident caused by slow response from the system. Based on that problem, we proposed to compare the effect of Coordinate Attention (CA), Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), and Shuffle Attention (SA) on YOLOv8 model. Based on our findings, CA module shows positive result on accuracy of 99,50%, precision of 1, and f1-score of 0,997. As for CBAM has reduced accuracy to 96,15% from original YOLOv8n that has 98,52% accuracy, this may occur because the placement of the CBAM module before detection head is not suitable in the case of room name plate detection. Meanwhile, SA module has the least number of parameters and model size increase of additional 73.896 parameters and 154 KB, respectively. Our findings enrich insight in improving object detection method for autonomous smart wheelchair room navigation system.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Anomaly Detection for Industrial Control System based on Heterogeneous Spatio-Temporal GCN
conference_papers.summary: Industrial control systems (ICSs) are pivotal in facilitating human-machine interactions, yet their susceptibility to cyber threats poses significant risks. The integration of information technology exposes a plethora of vulnerabilities in control devices, enabling adversaries to exploit these vulnerabilities. ICS often involve intricate interactions among heterogeneous variables, presenting challenges to anomaly detection methodologies that overlook spatial and temporal characteristics. Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as a promising tool for anomaly detection due to their ability to capture complex structural semantics. However, applying GNNs to ICS encounters hurdles, such as constructing heterogeneous graphs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes heterogeneous spatio-temporal GNN, a novel anomaly detection model tailored for ICS. By constructing heterogeneous graphs and employing attention mechanisms, the proposed model effectively captures the spatio-temporal dependencies among variables. Experimental evaluation on the SWaT dataset demonstrates the superiority of the approach over baseline methods, underscoring its efficacy in safeguarding ICSs.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Enabling Value Creation in Business
conference_papers.summary: Purpose-The future of business lies in adopting artificial intelligence (AI) across organisations. While companies have been attempting to integrate AI into their operations, it is often done in a fragmented manner, with organisational leaders seldom perceiving its value due to inadequate integration within and across the business [13]. Although AI is viewed as a technological edge in business, organisations have struggled to quantify its impact on value creation (VC) and business outcomes, leading to premature terminations of implementations at nascent or pilot stages. The purpose of this study was to build a conceptual framework for creating an AI adoption strategy that enables value creation (VC) in business Design/Methodology/Approach: The approach involves a comprehensive literature review developing a conceptual framework for value creation enabled by an integrated AI adoption strategy. Findings- A framework developed for value creation enabled by AI adoption. The framework provides insights on the relationship between the enablers emanating from adoption of AI and value creation. Research limitations/implications- The conceptual insights and comprehensive framework of value creation enabled by AI adoption in business, will contribute to researchers and academicians to further test the concepts, framework, methodology used in the research. We conducted this research through qualitative literature reviews. It is essential to validate these findings through quantitative studies and primary research Practical Implications- Managers can leverage the conceptual framework as a guide to explore elements for value creation enabled by AI adoption and make informed decisions regarding investments in key AI adoption priorities like proactively working on integrating AI strategy with other functions, plan for organization transformation and organization culture early in the adoption process to create a competitive advantage, evaluate the competency in the ecosystem for AI capability building, evaluate opportunities in the organization where AI can create value in the business model, and deciding to create an organization with principles of ambidexterity. Originality/value- While many studies have discussed AI adoption, our framework of value creation that incorporates multiple dimensions, encompassing both functional and behavioral enablers of AI adoption makes this study significant and will go a long way benefiting researchers, academicians and practicing managers.
institutions: S P Jain School of Global Management

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: AI - Driven CBR and Ontological Integration Framework for Enhancing Breast Cancer Care: Case Study
conference_papers.summary: Breast cancer remains a significant health challenge, particularly in resource-limited settings such as the Gaza Strip. This study introduces a Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) framework, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach with broad applicability to building intelligent systems in health sciences domains, designed to enhance BC's diagnostic and treatment capabilities by leveraging historical patient data and clinical expertise. CBR is a reasoning paradigm that relies on specific knowledge from previously solved instances of problems rather than on general rules or models. The proposed framework integrates ontological modeling and semantic similarity measures to improve case retrieval and adaptation processes. This approach supports the formalization of reasoning procedures for collaborative medical acts, particularly in determining the best treatment for diseases and identifying best practices. It not only aids in medical decision-making but also fosters significant collaborations and ensures traceability, which are crucial for the proper deployment of medical applications. Effective information management mechanisms with traceable reasoning are also vital in the fields of epidemiology and public health. The study utilized datasets from 205 medical records collected from A1-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City to evaluate the system's performance. The proposed system comprises an Ontology and several modules for querying, reasoning, diagnosing and recommending treatments. The system achieved an 86% accuracy rate in diagnosing breast cancer and a 75% accuracy rate in recommending treatments. The treatment recommendations were validated by comparing the system's suggestions with those provided by expert oncologists and actual treatments administered to patients.
institutions: University Malaysia of Computer Science and Engineering

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Swarm Optimization Method for Gas Plume Boundary Detection and Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Detecting the boundary of gas plumes is critical for environmental monitoring, disaster response, and industrial safety. Traditional fixed-sensor networks struggle to cover large areas efficiently, while autonomous drone swarms using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) show a scalable and flexible solution. Inspired by natural creatures, such as bees, that detect environmental boundaries using collective intelligence, we explore a multi-drone technique inspired by PSO to track and detect the dynamic boundaries of gas plumes in complex environments. We explored how plume detection is influenced by several factors: wind direction, the number of particles, and wind speed. The results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in accurately detecting the plume boundary.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Model Fusion of 1D CNN with NARX for Accurate Earthquake Time Series Prediction
conference_papers.summary: we proposed a fusion model for one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) with nonlinear autoregressive with exogenous inputs (NARX) that offers a potential method to improve the accuracy of predictions. The objective of this project is to create and assess a fusion 1D-CNN-NARX model for precise forecasting of earthquake time series. The data set consists of seismic records from West Java, Central Java, and East Java. The results indicate that the fusion 1D-CNN-NARX model achieves a high level of accuracy in predicting future outcomes, especially for short-term forecasts. The mean squared error (MSE) values for West Java, Central Java, and East Java are 9.3590e-06, 7.2549e-06, and 2.6432e-05, respectively. The results show that model is effective for short-term earthquake prediction in all regions, with accuracies generally exceeding 95% for the first three months. This study emphasizes the possibility of integrating 1D-CNN and NARX architectures to enhance earthquake prediction approaches, providing a reliable and precise tool for forecasting seismic activity and early warning systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Concatenation-Based Convolutional Network
conference_papers.summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel in image recognition and object detection but face challenges like the vanishing gradient problem in deeper networks. ResNets address this with skip connections, while ConcatNet introduces a novel approach inspired by DenseNets, connecting each layer to all subsequent layers via concatenation. This design enhances information flow, learning efficiency, and feature reuse. ConcatNet outperforms in object recognition, achieves high accuracy with minimal data augmentation, and excels in semantic segmentation. It optimizes memory usage and shows shorter training times per epoch, with full potential realized over longer training periods. ConcatNet's innovative architecture boosts performance in traditional tasks and opens new possibilities for computer vision applications. Future research may explore hybrid models combining ConcatNet's dense connectivity with ResNet's skip connections for improved training efficiency and robustness.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Comprehensive Review on Generative Models for Speech Enhancement
conference_papers.summary: This review paper provides an exhaustive analysis of the current state of generative models used for speech enhancement, with a focus on Autoencoders, Diffusion models, and Generative Adver- sarial Networks (GANs). Particular emphasis is placed on understanding their principles, architecture, and applicability to speech enhancement. Furthermore, we delve into the advantages and limitations of these models, highlighting methodological progression, and recent trends. The study also emphasizes the significance of Public Perception of Current Speech Enhancement Methods and discusses potential future directions and challenges in the field - exploring strategies for improving generalization, robustness, and the incorporation of multi-modal information. The conclusion summarizes the key findings of the collected literature, suggesting potential applications and impacts of the discussed generative models for speech enhancement.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: A Collaborative Multi-Autonomous-Vehicle System for Persistent Area Monitoring Under Communication Constraints
conference_papers.summary: Persistent area monitoring (PAM) systems utilise multiple autonomous vehicles (AVs) to surveil or sample environmental data from an area that cannot be fully covered by a limited amount of stationary sensors. An optimal PAM solution should coordinate AVs to visit any location in the area as frequently as possible while factoring in AVs' constraints and environmental dynamics. In recent years, model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approaches have been widely adopted due to their advantage of not requiring an accurate model of the environment and detailed specification of the AVs. However, a key challenge remains, as MARL-based multi-AV systems usually assume ideal AVs' communication conditions with no message loss or message corruption. This paper introduces a MARL-based multi-AV architecture that coordinates AVs for PAM problems that factors in their communication constraints. We propose a deep neural network architecture that provides accurate environment state estimation for the AVs' control policy based on potentially corrupted AVs' information due to communication errors. We validate the PAM performance of our approach in a simulation environment with different numbers of AVs on different maps and different AVs' communication conditions. The results show our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art MARL-based PAM solutions for AVs with communication constraints.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Velodyne LiDAR-Guided Safe Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Navigation Quality
conference_papers.summary: A goal of safe reinforcement learning is to minimize reward while respecting safety constraints, but achieving that balance remains a challenge. Popular approaches often lead to overly cautious policies that produce suboptimal results in different environments. This paper explores the potential of dual-delay deterministic policy gradients and proximal policy optimization combined with Velodyne VLP-16 LIDAR data to process the data in specific autonomous environment. The surroundings are searched for points of interest (POI) for potential navigation directions, and an ideal waypoint is chosen depending on the data at hand. We deliver comprehensions into improving the performance of Safe RL by enhance perception of receiving data with LiDAR, allowing us to analyze its ability to navigate in dynamic environments while maintaining safety and efficiency using safe reinforcement learning algorithms

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Trash Detection in Water Bodies Using Yolo With Explainable AI Insight
conference_papers.summary: Waste disposal into water bodies is a serious concern for environmental engineers, often resulting in urban flooding, soil degradation in agricultural areas, and freshwater pollution. Additionally, trash accumulation in water bodies threatens ma-rine life by introducing contaminants through storm drains, rivers, and other channels. Furthermore, the unique character-istics of underwater environments, including high noise levels, low visibility, and color variation, pose challenges for trash detection. Thus, addressing this issue is crucial for environmental sustainability. The work focuses on both floating and submerged trash in water bodies. Typically, the detection of trash on water bodies is impacted by environmental variability, diverse appearance, and background clutter. These conditions also make usual object detection techniques less effective. Deep learning methods have shown promise in handling challenging visual tasks, therefore researchers have turned to them to get over these challenges. In this work, we focus on applying different versions of YOLO to the problem of water trash detection. To assess these models' performance, we use four different datasets: Trash Flow rate Dataset, DeepTrash, FloW, and TrashICRA. Each dataset represents various trash types under different conditions such as underwater trash and floating trash. Our study attempts to identify the best method suitable for the detection of aquatic waste. Our results highlight the effectiveness of YOLO variants in identifying the presence of trash in water ecosystems. By leveraging Grad-CAM we gain insights into the interpretability and transparency of deep learning models thus enabling Explainable AI. This approach will also contribute to the understanding and trustworthiness of artificial systems deployed for trash detection applications by providing a transparent view of decision making process of deep learning models.
institutions: University of Engineering and Technology Taxila

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Time Series Forecasting of KSE-100 Index Using a Hybrid ESN-LSTM Model
conference_papers.summary: The volatility and complexity of stock markets, particularly in emerging economies like Pakistan, pose significant challenges for accurate forecasting. This paper aims to improve the predictive accuracy of the Karachi Stock Exchange index (KSE-100) by comparing and combining advanced deep learning models. The research investigates the effectiveness of Echo State Networks (ESN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a hybrid ESN-LSTM model in capturing both short-term fluctuations and long-term trends. Daily KSE-100 index prices from September 1, 2019, to September 1, 2024, were used, with scaled closing price, 50- and 200-day moving averages as input features. The models' performances were evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R-squared and Directional Accuracy (DA). Results indicate that the ESN-LSTM hybrid model outperformed both individual ESN and LSTM models, achieving the lowest MAE of 513.10 and RMSE of 650.59, along with the highest R-squared of 0.975 and DA of 94.12%. The superior performance of the hybrid model is attributed to its ability to use the efficient temporal feature extraction of ESNs and the long-term memory capabilities of LSTMs. These findings suggest that hybrid approaches can significantly improve stock market forecasting accuracy in emerging markets. Future research should explore the integration of sentiment analysis and macroeconomic indicators to further enhance predictive capabilities.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: TezNet: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Optical Coherence Tomography Classification
conference_papers.summary: Retinal diseases such as Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV), Drusen, and Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) can severely impair vision and are challenging to reverse if detected late. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) serves as a non-invasive imaging modality to diagnose these conditions through cross-sectional retinal images. Current advancements in retinal disease detection predominantly focus on fine-tuning larger models to achieve high accuracy, often at the expense of substantial training time and data requirements. We introduce an innovative Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) named TezNet that is deeper and wider than existing custom CNNs for the dataset used in this research yet maintains a lightweight architecture with only 3.6 million parameters. This high efficiency is accomplished by leveraging depthwise and spatial separable convolutional techniques without employing preprocessing techniques or noise reduction filters. The data augmentation techniques generate diverse image qualities, ensuring robust predictions across various scenarios. By training exclusively on a single dataset, our model achieves rapid training times and optimal resource utilization, minimizing the risk of overfitting. This blend of advanced parameter optimization, minimal preprocessing, and strategic data augmentation underscores the potential of our CNN model for swift, precise, and resource-efficient retinal disease detection. TezNet model achieves a remarkable 96% accuracy, competing closely with state-of-the-art networks like ResNet50 (over 23M parameters), InceptionV3 (over 25M parameters), and ResNeXt (89M parameters).

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Smart Muscle Guardian: A Wearable Device for Real-Time Monitoring of Muscle Fatigue
conference_papers.summary: In this paper, a wearable gadget is developed that can assess muscle tiredness in real-time by using an Electromyography (EMG) sensor. It is designed to detect muscle fatigue levels accurately, ensuring safety by alerting users to potential risks during intense physical activities. The Arduino UNO Microcontroller board is used to collect data from the muscle using an EMG sensor and to sound an alarm when muscle activity surpasses a pre-set threshold. The project aims to provide a practical solution for early intervention in emergencies and ongoing monitoring of muscle functionality. An implementation of the proposed device has potential application in improving individual health and reducing the risk of injuries.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Slam Based Robot Find Target EV to Plugin in Complex Environment
conference_papers.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging in complex environments presents significant challenges, precise and adaptable interaction between robotic systems and vehicle charging plugs. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) integrated with a robotic arm to facilitate autonomous charging. Methodology used SLAM techniques to enable the robot to accurately perceive and navigate dynamic and cluttered environments. The robotic arm, equipped with sensors and actuators, is guided by this precise environmental mapping to engage charging ports on a diverse range of vehicle models without human intervention. Implementation of the robotic system, including the integration of a vision-based kick algorithm that ensures robustness and adaptability in real-time obstacle detection and navigation. 3D simulations scenarios and robot to vehicle(R2V), robot 2 robot(R2R),robot to everything(R2X) communication demonstrating significant improvements in operational efficiency and adaptability compared to traditional charging solutions. Robot, IOT and EV charging applications increase autonomy and efficiency in electric vehicle infrastructure, high level of safety, economically benefits and monitoring techniques.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Robust State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using a Nonlinearity-Aware PID Observer
conference_papers.summary: An accurate estimation of state of charge (SOC) is crucial for the safe and reliable operation of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the complex and intermittent nature of LIBs against dynamic operating conditions makes this task highly challenging. Therefore, a novel nonlinearity-aware PID observer is proposed to ensure enhanced robustness and improved accuracy in dynamic scenarios. The proposed observer is designed using a second-order equivalent circuit model (ECM) whose observability is rigorously discussed. A strategy to detect nonlinearity is integrated with the proposed design to adapt to the most suitable mechanism in highly dynamic situations. An experimental testbench, using an INR21700 cell whose parameters are identified experimentally, is constructed to verify the practicability of the proposed design. Furthermore, comparative results against highly dynamic loadfiles underscore improved accuracy, enhanced robustness, and faster convergence, demonstrating the proposed design's effectiveness in practical scenarios.
institutions: National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Robust Sliding Mode Control of a Quadrotor With Disturbance Rejection for Enhanced Stability and Performance
conference_papers.summary: This research presents a comprehensive analysis of quadrotor stabilization and trajectory tracking control using Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) with integrated disturbance rejection. The nonlinear dynamics of the quadrotor are formulated using the Newton-Euler approach, accounting for six degrees of freedom. The PID controller is implemented as a baseline, while the SMC is designed for enhanced robustness to model uncertainties and external perturbations, with a disturbance observer for managing time-varying disturbances. A rigorous Lyapunov stability proof ensures global asymptotic stability of the SMC-controlled system. Extensive simulations evaluate both controllers in terms of tracking accuracy, control effort, and robustness to external disturbances. Results show that SMC outperforms PID in dis-turbance rejection, tracking accuracy, and robustness, making it ideal for UAV applications in complex environments.
institutions: National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Pushing and Rotating a Heavy Mass Rigid Body Using an Omnidirectional Aerial Manipulator
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the pushing and rotation of a heavy rigid body using an omnidirectional actively tilted aerial manipulator, controlled via a hybrid force/position controller. Unlike conventional unmanned aerial vehicles, the proposed system enables precise horizontal force application, making it ideal for aerial physical interaction tasks. The hybrid controller is implemented in the Robot Operating System and validated through extensive simulations in a Gazebo physics-engine-based environment. The manipulator's performance was evaluated in two scenarios: circular trajectory tracking and the rotation of a heavy rigid mass. Results demonstrated its capability to follow complex trajectories with high accuracy and exert sustained forces for object manipulation. The system exhibited excellent stability and precision, underscoring its potential for real-world applications in challenging environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
conference_papers.summary: An accurate estimation of battery state of charge (SOC) is crucial to ensure the safety of Li-ion batteries (LIBs), and the recent boom in machine learning (ML) has illustrated a strong potential for SOC estimation. However, the ignorance of LIB internal dynamics greatly limits the performance of ML-based methods. Therefore, this work incorporates multiple battery internal dynamics into the ML-based method to ensure enhanced performance. First, using a simple mechanism based on the LIB model, the open circuit voltage, ohmic response, and temperature-corrected pattern are extracted from the measured data and provided as inputs to the neural networks (NNs). Then, to ensure time adaptability and accuracy, the predictions of the proposed design are adjusted using short-term Ampere-hour results. The proposed technique is validated using different real-world driving profiles. The comparative results with benchmark NNs-based methods verify a >60% reduction in root mean square error, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating battery internal dynamics into NNs.

conference_papers.title: Optimizing Wind Speed Estimation with Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks: A Case Study of Pakistan
conference_papers.summary: Wind energy has emerged as a key player in sustainable power generation. Accurate prediction of wind speed is critical for optimizing wind farm operations, energy output forecasting, and reducing dependency on traditional power sources. In this study, we propose a Least-Squares Generative Adversarial Network (LSGAN) for wind speed prediction in a specific region of Pakistan, utilizing data from Tandoghulamali, which includes features like wind speeds at various altitudes and wind direction. The model is designed to predict wind speed at 80 meters, a crucial target variable for wind turbine operations. The LSGAN model effectively leverages adversarial training, achieving high accuracy with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.54 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.77. Through a detailed comparison of actual versus predicted values, the model demonstrates its ability to generalize well across unseen data, with stable performance during the adversarial learning process. This approach opens up new possibilities for applying advanced machine learning techniques in renewable energy forecasting, particularly in regions with sparse historical data.
