conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Analysis of Posture Influence on Memory Using fNIRS-BCI
conference_papers.summary: This study explores the impact of three varied body postures-sitting, standing, and upper-body movement on human memory using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) based brain- computer interface (BCI). The study involves two distinct cognitive activities i.e., the mental arithmetic and picture recall activity. The fNIRS brain signals from 10 healthy subjects (5 male and 5 female) were recorded, and pre-processed. After extracting features, supervised learning was used for classification to analyze how altering body postures affects the memory The Gaussian Naïve Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) classifiers were applied. For the Mental Arithmetic Activity, sitting posture emerged as the optimal posture, demonstrating the maximum achieved accuracy of 84.2%. Conversely, for the Picture Recall Activity, the upper-body movement emerged as the optimal posture, achieving the maximum accuracy of 87.4%. Through comprehensive analysis, this research contributes insights into the intricate relationship between body postures and cognitive functions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Analysis of Motor Imagery-Based fNIRS-BCI for Knee Flexion and Extension
conference_papers.summary: This study aimed to explore the potential of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) as a non-invasive technique for detecting hemodynamic responses in cortical brain activities during motor imagery (MI) tasks. Specifically, the study focused on classifying multiclass MI tasks with fNIRS data. A total of 10 healthy individuals participated in the experiment, where they were instructed to perform motor imagery tasks. A multi-channel continuous wave fNIRS system records the signals from the motor cortex for knee flexion and extension imagery tasks. Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), comparatively computationally efficient, algorithms were used to classify the data for fNIRS-based BCI applications. The SVM classifier performed comparatively better than the LDA classifier in accuracy, with 88.8% and 89.4% for two-feature and three-feature combinations. Brain activation maps show the increased activation for flexion movement of the knee. Future research should focus on refining the classification process through feature selection, preprocessing improvements, and ensemble methods to enhance accuracy.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: Advancement in Smart Cane Technology: Enhancing Mobility for the Visually Impaired Using ROS and LiDAR
conference_papers.summary: Visual impairment affects the ability to navigate independently in an unknown environment due to reliance on human/dog assistance, potential miscommunication, and discomfort during mobility. To make the visually impaired (VI) individuals self-reliant and confident in their mobility the proposed system has been developed that contains a light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensor for obstacle detection and two omni-wheels coupled with the DC gear encoder motors for precise movement in any direction without lifting the cane. Hector Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), A *, and steering wheel algorithms have been implemented in the robot operating system (ROS) for real-time environment mapping, efficient path planning, and navigating in an unknown indoor static environment, respectively. The Raspberry Pi 3B+ and Arduino Mega 2560 are used in the master-slave configuration for decision-making on path planning and controlling the maneuverability of the system in real-time. The proposed system in the paper is successfully tested on one subject in two indoor environments. The results demonstrate that the system serves as an assistive mobile robot, helping the VI individual to navigate confidently in an unknown environment and reach the destination without assistance.
institutions: University of Engineering and Technology Lahore

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: AI-Based Early Detection of Coronary Artery Disease Using Atherosclerosis Inflammatory and MicroRNA Biomarkers in Angina Patients
conference_papers.summary: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is one of the most common causes of sudden cardiac arrest and is responsible for a high percentage of global mortality. Early diagnosis of CAD in patients with chest pain is challenging. Coronary angiography, an invasive procedure that is not widely available in developing countries, confirms the diagnosis of CAD. It is imperative to establish noninvasive biomarkers for the early diagnosis of CAD in patients with angina. Motivated by two recent medical diagnostic studies that used novel molecular (microRNA) and chemical (atherosclerosis-inflammatory) biomarkers for early detection of CAD, the proposed study explores the hidden potential of novel biomarkers using machine learning (ML). The study combines the biomarkers of two medical studies and presents a NUMS-NIHD dataset. From the complete dataset, the best feature set is shortlisted after an extensive evaluative search in the biomarker feature space. Ten ML classifiers are applied to the selected biomarker inputs, including clinical, chemical, and molecular cardiac biomarkers. To select optimal biomarker-classifier combinations, experiments use K-fold cross-validation. The results of K-fold cross-validation are validated against a hold-out set of data. The results are then compared to current state-of-the-art benchmark studies. The detection strategy achieved an accuracy of 90.18%, a sensitivity of 92.33 % and a specificity of 100.00%. The proposed study validated previous medical diagnostic studies and significantly improved the results. These ML biomarkers-classifier combinations can be used to exclude healthy individuals non-invasively before angiography.
institutions: National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: A Soft Robotics Approach to Prosthetic Hands: Integrating 3D Printing Techniques and Embedded Vision
conference_papers.summary: The development of soft robotics hand has progressed significantly, evolving from a pneumatically actuated solution for industrial applications to a lightweight and easy-to-manufacture solution for 3d printed prosthetic hands. However, existing soft prosthetic hands often lack anthropomorphic appearances, intrinsic structural integrity, and sufficient feedback to the amputees, leading to a high rate of abandonment of prosthetic hands. This paper presents a design of a 3d printed soft robotic hand based on a monolithic design with an embedded camera and anthropomorphic appearance. The hand is fabricated using the flexible 3d printable material TPU-95 with an embedded Raspberry Pie Cam module for increased functionality. The hand utilizes a cable-driven mechanism integrated with five rotary actuators capable of multiple grasp patterns. Our design weighs around 246 grams with all the electronic components embedded inside the hand. This paper discusses the mechanical design, 3d printing methodology for the fabrication of the fingers, actuation mechanisms, and the results of the soft prosthetic hand's performance.
institutions: National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: A Parametric and Generative Based Panels Design Optimization for Mass Timber Panel Manufacturing
conference_papers.summary: With the development of Construction 4.0 and digital technologies, off-site construction has evolved and become a practical choice for rapid construction. In today's fast-paced manufacturing framework, there is a need to automate every construction step, especially the design and analysis phases of mass timber panel manufacturing, as these two steps are highly expert's dependent. This study summarizes a case to design multiple variants of mass timber panels using parametric and generative modeling. Integrating these technologies helps create speedy and tailored design solutions in the automation setting. A building information modeling (BIM) based on a 3D parametric design of a timber panel is generated, followed by optimizations via generative design. Focusing on the Canadian construction industry, different types of mass timber are examined to analyze and optimize design features such as stud width, stud bays, and weight-bearing capacity. This study aims to support customization and adaptability at the yield of less time and effort for ongoing industrial automation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: A Multi-Sensor Approach for Thermal Environment Monitoring in Public Transport
conference_papers.summary: Globally it is found that many vehicles do not have built-in intelligent monitoring systems which is very much dangerous especially when the temperature of the indoor environment is rising. This research fulfills the need by designing a thermal indoor environment monitoring device that increases the safety and intelligence of vehicles. The device collects and records a number of environmentally significant parameters like temperature, pressure, both indoor and outdoor humidity, light intensity, TVOC, CO2 levels, and GPS position. Large amounts of data were collected from different cars, buses and trains for both local city and inter-city environments. These datasets helped in the deployment of intelligent monitoring and management techniques which helped with the intervention. The outcomes of our experiments show that it is possible to enhance the safety and comfort of car passengers with the help of innovative solutions, for instance, pre-staging air conditioning when the temperature starts to rise. This research benefits the smart vehicle development field and provides a strong solution to Pakistan's environmental monitoring issues in the transportation industry.
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: A Lightweight CNN for RGB-D Grasp Classification in Computer Vision-Based Prosthetic Hands
conference_papers.summary: Prosthetic hand development has progressed significantly from basic mechanical designs to advanced systems that incorporate computer vision for enhanced functionality. However, the challenge now is creating a lightweight, accurate and computationally efficient model suitable for integrating embedded microcontrollers in prosthetic devices. This paper presents a novel framework based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with just 160,000 trainable parameters and a size of under 1MB, making it viable for deployment in microcontrollers like Arduino, ESP, and Raspberry Pi. The framework has a comprehensive input of 32x32x3 which incorporates grey-scaled RGB, depth, and masked data. The presented model is tested on a newly structured RGB-D dataset containing 51 objects across 7 grasp types, achieving 99% accuracy with minimal computational resources.
institutions: National University of Sciences and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
conference_papers.title: A Cryptography-Based Framework for Securing Medical Imaging Data in Robotic Systems
conference_papers.summary: Medical imaging data is crucial in robotics-assisted diagnostics and interventions, particularly in neurology. Ensuring the security and privacy of this sensitive data is increasingly challenging in the context of robotic systems. This study presents a robust framework to secure MRI brain images using the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm, tailored for use in robotics applications. The AES algorithm is chosen for its high level of data confidentiality and integrity, making it well-suited for protecting sensitive medical information in robotic systems. Encrypted MRI images are decrypted and then processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN), specifically AlexNet, integrated into the robotic platform to classify the images as either tumorous or healthy. The classification performance is thoroughly evaluated using confusion matrices and performance plots, assessing the accuracy of the system. The project is implemented using Python, and the results demonstrate significant improvements over recent advancements in this field. This study not only enhances the security of medical imaging data within robotics applications but also contributes to improving the precision and reliability of robotic diagnostic systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Wave-Bottleneck: an Enhanced Architecture for Decreasing Parameters in Deep Network Models
conference_papers.summary: The field of computer vision has seen remarkable advancements with deep neural networks, particularly the ResNet architecture, which effectively reduces the number of parameters and addresses the vanishing gradient problem through its Bottleneck block design and skip connections. In this study, we strive to further reduce network parameters while safeguarding model precision by introducing the Wave Bottleneck. This groundbreaking integration seamlessly merges the Bottleneck block with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). Wave Bottleneck leverages DWT for feature decomposition and reconstruction, combining 1D and 2D DWT to enhance computational efficiency. Our method performs feature extraction on the input data in the channel domain to efficiently and effectively capture the correlation and important features between channels. Moreover, we realize important feature extraction in the spatial domain by performing feature extraction. Extensive experiments on standard datasets show that Wave Bottleneck outperforms traditional ResNet models in terms of accuracy and parameter reduction, showcasing its potential for deployment in resource-constrained environments.
institutions: Baoji University of Arts and Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Two-Stage Optimization Model for Parcel Replenishment Delivery Based on Mobile Lockers
conference_papers.summary: This study addresses the replenishment delivery of packages received at the warehouse during the mobile lockers delivery process by establishing a two-stage optimization model. The first stage plans the delivery of parcels that arrived at the warehouse the previous day, while the second stage focuses on supply vehicles replenishing parcels that arrive during the delivery period. And the large neighborhood search algorithm is developed to solve the problem, and its accuracy and effectiveness are validated through numerical experiments. The results indicate that incorporating replenishment delivery significantly enhances customers' requirement for timeliness, with 400% to 600% of parcels successfully replenished on average. Additionally, replenishment contributes to substantial cost savings, reduces the travel distances of mobile locker, and decreases carbon emissions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Track Prediction Method of Unmanned Platform Based on Reinforcement Learning and Improved Potential Field Method
conference_papers.summary: In the modern battlefield environment, unmanned platforms and unmanned clusters are playing an increasingly important role, and the analysis and prediction of unmanned platform behavior and command and control have become a hot research topic. In this paper, the track parameters of the unmanned platform in a continuous time period are used as sample data, and the historical track of the unmanned platform is fitted by the function fitting method. Based on the static obstacle information and dynamic obstacle information in the application scene, the corresponding repulsion field is constructed. Based on the empirical playback training network model, the trained network model is finally used to predict the track of the unmanned platform in the future. Simulation experiments show that this method can significantly improve the training efficiency of the unmanned platform track prediction model and the accuracy of the prediction results.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Tool or Partner: Mental-Aware Human-Robot Collaboration
conference_papers.summary: Human-robot collaboration is a critical area of research, aiming to maximize synergy between humans and robots. However, a fundamental question persists: Should robots be seen as mere tools or genuine partners? Existing experimental environments have limitations in supporting virtual human-robot collaboration studies. In this paper, we propose a novel robot training framework designed for mental-aware human-robot collaboration. Within this framework, we introduce a Trust-Aware Mental Model incorporating a Human Trust component to represent human trust in robots. We create a virtual simulation environment to evaluate this model and conduct human-robot collaboration experiments. Quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate that integrating the trust-aware mental model enhances collaboration effectiveness. This finding underscores the necessity of viewing robots as true human partners and provides valuable insights for future research in human-robot collaboration.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: The PCA Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Causal Relationships
conference_papers.summary: Fault diagnosis is a critical and central issue in industrial engineering, essential for addressing problems encountered in engineering systems. In recent years, data-driven fault diagnosis methods have gained extensive attention and application. Traditional fault diagnosis techniques primarily focus on analyzing data from individual fault nodes, making it challenging to capture the causal relationships between fault nodes accurately. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on the combination of principal component analysis (PCA) and Liang-Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF). This method quantifies causal interactions between nodes by introducing information flow, thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, we conducted simulation experiments using the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) as a testbed. Specifically, we analyzed two faults in the TE platform and designed comparative experiments by varying two input variables. The results demonstrate that the LKIF-PCA fault diagnosis method achieves high accuracy, indicating its potential for practical applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: The Design and Implementation of a Control Computer Based-on FPGA Core
conference_papers.summary: According to the requirement of the system operation, a control computer monitors and controls a large number of key nodes, synthesizes a variety of excitation signals, obtains the angular state of the rotating mechanism, controls its rotation to the specified position. Based on an FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) core, this paper develops a signal synthesizing module, a digital axis-angle conversion module and a W5500 Ethernet interface using a SOPC system that can be tailored and configured flexibly. It integrates the customed logic IPs into the SOPC (System-on-a-Programmable Chip) system of the Nios II architecture. The software system coordinates the operation of all modules. Finally, the control computer synthetically implements all its functions.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Text Input Through Swipe Gestures Based Personalized AI Agent
conference_papers.summary: Text input based on virtual reality is a common technique in interactive systems, but it may face challenges related to input efficiency and task load when interacting with VR hardware and applications. The development of artificial intelligence interaction technologies offers new approaches to addressing text input challenges. In this paper, we propose a swipe gesture-based text input method under a personalized AI agent framework, combining portable devices (e.g. smartphones) with VR input and incorporating user profile information, input habits, and conversational intent. By integrating the GPT-3.5 model to train a personalized AI agent, we emphasize the importance of understanding and responding to human behavior or capabilities from the agent's perspective, enabling text prediction based on specific contexts. The keyboard layout design is based on a disk divided into 8 equal regions, where the outer circle is subdivided into key areas containing letters, and the inner circle serves as the input buffer area. By resolving word ambiguities based on user input and leveraging the extensive capabilities of large language models in context awareness and text prediction, the system allows complete sentences to be generated from keywords. This reduces the number of manual inputs required by the user, improving text input efficiency and enhancing the overall user experience.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Teleoperated Mobile Robotic Manipulator for Rescue Scenarios
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces a teleoperated mobile robotic manipulator specifically designed for rescue operations. The system integrates a robotic manipulator, a mobile platform, a hybrid power system, an environmental perception system, and a teleoperation console, forming a modular and highly adaptable architecture. A key innovation is the Feedback Correction Loop, which improves manipulator control by mitigating issues like communication delays, workspace constraints, and packet loss. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the framework, demonstrating that the system can execute tasks smoothly, continuously, and safely under teleoperation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Study on Point Cloud Processing Technology in Robotic Welding for Ship Sub-Assembly
conference_papers.summary: To address the issue of insufficient automation in robotic welding for ship small assemblies, this study develops a welding technology based on point cloud processing. The research utilizes vision sensors to collect point cloud data of workpieces, and an improved point cloud processing algorithm is employed to extract weld seam information effectively. A novel real-time online calibration method for vision sensors is introduced, which precisely transforms the weld seam position from the vision sensor coordinate system to the robot coordinate system, thereby ensuring accuracy and continuity in the robotic welding process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technology significantly enhances automation and weld quality in ship small assemblies, showing substantial industrial application potential.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Students' Attitudes Towards the AI-Based Automated Essay Scoring System: An Influencing Mechanism from Perceived Interactivity to Criticism
conference_papers.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has penetrated our lives by way of web search engines and mobile applications. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) is playing an increasingly important role in the field of education. This study explored the relationship between students' perceived interactivity of AES and their individual innovativeness as well as their reflective thinking about AES, and how these variables influence their criticism of AES. This study employed Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for the data analysis. Valid data were collected from 442 students (40.05% male, 59.95% female, average age= 19.7) who had experience of AVE in private universities in China. The findings showed that: (a) Students' perceived interactivity of AES positively affected their individual innovativeness and reflective thinking about AES; (b) Students' individual innovativeness of AES positively affected their reflective thinking and criticism of AES; and (c) Students' perceived interactivity and reflective thinking about AES did not positively affect their criticism of AES. The findings not only revealed students' attitudes towards and experiences of this technological tool, but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.
institutions: Guangzhou Institute of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Space Launch Group Planning Technique for Manned Space Station Construction
conference_papers.summary: The launch mission for manned space station construction is characterized by strong constraints of spacecraft orbit and launch site, as well as tight coupling between multiple launch missions. It is a huge challenge for space launch planning to meet the overall requirements of engineering for reliability, safety, and efficiency. The space launch group planning technique is proposed based on the constraints of space rendezvous and docking and the coupling relationship between space launches using different types of launch vehicles, within the background of manned space station construction. The objective is to design space launch programs that meet the requirements of reliability, safety and efficiency within the specified timeframe. First and foremost, the four-dimensional space launch group-planning diagram is designed using isochrones, referring to the in-orbit space station, two launch sites, and the aerospace manufacturing plants. In the second place, a reliability evaluation function based on reliability growth, launch opportunity increase and launch window lengthening is proposed. Additionally, a safety evaluation function based on emergency rescue launch, and a benefit function based on parallel operation of multiple launch sites is introduced. Finally, the feasibility of the technology proposed is verified taken the construction of Tiangong space station as an example. The result indicates that the launch mission group planning designed using the technology proposed is highly consistent with the engineering practice results.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: SE(3) Pose Estimation for Simultaneous Localization of Objects and Sensors in Dynamic Environments
conference_papers.summary: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology offers considerable advantages for enhancing cognitive abilities for mobile robots, especially under complex, dynamic environments. The creation of robust computer vision methods is essential to optimize the understanding of rigid object motion while ensuring precise localization of sensors or cameras. In this study, we introduce a tightly-integrated SLAM approach (MOT), designed to accurately capture SE (3) pose data for sensors/cameras and motion details of objects in the environment. The method initiates by building a streamlined EKF-tracker to determine and associate the real-time motion states of objects. Then, features are separated into static background and object-specific categories based on both instance mask and state information. Static features facilitate the initialization of camera poses, while dynamic features provide SE(3) pose data for objects under observation. Finally, we introduce a novel graph optimization technique to co-optimize the static 3D landmarks, object landmarks, camera poses, and moving object poses within the scene. The proposed approach has shown effectiveness on the KITTI and OMD datasets.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Robot Teleoperation via Virtual Reality: A Unity and ROS Approach
conference_papers.summary: This paper explores the integration of virtual reality (VR) with teleoperation systems to enhance human-robot interaction. With the rise of remote operations, traditional methods often rely on two-dimensional interfaces, making it challenging to control robots in complex three-dimensional environments. This research presents a VR teleoperation system using the Meta Quest 2 headset, enabling immersive control of a climbing robot with six degrees-of-freedom and magnetic adhesion. The system architecture integrates Unity for virtual simulation and the Robot Operating System (ROS) for real-time communication and control. A virtual environment allows the user to control the virtual robot model through the VR headset and controllers, with ROS serving as the communication bridge between the virtual and physical robots, enabling effective operations in various applications, including high-risk environments (A video is available at https://youtu.be/MiZDOV4IfLA).

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on the Features of the Series Arc Fault Detection and Phase Selection Based on Singular Value Decomposition and Multi-scale Norm
conference_papers.summary: Electrical fires caused by arc fault are very common. To effectively prevent the electrical fire accidents resulted by the arc fault and reduce the troubleshooting time, a feature extraction method of the series arc fault (SAF) detection and phase selection in the three-phase motor and frequency converter load circuit was proposed. First, the SAF experiments under different lines conditions were conducted by using the three-phase motor and frequency converter loads. Second, a reconstruction of attractor track matrix was constructed, and combined it with the singular value decomposition to enhance the fault features. Third, the features of the SAF detection and phase selection were extracted from the feature enhancement matrix by using the multi-scale norm. Finally, by employing particle swarm optimization algorithm to refine a support vector machine, a detection and line selection model for the SAF was developed. According to the test results, the detection and phase selection accuracy of the SAF in the three-phase motor and the frequency converter load circuit were 98.12% and 91.63% respectively. It can serve as a point of reference for the development of the industrial arc fault circuit breakers with the SAF phase selection function.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Robustness and Denoising Based on the H-F Algorithm of the Large-aperture Optical Infrared Telescope
conference_papers.summary: In this paper, an H-F($H$∞ -Filter) control algorithm is proposed to ensure that the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) of the large-aperture optical infrared telescope drive system can operate normally under the condition of high switching noise and extreme large wind-borne disturbances in the control system. The H-F algorithm combines the position loop and the velocity loop controller with the filtering algorithm to form the H-F controller and optimizes the control structure of the telescope drive system to be applied to the large-aperture optical infrared telescope. The telescope drive system is a typical large-inertia, ultra-low-speed, high-precision system, and the robustness of the H-F algorithm is verified by the position tracking form in the arc second range, the influence of switching noise, and the addition of wind-borne disturbance in the experimental process. The superior performance of the H-F algorithm is verified by comparing it with the traditional triple closed-loop PID control.
institutions: Nanjing Institute of Astronomical Optics & Technology
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Multiple Failure Analysis Method for Dynamic Reconfiguration Flight Control System of BWB Aircraft
conference_papers.summary: For the multifunctional configuration of control surfaces in the flight control system of BWB aircraft, and the complex redundancy management and reconfiguration capabilities implemented in the event of failures, a multiple failure analysis method based on multiple failure state space is proposed. Taking a certain type of BWB aircraft as an example, a failure relationship matrix is defined to automate the analysis of Failure combinations under different state spaces. The results show that this method can effectively analyze the evolution process of system failure states and safety impacts across different state spaces, systematically identifying failure modes and the processes of redundancy switching and reconfiguration.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Matching Degree of Agricultural Landscape Based on UAV Space Ranging
conference_papers.summary: Agricultural landscape is a form of expression of the earth's landscape achieved through agricultural planting, usually presenting a design image of the earth with different types of plants working together. In the specific implementation process, due to spatial errors in plant planting, there are often some errors in the presentation of the final effect compared to the initial design image, which becomes an important factor affecting the appearance of the final effect. This article aims to use unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) spatial ranging technology to calculate the error values between agricultural landscape products and design patterns based on several feature points, comprehensively measure their presentation effects, and provide evaluation criteria for the planting quality of agricultural landscapes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Imaging Detection of Defects in X-ray Oil and Gas Casings Based on MIT-MTT Combined Instrument
conference_papers.summary: The paper aims to study the X-ray oil and gas casing defect imaging detection based on the MIT-MTT combination logging instrument. By reviewing and analyzing relevant domestic and international literature, the paper summarizes the principles, advantages, disadvantages, and applications of existing algorithms. The research, based on experimental data from the MIT -MTT combination logging instrument, indicates that X-ray-based defect detection algorithms, combined with the imaging of the MIT -MTT combination logging instrument, play a significant role in improving the accuracy, efficiency, and automation of oil well casing inspection. With the continuous development of deep learning and defect detection technologies, the field is expected to achieve more breakthroughs in the future.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Application of Stewart Platform in Uniform Scanning
conference_papers.summary: The space spectral imaging camera is planned to use a Stewart 6-DOF platform to drive a mirror for scanning and imaging, which requires the accuracy of the platform to reach the order of arcsec under the condition of multi-struts dynamic coupling. A Stewart platform realizes high angle resolution mainly by designing high-resolution linear driving struts. The resolution index of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, which needs the struts to achieve a high resolution of 60 nm. Based on this requirement, a driving strut with 50 nm resolution based on BLDC motor, ball screw, grating ruler is designed, which effectively ensures the high resolution of the platform. The transfer function of the single drive strut is identified by time domain method, and the closed-loop control model of the single drive strut is established. The dynamic performance of the single drive strut is simulated and analyzed. Finally, the dynamic performance of the 6-DOF scanning platform is experimentally studied. The experimental results show that the angular resolution of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, the swing angle range of the constant speed scanning is −1~1 degree, the nonlinear error of scanning angle in place curve is less than 0.2%, and the rotational speed is adjustable from 40”/s to 1800 ”/s, all the indicators meet the design index. This research has laid a solid foundation for the aerospace application of Stewart Parallel Platform.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Research on Aircraft Automatic Drilling and Riveting Task Planning and Simulation Technology Based on DELMIA
conference_papers.summary: Based on the application content, scope, and process of digital enterprise lean manufacturing interactive application (DELMIA), conduct research on aircraft automatic drilling and riveting task planning and simulation technology. Establish a process numerical model for the product, study the optimal path planning for the assembly process, achieve automatic planning of robot drilling and riveting tasks, and generate numerical control (NC) code for robot execution. Virtual simulation of robot automatic drilling and riveting tasks based on DELMIA, conducting assembly interference inspection, and achieving advance planning and simulation of production assembly tasks. Verify the effectiveness and accuracy of automatic drilling and riveting task planning and simulation methods through examples. The results indicate that the hole position error after processing is controlled within 0.3mm, which can meet the requirements of hole making.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Rapid Assembly Method of Large Volume Stone for Transportation Facilities Based on BIM
conference_papers.summary: Nowadays, in order to meet the needs of traffic facilities for landscape, stone is widely used in municipal engineering sidewalk paving. However, the phenomenon of stone cutting caused by the mismatch between the stone size and the station area often occurs in the actual project, which increases the construction cost and affects the construction efficiency, and does not meet the strategic needs of the sustainable development of today's society. Aiming at the above problems, this paper puts forward a rapid assembling method of railway yard stone based on BIM technology. By analyzing the characteristics of the blanking problem, the assembly area is regarded as the base material, the stone is regarded as the sub-material, and the stone loss of the boundary of the assembly area is considered in the actual assembly process. The four-point adaptive stone family is constructed by using Revit conceptual volumetric method, and the parametric assembly of traffic facilities stone based on BIM is realized by Dynamo visualization program editor. Finally, taking a certain area of a traffic facilities in Xi 'an City as an example, by calculating and comparing the boundary loss of the stone combination with six different sizes, the optimal stone combination is selected to carry out BIM parametric assembly. The research results show that the stone assembly method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the construction efficiency, improve the degree of engineering refinement, and reduce the construction cost.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: RELA: An Online-Offline Framework for Rules Enhanced Logs Analysis Based on Large Language Models
conference_papers.summary: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have played a pivotal role in the field of Artificial Intelligence Operations (AIOps), particularly in the analysis of log data. However, the use of open-source LLMs for automated log analysis often falls short of expectations in offline environments in practice. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative Online-Offline framework named RELA to enhance the performance of LLMs in log analysis. In the online phase of our framework, GPT-4 meticulously analyzes logs to determine the presence of anomalies and deduces rules based on these determinations, which are then compiled into a comprehensive rules base. In the offline phase, open-source LLMs leverage this rules base to significantly enhance the effectiveness of log analysis by retrieving the most applicable rules. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework, we meticulously annotated a dataset specifically designed for a distinct offline scenario, focusing on two primary tasks: the detection of log anomalies and the explanation of these anomalies. Our experimental results demonstrate that the implementation of the rules base leads to a 3% to 25.3% increase in the accuracy of anomaly detection. Additionally, assessments conducted by domain experts validate the improvements, highlighting a substantial enhancement in the credibility of the explanations provided by LLMs within this framework. These findings not only underscore the practicality but also the efficacy of our approach, establishing a solid foundation for further research and application in AIOps.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: RANS Model-based Constant Temperature Anemometry Examination to Validate Negligible Wind Tunnel Blockage Effect on Developed Multi-scale Generated Grid Turbulence
conference_papers.summary: The aim of this study is to quantitatively assess the effect of wind tunnel blockage on multi-scale generated turbulence and to analyze the results in comparison with the results of previous studies. In particular, the study focuses on the mainstream weak acceleration phenomena and their turbulence characteristics, and the effects are evaluated using acceleration parameters. The decay exponent calculated by introducing a turbulence time scale was larger than the results in the previous study for square lattice turbulence, indicating a rapidly decaying field. An evaluation of the dependence on flow velocity was also carried out, and the results obtained by varying the set flow velocity confirm that the effect of acceleration on turbulent energy, dissipation rate, length scale and time scale is independent of flow velocity. Compared to the measurement uncertainty, the effect of acceleration was small and no statistically significant differences were found. The results of this study provide important information for the quantitative assessment of the impact of weak acceleration phenomena in the main flow due to blockage effects in the wind tunnel test section on multi-scale generated turbulence.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Qasync: A Dual Network Architecture for Value Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: In this work, we propose Qasync, a novel dual network framework for value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning, aimed at addressing the control decision-making issues of Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) in merge scenario. The core contributions of Qasync include the following two aspects: 1) Qasync extends QMIX by integrating a feedforward network, which reduces the limitations of QMIX's linearity assumption. 2) Qasync introduces a periodic mixing mechanism that combines Q-values from both networks, enabling Qasync to better capture non-linear relationships and enhance agents' exploration of diverse strategies. We evaluated Qasync using the SMARTS platform in a mixed traffic merging scenario, where autonomous vehicles must merge onto a two-lane road from a slip road, interacting with vehicles that randomly generated at the starting point to simulate realistic traffic conditions. Qasync was compared against several value-based baselines, including VDN, QMIX, and QTRAN, achieving average merging success rates of 80%, 89%, and 94%, respectively. Qasync achieved an overall merging success rate of 95%, demonstrating its ability to effectively handle complex traffic interactions and highlighting its potential for enhancing autonomous driving systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Particle Swarm Algorithm Based Scheduling Method for Flexible Production Line
conference_papers.summary: The State Council in “Made in China 2025” clearly put forward to vigorously promote the integration of information technology and industrialization, to achieve technological breakthroughs in key areas in aerospace equipment. In the next decade, China's demand for aircraft will continue to increase, which requires high manufacturing efficiency and fast response speed of aircraft parts. However, in actual production, the research and application of the production line scheduling algorithm is still relatively small, which leads to the actual production cannot play out the maximum efficiency of the production line. In view of the above problems, this paper takes the actual flexible production line as the research object, establishes the scheduling model in line with the actual production on the spot, and uses the optimized particle swarm algorithm to solve the model, to obtain the optimal solution to meet the requirements of the actual scheduling, so as to give full play to the maximum efficiency of the production.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Participation in Vehicle-to-Grid Systems: Understanding the Role of Technology Awareness, Policy Incentives, and Personal Financial Gain
conference_papers.summary: This paper investigates the key factors influencing consumers' willingness to participate in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, focusing on the roles of technology awareness, policy incentives, and personal financial gain. Using data from 547 electric vehicle users, we conduct factor and regression analyses to explore how these factors individually and interactively affect customers' V2G participation. Our findings reveal that technology awareness significantly boosts consumer participation, as more informed users are likely to engage with V2G regardless of immediate financial rewards. Policy incentives also play a critical role, with clear and consistent government and organizational support enhancing participation rates. However, personal financial gain shows a more nuanced effect—while compensation is a motivator, excessively high expectations can deter users. Additionally, we identify that strong policy frameworks and increased awareness can reduce the need for high financial incentives, creating a more sustainable pathway for V2G adoption. Based on these findings, we propose policy recommendations aimed at improving consumer education, standardizing incentives, and better aligning financial rewards with realistic expectations to promote broader engagement with V2G technology.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Optimization Machining Processes in Multi-User Cyber-Physical Cells: A Comparative
conference_papers.summary: This article presents the virtual commissioning of a multi-user cyber-physical laboratory for remote access (Multicyber) integrated with Industry 4.0 technologies to promote neoindustrialization. The project incorporates Digital Twins, Virtual and Augmented Reality, Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Robotics, Vision Systems, Autonomous and Collaborative Robots, Cybersecurity, and the Industrial Internet of Things. The objective of the Multicyber project is to create a demonstration center focused on advancing applied research in manufacturing processes. The laboratory features a manufacturing cell with an Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR), a collaborative anthropomorphic manipulator (cobot), quality inspection via computer vision, a five-axis machine, and a robotic arm for machining. This study presents the simulation of three complete manufacturing routines. Plant Simulation software was used to obtain travel times for the AMR, inspection, and part removal stages, while NX software was used for detailed machining simulations with precision adjustments. The results highlight the benefits of using robotic arms in manufacturing and demonstrate how AMRs and cobots can add value through the planning and integration of routines.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: One-Handed Gesture Recognition Based on Improved ST-GCN and CA Attention Mechanism
conference_papers.summary: The article takes one-handed gesture video as the research object, and mainly focuses on the recognition process and method of “isolated words” and static gesture mixtures. Firstly, the algorithm of extracting the key point positions of frame pictures is proposed by grouping rules of frame sequences of different gestures. This algorithm solves the problem of invalid gesture images affecting the recognition due to the redundancy of gesture images when extracting gestures from traditional gesture videos. Finally, a new network (ST-GCN-CA) is proposed, which improves the traditional spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) and adds the CA attention mechanism. The method and network in this paper are applied to the Chinese isolated word sign language dataset (CSL-500) single-handed video, and the experimental results show that the recognition accuracies in the isolated word gesture video and the hybrid video reach 94.3% and 94.1%, respectively, which improves the recognition accuracies in comparison with other methods in the public domain.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Multimodal Physiological Signal for the Diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease
conference_papers.summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by a complex etiology and diverse clinical presentations. The intelligent diagnosis of this condition poses a significant challenge. Despite abnormal electrocardiogram (ECG), respiratory (RSP), and pulse signals in PD, which are closely linked to clinical symptoms, there remains a dearth of intelligent diagnostic models centered on multimodal physiological signals. In this study, we gathered multimodal physiological data from 55 PD patients and 30 healthy individuals, comprising ECG, photoplethysmogram (PPG), and RSP. Subsequently, we proposed a random forest classification model employing averaging probabilities, achieving an 89.41% accuracy in distinguishing between PD patients and healthy controls. Moreover, a feature ranking analysis was conducted on the time-domain features across the three modalities. This analysis unveiled the significance of time-domain features from diverse physiological signals in identifying PD, leading to optimization of the classification model and ultimately attaining a classification accuracy of 90.59%. In addition, the pulse and breathing characteristics in the open eyes state contribute more to disease identification, while the closed eyes state is mainly based on ECG characteristics. This research underscores the potential of machine learning techniques in amalgamating multimodal physiological data to enhance the diagnostic precision of PD, offering an objective and efficient clinical diagnostic approach.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: MER-MFNet: Micro-Expression Recognition Based on Multimodal Fusion Network
conference_papers.summary: Micro-expressions (MEs) are brief and subtle facial movements that can reveal hidden emotions. We observe that MEs are manifestations of small localized changes, and deep learning has already played an important role in this area. However, existing studies do not adequately consider the local and global characteristics of the data: apex frames represent global apex features, while optical flow maps reflect localized subtle movements. Therefore, different data modalities require the use of suitable feature extraction network architectures. In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal fusion network for micro-expression recognition (MER-MFNet). The network comprises three components: apex frames feature learning using vision transformers (ViT), optical flow maps feature selection using convolution neural networks (CNNs), and micro-expression (ME) keypoint feature classification. The apex frames and optical flow maps features are fused using a convex combination method, and their similarity is compared. Finally, the combined features are integrated with the keypoint classification results to achieve efficient MER. Experiments on CASME II, SAMM, SMIC-HS and MEGC2019-CD datasets show that MER-MFNet exhibits excellent performance in MER, significantly improving recognition accuracy and robustness.
institutions: Baoji University of Arts and Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Inverse Linear Quadratic Regulator Problem for Discrete-Time Systems via LMI
conference_papers.summary: This paper focuses on the inverse optimal control problem for discrete-time systems with unknown cost functions using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Based on Pontryagin's minimum principle, a novel model-based algorithm is proposed to reconstruct the weight matrices of an unknown quadratic cost function. This algorithm is formulated using LMIs to find a solution to the algebraic Riccati equation, which is then used to determine the weight matrices. We prove that the solution obtained from LMIs belongs to the set of solutions for the inverse optimal control problem. On this basis, a noniterative model-free algorithm is presented to solve the problem without requiring system matrices. The collected data is used to estimate the unknown weight matrices, and we prove that our algorithm can obtain an approximate optimal solution. Finally, an example illustrates the effectiveness of our algorithms, and comparisons show that our algorithms outperform others.
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Implementation of Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filter on LIMO ROS2
conference_papers.summary: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is crucial for autonomous mobile robots navigating unknown environments. Traditional methods like Extended Kalman Filters and Particle Filters manage uncertainties but often falter in dynamic settings. This article discusses the implementation of the Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filter (RBPF) in the SLAM system of the LIMO ROS2 platform. By integrating RBPF into the default ROS2 framework, we decompose the SLAM problem into simpler sub-problems, enhancing computational efficiency and estimation accuracy. Results show that the implemented system effectively handles dynamic environments and noisy data, as demonstrated through simulations and real-world experiments with the LIMO ROS2 robot.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Human-Robot Collaboration Attack Based on Perception Deception
conference_papers.summary: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) plays a crucial role in various fields, highly relying on the perception capabilities of robots. While some literature explores HRC, research on potential attacks against HRC systems remains lacking. This research gap could lead to system vulnerabilities being exploited, affecting productivity and worker safety, and hindering the further adoption and application of HRC technology. We propose a perception-based deception attack method for HRC, which misguides the robot's perception to attack its decision-making, thereby impacting the effectiveness of human-robot collaboration. Our experiments involved a widely-used HRC task and demonstrated that perception deception could reduce the human-robot collaboration completion rate by over 36.67% and increase decision latency by 87.58%. The experimental results indicate that these attack methods can significantly reduce the robot's perception success rate. Through this research, we lay the foundation for further studies on improving the efficiency and robustness of human-robot collaboration.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Gameplay Generation System Based on Game Description Language
conference_papers.summary: This study defines a specialized game description language, CCGDL, and develops an automated gameplay generation system called Creative Game Machine based on CCGDL. The system facilitates automated gameplay generation and quality evaluation by employing techniques like parent selection and rule crossover, ensuring controllable gameplay quality. Additionally, the study introduces a quantitative analysis method for gameplay quality, utilizing machine learning algorithms to predict gameplay quality. The system significantly reduces design cycles and development costs, demonstrating the potential to enhance traditional game design methodologies.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Fall Detection by 1D-CNN Based on Public Dataset Using a Wrist-Worn Smartwatch
conference_papers.summary: Falls among the elderly population pose a significant threat, often leading to severe injuries, loss of independence, and even fatality. To address this critical issue, researchers have been exploring various approaches to develop effective fall detection systems. In this study, we present a novel fall detection algorithm that leverages the WEDA-FALL dataset, a comprehensive dataset that includes data from wrist-worn sensors capturing both simulated and real-world fall incidents involving elderly individuals. The key insight behind our approach is the observation that falls often exhibit distinct patterns in sensor data. To capture these patterns, we employ a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) architecture, which has been shown to be well-suited for time-series data analysis. By training our model on the WEDA-FALL dataset, we were able to achieve an impressive accuracy of 94% in fall detection, surpassing the commonly reported accuracy levels of around 90% in the existing literature. The high performance of our algorithm can be attributed to the use of the WEDA-FALL dataset and the effectiveness of the 1D-CNN architecture in extracting and learning the characteristic patterns in the sensor data. Notably, our algorithm offers the key features of being quick, highly accurate, and cost-effective, making it a promising solution for practical deployment in real-world settings to improve the safety and well-being of the aging population.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Extremely Low Frequency Communications: Antenna Design, System Design, and Experimental Verification
conference_papers.summary: Wireless communication is the main means of emergency rescue after a disaster. However, electromagnetic waves (EMWs) in commonly used frequency bands experience significant attenuation when passing through obstacles, and traditional extremely low frequency (ELF) antennas are too large to be carried by rescue robots. This paper proposes a new radiation mechanism, which involves changing the current in the solenoid to alter the magnetic field distribution around the solenoid, thereby enabling information loading. This solenoid antenna is capable of emitting a single-cycle sine pulse. To achieve ELF communication using this pulse, this paper presents a joint pulse position and shape modulation (JPPSM) scheme for the transmitter and a flexible delay synchronization (FDS) scheme for the receiver. FDS utilizes distributed pulses to ensure low redundancy and exploits the acquiring and tracking ability to adaptively increase delay to ensure synchronization accuracy. Simulations show that FDS has higher accuracy and faster acquisition than existing schemes. Experiments show that the operating frequency range of the solenoid antenna is from 14 to 165 Hz. The proposed ELF communication system is capable of achieving error-free transmission over a distance of 450 meters.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Exploring the Capability of Deep Neural Network on Ship Sub-Assembly Weld Seam Recognition
conference_papers.summary: To address the problem of robot weld process planning for complex ship sub-assembly work-pieces, this paper explores the capability of the deep neural network models on seam cloud point segmentation tasks. By studying and leveraging the performance of three popular point cloud segmentation models, we choose PointNet++ as the backbone and introduce three improvements to enhance its performance on the weld seam segmentation problem. First, a multi-perspective edge detection method is proposed to improve segmentation accuracy. Second, neighborhood sampling and fast farthest point sampling are introduced to improve the sampling efficiency. Finally, we use fewer convolution layers to reduce the time and space complexity and resolve the overfitting problem. A dataset of sub-assembly models containing 4 plate type classes and 5 seam type classes was established. The training and recognition performance of the advanced PointNet++ model was evaluated and compared with the traditional geometrical weld seam recognition method. The experimental results prove that the proposed method can adapt to 5 typical weld seam classes at a mIoU 83.38%, and it is robust to arbitrary work-piece layout positions, meanwhile, it reaches a speed at 15fps. All the above results demonstrate the great potential of deep neural networks on the robot weld applications for ship sub-assembly work-pieces.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Enhanced CBBA with Multi-Condition Evaluation for Multi-Robot Collaborative Exploration
conference_papers.summary: In multi-robot collaborative exploration of unstructured environments, redundant exploration often occurs, leading to significant consumption of computational resources and thus reducing exploration efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposed the EC-MCE algorithm, an enhancement of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm (CBBA) algorithm, which integrates a fully connected neural network to evaluate five key factors: travel cost, information gain, loop closure likelihood, revisit probability, and deviation for local benefit evaluation. This approach ensures the efficient allocation of boundary points, which in turn ensures the efficient completion of exploration tasks. The effectiveness of this method was verified on the Airsim simulation platform, with experimental results showing that compared to traditional methods, this approach reduced the total exploration time by about 10% and decreased the number of repeated area explorations by about 20%. These improvements significantly enhance the exploration efficiency of the system while ensuring the safe navigation of multiple mobile robots in unstructured environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Energy Optimization Analysis of Robot Trajectories and Optimization Strategies of Processing Tasks Based on Time-Scaling Functions
conference_papers.summary: Currently, optimizing trajectories is an effective method to reduce energy consumption of robotic manufacturing systems. Nevertheless, energy-efficient trajectory planning of robots has consistently posed a challenge. In this paper, we initially analyzed the energy consumption characteristics of industrial robots in detail. Subsequently, a qualitative analysis was conducted on the systematic modeling process from the general energy consumption model to a time-scaling function-based task energy characteristic model. Furthermore, the influencing factors of task energy coefficients were analyzed in depth, and the energy-saving optimization performance of robotic trajectory modification with time-scaling functions was evaluated via case studies. The results demonstrate that execution time is the primary determinant of energy consumption; moreover, the acceleration and deceleration patterns of end tools also have an influence on energy consumption, but this influence is notably significant in scenarios with shorter execution time only, and is usually smaller than the impact of execution time on energy consumption. Finally, energy-saving optimization strategies of typical processing tasks were proposed after analyzing the optimization hierarchies of robot processing trajectories based on the time-scaling method. This study can provide theoretical bases and technical supports for energy consumption modeling and energy-saving trajectory planning of industrial robots and robotic processing systems.
