conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Efficient Residual Chlorine Tracking and Automated Neutralization System
conference_papers.summary: In industrial applications, seawater is frequently utilized as a heat source for gasification, necessitating chlorination to prevent microbial fouling of equipment. However, leftover residual chlorine poses a risk of marine pollution. This design outlines an STM32 microcontroller-based automatic system for monitoring and neutralizing residual chlorine. The system continuously tracks chlorine levels and autonomously administers sodium sulfite to neutralize excess chlorine. The hardware integrates modules for residual chlorine detection, flow rate measurement of the metering pump, motor driving, and signal conversion. The software framework includes systems for regulating chlorine concentration, monitoring pump flow rates, and controlling motor operations. Tests validate that all modules perform well, ensuring the system runs smoothly, efficiently manages residual chlorine, and safeguards the marine ecosystem.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Voxel-Based Lidar Inertial Fusion SLAM Algorithm for Denial Scenarios
conference_papers.summary: To solve the problem of vehicle location mapping limitation in urban canyons, tunnels, and other low-texture, low-light, and high-dynamic denial scenes, a dynamic voxel-based lidar inertial fusion SLAM algorithm DSC-Algo for denial scenes is proposed. The algorithm introduces a dynamic voxel data structure to maintain the local map and nearest neighbor search, which can efficiently insert and delete new lidar points, to improve the computational efficiency of the algorithm. At the same time, the pose optimization method of factor map was used to introduce the loop detection factor of scan-context descriptors that could reflect the three-dimensional structure characteristics of the point cloud, and the objective function including odometer factor, IMU pre-integration factor and the error term of scan-context environment loop detection factor was constructed. The optimal pose state was solved by a nonlinear optimization algorithm, and the positioning accuracy was improved. A complete SLAM algorithm framework is constructed by odometry algorithm, factor graph optimization, and loop closure detection. Compared with the mainstream lidar inertial SLAM algorithm FAST-LIO2, the computational efficiency of the proposed DSC-Algo algorithm in the iterative Kalman filtering stage and point cloud distortion removal stage is improved by nearly 40%. The test results of real vehicles in the reality denial scenario of the underground parking lot and urban tunnel show that DSC-Algo algorithm has higher positioning accuracy and more accurate mapping effect than the FAST-LIO2 and LeGO-LOAM algorithms.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Task Sequence Allocation Based on Natural Language Instruction
conference_papers.summary: In recent years, with the development of technology, robots have become more prominent in the public eye. Service robots are now being used in some smart hotels to decrease manual transportation costs. However, these service robots operate according to set instructions, and humans usually apply fixed operating instructions to control the robots. Whether in daily life or at work, humans are more likely to use natural language to communicate and give task instructions. Moreover, in the field of multi-robotics, most of the existing researches on multi-task assignment have been conducted in simulation environments on a list of pre-set tasks, and seldom update the task sequences in real time in conjunction with the real environmental information and time. In this paper, we propose a method for assigning dynamic navigation task sequences based on natural language instruction and verify its effectiveness in a real scenario.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Simulation of MNPs Particles Removed from Vessels by Micro-Nanorobots
conference_papers.summary: In this study, a Spherical Magnetic Robot (SMR) was designed to remove Magnetic Nanoparticles (MNPs) particles from blood vessels by micro and nano robots, and was studied by dynamic simulation model. SMR is based on a miniaturized design that utilizes magnet drive and integrates a high permeability alloy material to achieve effective adsorption and transport of MNPs particles. In this study, multiphysics problems for vascular modeling, SMR design, motion control, and MNPs particle capture were integrated, and a simulation model was constructed using the COMSOL Multiphysics software. The results show that SMR shows excellent navigation accuracy and adsorption performance in the process of removing MNPs, which verifies the key role of high-precision magnetic field control in SMR motion and MNPs adsorption process.
institutions: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Development of a Laser-based Measuring System for the Radius and Roundness of Stator
conference_papers.summary: A stator measurement system based on laser displacement sensors was developed to solve the problems of low efficiency, human error, and data visualization of the manual measurement of the stacked core radius in the stator assembly process of hydropower stations. First, the mechanical structure of the stator measurement system is designed based on the principle of comparison measurement, and the measurement of the stator radius of any cross-section is realized through motion control of the mechanical structure. Second, based on the laser sampling data, a method of compensating for the measurement error caused by the center column and stator's eccentricity is proposed, saving the time required to install and adjust the center column. Then, a software system with the functions of data processing, display, and storage was developed based on Python. Finally, the stator radius and roundness field test is carried out based on the above process. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the radius and roundness measurements of the measuring system is 0.078 and 0.051 mm, respectively, which meets the demand for fast and accurate measurement of the stator radius and roundness.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Development of Soccer Robot
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents the development of soccer robots for the WRG (World Robot Game) competition. Two models of soccer robots are designed and developed following the rules of WRG competition. One model is designed for 4WD (wheel drive), and another one is designed for 2WD. The soccer robots are controlled using a Flysky FS-GT3B RC transmitter in wireless communication. System structure and software development for controlling movement of the soccer robot are presented in this paper.
institutions: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Development and Implementation of a 6-DOF Robotic Arm with Machine Vision for Sorting Application
conference_papers.summary: The automation of sorting tasks has been essential for various industrial applications, and this study focused on developing a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic arm to accurately sort objects through QR code scanning. The researcher conducted 40 trials across four distinct sets, categorized by color (red/blue) and size (small/large), obtained from a comprehensive functionality test. This study used sorting time as the dependent variable, while the independent variables are the four sorting categories analyzed through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results revealed no significant differences in sorting times among the four sets, indicating that the robotic arm performed consistently across all categories. This finding demonstrated the robotic arm's effectiveness, accuracy, and flexibility in handling variations in object attributes such as color and size. The study concluded that the developed 6-DOF robotic arm, combined with machine vision technology and advanced control algorithms, was a reliable and efficient solution for small-scale automated sorting applications, making a valuable contribution to the advancement of robotic systems in industrial automation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of an Intelligent Assisted Medical Robotic Arm
conference_papers.summary: With the continuous development of science and technology and the aging trend of population, the accuracy, efficiency and safety of medical and manufacturing services have been put forward higher requirements. As an important branch in the field of productivity development, the robotic arm provides assistance to the development of manufacturing and medical fields by integrating advanced automation, sensor technology and precise mechanical structure design. In this paper, we design a kind of intelligent medical robot arm, realize the control of robot arm through visual recognition and voice recognition function, aiming to improve the quality of medical service and manufacturing production, reduce medical cost, reduce the waste of human resources, and promote the innovation and development of medical technology.
institutions: Jilin Agricultural Science and Technology University

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Prototyping of an Robotic Exoskeleton for Rehabilitation After Total Knee Arthroplasty
conference_papers.summary: The most increasing trend is to utilize total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as a surgical solution to relief the effects of severe arthritis. Researchers have become interested in replacing an efficient robotic assisted method in place of traditional physiotherapy post-TKA. The effectiveness of these devices in reducing recovery time, improving mobility, and decreasing the risk of future injuries is entirely reliant on the design and functionality of the proposed robotic system. The main objective of this study is to propose a streamlined and organized process to design and construct an exoskeletal robotic system for post-TKA, drawing on biomechanical investigations. In the design of a system for safe human-robot interaction during rehabilitation, it is crucial to prioritize compatibility and reliability as important parameters. This research proposes a framework that combines physiotherapy protocol with biomechanical analysis of human motion to address these issues. An experimental investigation was conducted on the built prototype to assess the performance of the suggested design framework.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of VGA Image Transmission Based on FPGA
conference_papers.summary: With the increase of image data scale, a faster and more efficient image acquisition and processing system is needed. FPGA has good parallel performance, which is very suitable for algorithms dealing with basic parallel features, and can greatly improve the efficiency of image acquisition and processing system. Aiming at the problem of FPGA image acquisition, processing and display, this paper carries out the design of real-time image acquisition system, which has the function of real-time display after processing the acquired image. In this paper, the chip of EP4CE6F17C8 of Cyclone IV series is used, the CMOS camera is OV5640 and the monitor is VAG. After full experimental verification, the system is extensible, the later expansion goal can not be achieved without the cooperation of Bluetooth and other facilities, with the role of recognizing and positioning license plates, obviously this series of application prospects are considerable; With flexibility, can customize the algorithm for optimization; Low cost a series of advantages.
institutions: Chongqing Vocational College of Culture and Arts

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Application of Communication Technology System for Mine Power Supply
conference_papers.summary: This paper deeply discusses the present situation, development and application of communication technology of mine power supply. The communication technology of mine power supply plays a vital role in modern mining production. With the improvement of automation and intelligence in coal mines, the requirements for power supply and communication technology are increasingly strict. The harsh working environment under the mine, such as high dust, high gas concentration and high noise, poses a severe challenge to the stability of power supply and the reliability of communication. Therefore, this paper studies the communication technology of mine power supply, puts forward the system design and application of mine power supply communication technology, and gives a detailed explanation from hardware design to software design and system integration and testing. The test shows that the system improves the safety, efficiency and intelligence level of mine production, which is of great significance for ensuring the safety of miners, optimizing the energy structure and promoting the sustainable development of mines.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Comparison of KAN, MLP, and SVM for NIR Spectra Classification
conference_papers.summary: Near infrared spectra are typically high dimensional data and widely used in various industries and scientific areas. Various machine learning algorithms have been employed to classify the NIR spectral data. This paper compares the performance of three popular models: the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), in classifying Mah map datasets which are derived from preprocessed NIR spectra. This study investigates the performance of three prominent machine learning models Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Network (KAN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), in classifying high-dimensional Near Infrared (NIR) data within the tobacco industry. The impact of hidden layer architecture on classification accuracy was examined for both MLP and KAN networks. While KAN demonstrated superior accuracy and stability with L-BFGS optimization, particularly when employing two hidden layers, it exhibited inferior performance with Adam optimization compared to MLP. With one hidden layer and same hidden neuron number, KAN can provide slightly better classification accuracy in high dimension than both MLP and SVM. However, SVM proved generally stable across various input dimensions, achieving high classification accuracy.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Closed-Loop Individual Music Neurofeedback Based on Brain-Computer Interaction for Student Stress Intervention
conference_papers.summary: Music neurofeedback is a non-invasive method for regulating neural activity and reducing stress based on brain-computer interface technology combined with music stimulation. However, the current music neurofeedback protocol is regulated by a single indicator, resulting in significant differences in individual effects. This study proposed a neurofeedback protocol based on personalized music selection and used three stress scales and two cognitive behavioral experiments to evaluate the stress regulation effect, and combined electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate analysis to explore the stress relief mechanism. Five university students participated in a five-session neurofeedback training. After the intervention, the results of the Depression-Anxiety-Stress Scale (DASS-21) and the Stroop task showed a significant decrease in the scores of stress-related symptoms and a significant improvement in response inhibition. The EEG results showed that the absolute power of the a band in the frontal and temporal lobes increased significantly, the coverage and duration of microstate C decreased significantly, and the duration of microstate D increased significantly, which was significantly correlated with the reduction of stress scores. Personalized music neurofeedback provides a potentially effective tool and innovative perspective for student stress management. The elucidation of spatiotemporal neurocognitive mechanisms provides a new theoretical framework for the development and optimization of neurofeedback protocols.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Calculation Method of Collision Probability for Airdroping Targets in Limited Space
conference_papers.summary: Airdropping relief supplies to disaster-stricken areas is one of the most effective means to implement rapid supply after major natural disasters. Due to the relatively small key disaster-stricken areas, the collision of airdrop targets in a limited space will make it difficult for relief supplies to reach the rescue area accurately, thus losing the value of airdrop. Starting from the general form of collision probability, this paper studies three numerical calculations: direct solution, two-dimensional integral and one-dimensional integral by transforming the three-dimensional probability calculation problem into the two-dimensional probability calculation problem in the vertical encounter plane. Numerical examples show that the results of the two kinds of integrals are relatively close, and they can be used to calculate the collision probability of airdrop targets in most cases, and the one-dimensional integrals are more advantageous without considering the factor of calculation efficiency; Based on the condition that the projected area is circular and the probability density does not change much, the direct solution can also be used to calculate the collision probability in general cases, but compared with the two-dimensional integral and the one-dimensional integral, the maximum calculation error is about 2.74% and 2.97% respectively; The two-dimensional integral calculation can be used to calculate the collision probability in most cases, and the calculation accuracy is relatively high. When considering the calculation efficiency factor, the two-dimensional integral calculation can replace the one-dimensional integral calculation. The conclusion of the study can provide support for the implementation of active evasion strategy of airdrop targets.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Bringing Two Worlds Together: The Convergence of Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
conference_papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed numerous fields with their strong capabilities in generalization and inference, yet they face challenges such as dependence on probabilistic reasoning, lack of factual knowledge, and limited interpretability. Knowledge Graphs (KGs), with their structured factual information, can address these gaps by providing external knowledge, though they also struggle with issues like scalability and representing new or unseen facts. Integrating LLMs and KGs offers a complementary solution, as both can mutually enhance each other. This article categorizes and reviews three main frameworks: (1) LLM-enhanced KGs, where LLMs support KG tasks like embedding, completion, and question answering; (2) KGenhanced LLMs, which integrate KGs to improve LLMs' factual understanding; and (3) Collaborative KGs and LLMs, where both systems interact symbiotically, enabling bidirectional reasoning. We review representative methods, analyze current limitations, and discuss future research directions and applications.
institutions: Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics Dongfang College

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Automatic Detection Device for Ripple of Mine Power Supply
conference_papers.summary: Power supply ripple, as one of the important indexes to measure the quality of power supply, has an important influence on the stability and reliability of mine electronic equipment. Because of its special working environment and load requirements, mine power supply puts forward higher requirements for the suppression and detection of power supply ripple. This paper expounds the generation mechanism of power supply ripple, analyzes the difference between linear power supply and switching power supply in ripple generation, and puts forward an automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple. The hardware of the device is highly integrated with high-precision detection equipment such as oscilloscope, source voltage and electronic load, and the software adopts virtual instrument technology to design an automatic detection system for mine power supply ripple. The experimental results show that the automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple has been improved in accuracy, stability and automation, which provides a more efficient and reliable solution for mine power supply ripple detection.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Automated Detection of Korean Melons Based on YOLOv10 for Use in Quadruped Robot
conference_papers.summary: The production of Korean melon, known as Chamoe, in South Korea faces significant challenges due to the decline of the rural labor force and the high labor demands of manual greenhouse harvesting. This study provides a critical step toward developing an automated Korean melon harvesting system using a quadruped robotic platform. This study focuses on the evaluation of a deep learning model, YOLOv10, for accurate melon detection in Korean greenhouse environments, which is a key component of the proposed automated harvesting system. We used YOLOv10, a state-of-the-art object detection algorithm, and the model was trained and tested on a custom dataset of Korean melon images. An NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU and an Intel Core i9-13900K (3.0-5.8 GHz) CPU running Ubuntu 22.04 were used for the performance evaluation. The YOLOv10-based model showed promising results, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.927 at an intersection over union (IoU) threshold of 0.5. This model is suitable for use in robotic systems where resources are limited due to its compact size of only 5.7 MB. The model used only 11 % of the GPU capacity for setup and 2–3 % for inference. This demonstrates its efficiency and potential for real-time applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Application Research on Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance and Navigation of Intelligent Vehicle Based on ROS
conference_papers.summary: The research and application of autonomous driving technology are rapidly entering a stage of vigorous development, in which dynamic obstacle avoidance navigation technology is the key to achieve autonomous driving. In this paper, an intelligent car based on ROS (Robot Operating System) is studied and applied for dynamic obstacle avoidance and navigation. This paper aims to use the laser radar, so that the system can sense the surrounding environment in real time, through the SLAM algorithm to build a map, and combined with advanced path planning algorithm. At the same time, it can achieve intelligent avoidance of dynamic obstacles for vehicles. In the process of navigation, in order to adapt to the dynamic environment, A * and TEB path planner algorithms are used by the system to select the optimal path to the target location, and at the same time, it can dynamically avoid obstacles, and finally through the test to ensure the rationality of the design. The experimental results show that the global path planner and TEB local path planner can realize the dynamic obstacle avoidance of intelligent vehicle in the process of navigation. This research can bring certain reference for the development and application of unmanned driving technology in the later period.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Analysis of Electric Field on the Surface of Fittings and Main Equipment Inside ± 800kV UHV Converter Valve Hall Based on the Finite Element Analysis
conference_papers.summary: The valve hall in a UHV converter station serves as the hub of a UHV DC transmission project. When operating normally, it adheres to rigorous standards concerning the surface electric field of its internal fittings. Consequently, during the design phase of the valve hall, it is crucial to calculate and validate the electric field strength on the surface of these fittings to guarantee that it remains beneath the corona field strength for each piece of equipment. In this paper, the simulation calculation of the high-end valve hall fittings of a UHV DC transmission project ± 800kV converter station is carried out. The numerical calculation method of the surface electric field of the UHV DC valve hall fittings is studied. The whole model of the valve hall equipment is established to calculate and analyze the electric field. The distribution characteristics of the surface electric field when the valve hall equipment is working are obtained, and the maximum surface field strength of each fitting in the valve hall is found. Analyze whether it is dizzy, study the distribution law of its surface field strength, and check the performance of shielding fittings.
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Electrical Insulation and Power Equipment

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: An Iterative Variable Step Error Compensation Approach for Enhancing Robot Trajectory Accuracy
conference_papers.summary: In this paper, an iterative error compensation approach is analyzed and designed to improve trajectory accuracy of industrial robots. Advanced offline programming and robotic machining tasks require high trajectory accuracy of industrial robots, which is significantly affected by parameter inaccuracy, stiffness deformation, backlash, and so on. Such complicated coupling makes it impossible to model each factor separately, thus data-driven direct error compensation is the major solution to improve trajectory accuracy. Previous methods utilize external measurement equipment to obtain tracking error and rely on the error consistency assumption to compensate for the error by modifying the trajectory commands directly. However, such consistency assumption does not hold. Even a minor incremental modification of the initial commands can lead to unexpected influence on the robot's tracking performance, owning to unaccounted factors such as the robot's dynamic stiffness and natural frequency. This paper decomposes trajectory tracking errors based on servo encoder feedback and external laser tracker, and proposes a variable step error compensation scheme to improve tracking performance. Physical experiments are conducted on a standard 6 degree-of-freedom industrial robot to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results of various error compensation approaches are analyzed to draw a possible error correlation model, in order to account for the error inconsistency in the compensation process.
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Robotics and Systems

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Advanced Government Chatbot Featuring Multi-Source Strategy for Effective Goal-Driven Dialogues
conference_papers.summary: Government chatbots (G-chatbots) aim to provide proactive, comprehensive information services, focusing on high-quality consultation rather than just answering queries. Due to the complexity of user questions, multiple dialogue turns are often needed for accurate responses. However, optimal answers in single turns may not align with the user's ultimate goal. To address this, we propose a Multi-Source-Aware algorithm designed for conversation-level objectives in G-chatbots. This algorithm features two key components: the Multi-Source-Aware (MSA) adapter module, which fine-tunes the chatbot's understanding based on user intent, conversation context, and preset knowledge, and the Virtual Edge module, which guides the conversation toward the final goal. Experiments show that this approach improves QA efficiency and answer quality, with fine-tuning using just 0. 01-13% of the parameters, resulting in a 2% increase in question comprehension and a 6% boost in answer quality compared to baseline models.
institutions: Dongbei University of Finance and Economics

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Active Lateral Riding Comfort Control Strategies of High-Speed Train
conference_papers.summary: Based on the lateral vibration control of bogie frame for improving hunting stability in high-speed trains, three control strategies including linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control, Fuzzy Proportional-Integral (Fuzzy-PI) Control and Particle Swarm Optimization Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PSO-PID) Control are compared in this study. For the simplified linear lateral dynamics model of single bogie, the control parameters under the three control strategies are acquired, then they are applied to the vehicle dynamics model co-simulated by the SIMPACK and MATLAB codes. The different train operating conditions are taken into account and the improvement of dynamics indexes under the three control strategies are evaluated from the aspects of lateral riding quality of the car body and lateral force of wheelsets. The results show that the three control strategies lead to obvious mitigation on lateral vibration, and the improvement of PSO-PID control is the most obvious, but the LQR control effect is the worst.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: AI-Driven Metaverse Digital Twin Cities: Prototype Platform Design for Integrated Virtual Urban Ecosystems and Services
conference_papers.summary: This study presents a cutting-edge platform, meticulously crafted by a multidisciplinary team, designed to actualize Metaverse Digital Twin Cities (Meta-city) and their associated Scene Services. The Meta-city integrates real-world urban services with a virtual CIM platform, offering a novel hybrid experience that merges virtual and real-world services. The platform's architecture is structured into five layers: Perception, Data, Platform, AI Engine, and Metaverse, culminating in an extensive 3D model database that augments the capabilities of traditional smart city frameworks. It targets users with significant urban modeling needs, such as city administrators and residents, providing a multi-dimensional 3D city operation and maintenance model suitable for both administrative and commercial use. This model is complemented by services like real-time rendering monitoring and urban disaster prevention etc., tailored to meet the unique demands of urban stakeholders. The platform's integrated approach is poised to streamline urban governance by leveraging digital twins, thereby revolutionizing the urban experience. The fusion of diverse expertise within the platform ensures a holistic strategy for advancing urban digital ecosystems, potentially redefining smart city technologies. Currently operational in several pilot Chinese cities, this initiative exemplifies the application of theoretical research to engineering practice to enhance urban operations and governance efficiency.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Structure Design and Finite Element Analysis of a Dual Servo-Driven Gripping Manipulator
conference_papers.summary: In response to the difficulties in grasping irregular objects and the single grasping angle issue of mechanical claws carried by small multi-rotor aerial vehicles, this paper takes the grasping mechanical claw carried by multi-rotor aerial vehicles as the research object and designs a four-finger mechanical claw driven by dual servos that can rotate. First, the mechanical claw model was established in SolidWorks, and then it was imported into ANSYS Workbench for static and transient dynamic analysis of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw, obtaining the total deformation and stress distribution cloud diagrams of each component. The analysis results indicate that during the process of grasping objects, the maximum stress of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw is far less than the material yield strength, and all meet the working requirements. This provides a reference for the design and optimization of similar structures such as mechanical claws carried by rotor aerial vehicles.
institutions: Jiangxi University of Water Resources and Electric Power

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Practical HCI Evaluation Approach of Flight Deck
conference_papers.summary: To evaluate the Human-Computer Interface (HCI) of the flight deck effectively and thoroughly, a practical evaluation approach of flight deck has been proposed. This methodology involves conducting a series of crew-task-based human factors evaluations, and has gained widespread acceptance in both the design and iterative phases of flight deck. Through extensive practical application, this approach has demonstrated its importance and practicality, particularly in identifying potential human factors issues and analyzing design optimization requirements. It facilitates iterative upgrades of cockpit design during the initial stages effectively, thereby preventing potential human factors issues and ensuring design optimization and improvement.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A New Efficient Classification Method for Monkeypox Virus Skin Lesions Based on MPFormer
conference_papers.summary: Monkeypox is a serious zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus. Traditional laboratory detection methods are time-consuming and have high biosafety requirements; in particular, electron microscopy is expensive and complicated to operate. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel classification algorithm for monkeypox virus skin lesions based on the Vision Transformer-MPFormer. We adopted a transfer learning strategy to train the MPFormer model on a monkeypox virus skin lesion dataset for accurate classification. Experimental results on the MSLD dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves significant performance improvements compared to common models and other classification algorithms, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 97.78%, 97.88%, 97.78%, and 97.78%, respectively. This study provides an efficient computer-aided diagnostic tool for rapid and accurate detection of the monkeypox virus, offering important practical application value.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Method for Cockpit Human-Machine Interface Assessment Based on Human Error Analysis
conference_papers.summary: With technological advancements and increased automation, many traditional mechanical failures have been effectively prevented and resolved, but human errors remain difficult to completely avoid. New technologies and highly integrated complex designs are continuously being introduced into the cockpit, presenting new challenges for cockpit operations. Advanced human-machine interface designs that lack consideration for human factors may, paradoxically, increase the risk of operational errors by the crew, affecting operational efficiency and potentially threatening flight safety. Therefore, it is crucial to fully consider human factors in cockpit human-machine interface design, identify potential design traps that may lead to human errors, optimize the design accordingly, and thereby improve crew operational efficiency and flight safety. This paper proposes a systematic, structured assessment method for civil aircraft cockpit human-machine interfaces based on human error analysis. This method analyzes the cockpit human-machine interface by predicting human errors caused by or related to the design and assesses the adequacy and effectiveness of the cockpit human-machine interface in managing crew errors. It aims to help designers identify potential deficiencies in the cockpit human-machine interface design and enables programs to understand and manage potential human error effects, understand the relative risks and uncertainties within the system design, and influence decisions throughout the system lifecycle. And this method is good at standardization of Cockpit HMI human error analysis during CS 25.1302 compliance demonstration practices.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Language-Prompted Model for Semi-Supervised Object Detection
conference_papers.summary: Object detection is a cornerstone of computer vision and artificial intelligence. Despite the advancements made by previous methods, they typically focus on visual signals, often overlooking the potential benefits of integrating language descriptions. Large-scale pre-trained language models offer rich semantic understanding that can complement visual cues, yet their application in object detection remains underexplored. This paper proposes a novel approach: a language-guided model for semi-supervised object detection. Unlike conventional methods that rely solely on visual features, our approach integrates a language model to encode descriptive information corresponding to images. For annotated data, language descriptions are derived from ground truth, capturing object categories and precise spatial coordinates in coherent sentences. In addition to leveraging labeled data, our method utilizes pseudo-labels for language descriptions on unlabeled data, enhancing training efficiency and model generalization. Experiments on MS-COCO dataset validate the superiority of our approach, which outperforms competitive methods with fewer labels.
institutions: Gannan University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Human Factors Validation Methods Incorporating the Degrees of Novelty, Complexity, and Integration of Cockpit Design Items
conference_papers.summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive Human Factors validation framework for CS25.1302 regulation, explaining how the degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration impact the level of scrutiny required for aircraft cockpit design items. The background underscores the role of human factors consideration for new, complex, and integrated designs in aircraft cockpit. The study aims to provide designers and regulatory authorities with a systematic methodology for determining appropriate means of compliance tailored to the varying degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration of design items. This method outlines the process of selecting a reference aircraft, participants, criteria employed, and how to carry out the assessment. Furthermore, it proposes the framework for selecting appropriate means of compliance considering the level of scrutiny supported by a case study. This framework not only optimizes the Human Factors evaluation procedures but also develops more reasonable scrutiny strategies. This, in turn, contributes to the overall enhancement of cockpit design safety and reliability.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: A Corrosion Detection Method for Hydraulic Metal Structures Based on an Improved YOLOv10 Model
conference_papers.summary: To achieve corrosion detection of hydraulic metal structures based on deep learning, reduce subjectivity in the corrosion annotation process, and enhance annotation efficiency, this study proposes a corrosion detection method for hydraulic metal structures based on a YOLOv10 serial architecture that incorporates a Transformer module. The serial architecture first uses an object detection model to locate corrosion, followed by a classification model to assess corrosion severity. In terms of F1-score, the proposed corrosion detection network shows a 1% improvement over the baseline. For accuracy, after transfer learning, the proposed corrosion classification model outperforms the baseline by 8.8%. This method was implemented in real-world scenarios, successfully enabling corrosion detection and severity classification of hydraulic metal structures, and verifying the feasibility of the serial architecture.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Workspace Analysis of 6-RSS Parallel Robot to Assist Cervical Laminectomy
conference_papers.summary: Cervical laminectomy is a common clinical procedure to decompress the cervical spine. However, because of the limited operating space of cervical spine surgery, the surgeon's operation precision is required to be high. Robot-assisted surgery can usually achieve good precision by precise positioning and manipulation of the robot, while parallel robots can attain better precision due to their mechanical characteristics. Compared with other types of parallel robots, the 6-RSS has a simpler structure and lower mass of moving parts, and therefore performs better in human-robot interaction, which ensures the surgeon's precise operation. However, the kinematic analysis of 6-RSS parallel robots is usually more complicated than other types, making the workspace analysis difficult. In this paper, the theoretical mechanism model of the 6-RSS parallel robot was built and coordinates were defined. The workspace was analyzed to evaluate end rotation and movement ability, which can optimize the structural design and guide the robot design.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Wheel-Terrain Contact Geometry Estimation using the Aside-Wheel RGB-D Sensor over Soft Terrain
conference_papers.summary: Wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) have exhibited notable competitiveness in various applications, including geo-graphic and planetary exploration. Nonetheless, when traversing on soft terrains, their wheels might encounter sinkage and slippage, leading to mission failure. Consequently, real-time estimation of contact parameters such as sinkage and slip ratio holds significant importance for rover operations. In this paper, we introduce a novel algorithm that employs only one aside-wheel RGB-D camera for the simultaneous detection of wheel sinkage and slip ratio on deformable terrains in real-time. We estimate sinkage through the depth module by processing point cloud data, and we estimate slip ratio through the color module with a sequence of image processing steps. Utilizing only one single camera reduces errors arising from sensor signal alignment and enhances detection accuracy. With a single-wheel testbed, we simulate wheel motion under different slip ratios and carry out numerous experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Our algorithm attains a detection frequency of up to 20Hz and exhibits outstanding precision. The relative sinkage error remains below 4%, while the relative slippage error is confined within 0.8%.
institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Viscometer with Remote Electromagnetic Control
conference_papers.summary: A new modification of a smartphone-controlled viscometer is proposed, in which a significant part of the operations performed by the electronic components of existing analogs are transferred to operations performed by software installed on the user's smartphone. The principle of operation of the viscometer is based on the Stokes method, i.e., the speed of falling of a ball in a tube filled with the test solution is measured experimentally. A distinctive feature of the design of the proposed equipment is the use of a rotary mechanism that turns the tube over. There are also two electromagnets on the turntable that hold the ball in position at the ends of the tube when it is turned over. The advantage of this design is the possibility of multiple repetitions of measurements: when the ball falls to the bottom of the tube, one of the electromagnets is turned on, fixing the position of the ball, and then the tube is turned over and the process is repeated again. The most significant advantage of the proposed design is a significant reduction in operating costs associated with the washing of the measuring unit.
institutions: Almaty University of Power Engineering and Telecommunications
Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Macromolecular Chemistry

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Verification Method of Intelligent Prosthetic Algorithm Based on Anthropomorphic Walking Robot
conference_papers.summary: A key issue in the research of intelligent prosthetics is the verification and analysis of the proposed prosthetic motion planning and control methods. In this paper, it is proposed that using a humanoid walking robot as the subject can effectively test the interaction dynamics between the prosthesis and the human body. This method also avoids the risk of injury to amputee patients when participating in the test before the control method is mature. Specifically, the anthropomorphic walking of bipedal walking robots is first realized, and a testbed that fully simulates the straight leg walking is obtained. The right leg (below the thigh) of the bipedal robot is then replaced with an intelligent prosthesis. When testing the planning and control methods of intelligent prosthetics, prosthetic controllers run independently. The bipedal walking robot, except for the part below the right thigh, normally performs the “humanoid motion controller”. Effective intelligent prosthetic control methods will make the prosthesis-“human” coupling system produce smooth walking movements, while ineffective intelligent prosthetic control will cause the coupling system to fall due to strong interference.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Vehicle Formation Matching and Simulation in Cooperative Vehicle Infrastructure System Environment
conference_papers.summary: In order to solve the problem that independent vehicles can choose the best formation to join, this paper proposes a vehicle formation matching strategy in cooperative vehicle infrastructure system (CVIS). Firstly, a description of the formation matching problem in the highway scenario is given, and secondly, the objective function of the formation matching problem is constructed and the corresponding constraints are set. In this way, matching algorithms for centralised and distributed formations are obtained. Finally, based on the set conditions, the formation matching strategy in the scenario of this paper is simulated and verified. The results show that based on the proposed formation matching strategy, the pass time is reduced by 381s and the energy consumption is improved by 38.7%,31.8%,40.6%,26.2%,22.1% and 29.4% in different degrees. This implies that the formation matching strategy, is more effective in selecting the best formation to join, resulting in a more efficient and energy-efficient traffic system.
institutions: Shandong University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Utilizing Lyapunov-Based Model Predictive Control to Achieve Dynamic Positioning for the Haizhe Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
conference_papers.summary: This paper demonstrates the application of a Lyapunov-Based Model Predictive Control (LBMPC) framework in achieving dynamic positioning (DP) using the Haizhe autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) as a case study. Moreover, addressing the thrust allocation (TA) subproblem and optimizing DP control, LBMPC considers real-world restrictions. It makes use of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller, which ensures stability in the closed-loop system and continual feasibility within the system. Furthermore, attaining an extensive region of attraction, the contraction constraint improves stability. Control theory and optimization techniques are integrated into the framework, enabling smooth online optimization integration for enhanced control performance. The success of this strategy is shown by simulation findings on the Haizhe AUV, which represents a breakthrough in underwater vehicle control.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Unmanned Vehicle Navigation Based on ROS
conference_papers.summary: Under modern conditions, the development momentum of international unmanned driving technology is booming, but the industrialization of unmanned driving cars is still limited by the current level of software and hardware. Reducing the complex and high standard requirements of unmanned driving and then studying unmanned vehicle navigation technology in some simple scenarios are also a hot topic in current research. This paper studies an unmanned autonomous navigation vehicle based on robot operating system (ROS) software framework on the Ubuntu operating system. It combines algorithms such as simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) technology, adaptive Monte Carlo localization (AMCL) technology and path planning, aiming to solve the problems of simultaneous localization, mapping and path planning in a closed environment. This case algorithm avoids the problem of large error accumulation caused by traditional odometer navigation and global positioning system (GPS) navigation technologies. The simulation results show that the algorithm has good practical application value.
institutions: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Trajectory Tracking of AUV under Current Disturbance Based on Adaptive LADRC
conference_papers.summary: In consideration of the trajectory tracking problem of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) under external current disturbance, an adaptive linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) method is proposed. Unlike the conditional LADRC using fixed parameters for extended state observer, the proposed controller makes use of the error of estimation and automatically adjusts the parameter online. As shown in the simulation, the adaptive LADRC estimates the external current disturbance effectively, and tracks the 3D trajectory better compared with traditional LADRC.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Towards a Safe Real-Time Motion Planning Framework for Autonomous Driving Systems: A Model Predictive Path Integral Approach
conference_papers.summary: Planning safe trajectories in Autonomous Driving Systems (ADS) is a complex problem to solve in real-time. The main challenge to solve this problem arises from the various conditions and constraints imposed by road geometry, semantics and traffic rules, as well as the presence of dy-namic agents. Recently, Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) has shown to be an effective framework for optimal motion planning and control in robot navigation in unstructured and highly uncertain environments. In this paper, we formulate the motion planning problem in ADS as a nonlinear stochastic dynamic optimization problem that can be solved using an MPPI strategy. The main technical contribution of this work is a method to handle obstacles within the MPPI formulation safely. In this method, obstacles are approximated by circles that can be easily integrated into the MPPI cost formulation while considering safety margins. The proposed MPPI framework has been efficiently implemented in our autonomous vehicle and experimentally validated using three different primitive scenarios. Experimental results show that generated trajectories are safe, feasible and perfectly achieve the planning objective. The video results as well as the open-source implementation are available at https://gitlab.uni.lu/360lab-public/mppi.
institutions: Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Three-Dimensional Trajectory Planning for Multi-Robot Collaboration in Complex Components with Heterogeneous Materials
conference_papers.summary: A multi-robot collaboration can reliably perform complex tasks that would be difficult for a single robot to accomplish, especially advanced welding operations in complex components with heterogeneous materials. We focused on a three-dimensional (3D) trajectory planning for complex components with heterogeneous materials, and carries out the research of multi-robot collaboration. By using the software of robot simulator CoppeliaSim, the comparative simulation analysis of multi-robot active-slave and distributed in 3D intersecting line was proposed. Through the establishment of multi-robot collaborative experiment system, the trajectory planning of multi-robot axial motion with semi-∞ was put forward. Simulation and experimental results show that our proposed multi-robot system is feasible and is capable of realizing 3D trajectory planning for complex components with heterogeneous materials.
institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Thermal Perception Using Augmented Reality for Industrial Safety
conference_papers.summary: There are many factors that can negatively impact worker safety in manufacturing or industry. In particular, hazards such as contact of workers' hands or other body parts with overheated components can lead to accidents and production losses. Hot surfaces cannot be seen with the naked eye. To detect hot surfaces, thermal cameras can be utilized in work areas. Placing multiple thermal cameras in large work environments, such as factories, is cost prohibitive, and carrying them is not a solution. This paper proposes an augmented reality-based assistant that visualizes hot surfaces by integrating thermal camera information into augmented reality goggles. The major advantages of the system are twofold: (1) it consists of an untethered mobile hardware platform with a thermal camera that can send information through a wireless connection, (2) the visualization is implemented for augmented reality head-mounted displays that do not require the use of workers' hands, unlike tablet-based augmented reality. Augmenting human sight with thermal vision may also have an impact on other research areas in the future.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: The Temperature Field Characteristics of Deflector Jet Servo Valve Under Extreme High-Temperature Conditions
conference_papers.summary: The Deflector Jet Servo Valve (DJSV) is often exposed to operating conditions with extreme high-temperature environments. Such as, the DJSV is installed within aero engines, the ambient temperature can reach as high as 250°C, and the maximum temperature of the working oil is 140 °C. To ensure optimal performance, the temperature distribution of DJSV under extreme high-temperature conditions is simulated by Fluent simulation software. By combining the simulation results with the actual working conditions, a new self-cooling structure of DJSV is proposed, and the cooling effect of this structure is comparatively analyzed. The results indicate that under extreme high-temperature conditions with ambient temperature conditions of 250°C and working oil temperature of 140 °C the DJSV exhibits an overall temperature ranging from 140°C to 233 °C. The highest temperature appears at the upper end of the torque motor shell. The temperature of the torque motor component exhibits a temperature gradient in the longitudinal direction, and ranges from143°C to 222°C. The torque motor exhibits a high overall temperature and significantly impacts the performance of the servo valve, which is a temperature-sensitive part. In response, a self-cooling structure is proposed, and the temperature distribution of the modified DJSV is analyzed. The analysis result indicates an overall temperature range reduced to 140 °C-182 °C, in which the temperature of the torque motor component effectively reduces to 140 °C-157 °C demonstrating the efficacy of the self-cooling structure. The analysis of the temperature field characteristic of the DJSV under extreme high-temperature conditions provides a theoretical basis for the design and manufacture of the DJSV.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: The Research on Spray Trajectory Planning Issues Digest
conference_papers.summary: The problem of glaze coating spraying is one of the problems faced in the production practice. Uniform glaze coating can greatly improve the quality and aesthetic degree of ceramics, so how to spray evenly has become an important research object. For the material with smooth surface, we analyzed the spraying situation of the spray gun on the single point and single line, drew the spraying situation of the spray gun on a line, and determined the translation distance interval according to the actual needs, and calculated the best translation distance by enumeration method. For the surface, obviously the calculation formula for the plane is not applicable to the surface, we use the projection principle, through the reference surface area element to establish the surface area element, and finally determine the surface area thickness. Finally, the optimal translation distance is obtained.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: The Mechanical Designing Process of Proposed Ventilation System For Home Environments
conference_papers.summary: The research began with general idea to look regards to ventilation system performance in Malaysia. Ventilation is the mechanical system in a building that acquires “new” open air and evacuates the “defiled” indoor air. Ventilation system utilized to control disclosure to airborne contaminants. It is usually use to evacuate contaminants, for example, exhaust, cleans, and vapours. There are fundamental factors that need to be considered. The customer criteria were collected in Klang Valley through survey and interview. The conceptual design was selected by using morphological diagram and was translated to SOLIDWORK. There are four conceptual designs were generated. The confirmation result was gained by using Ansys, to stimulate, to run and able to verify that this product design will run automatically when the enclosed room temperature at 27°C to 30°C. Objective to reduce the waste of electricity and maintain the enclosed room temperature.
