A fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is used for adjusting gain values of trajectory tracking control and balance recovery control according to the magnitude of external disturbances. For the ankle and hip strategies, ankle and hip torques are calculated using the CP criteria to avoid balance loss. For the step strategy, the controller computes footholds to maintain the desired Center of Mass (CoM) velocity against external disturbances. A simulation was conducted on a 3D quadruped robot to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed controller. Forces in both longitudinal and lateral directions were applied to the robot body, with the controller active and inactive. The simulation results showed that the controller reduced CP, CoM position, and CoM velocity errors in both directions. The results demonstrate that the controller, which integrates hip, ankle, and step strategies, improves a quadruped robot's trajectory following and balance recovering capabilities.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Large Eddy Simulation Study on the Sub-Grid Scale Model Constant Value Relationship in Homogeneous Steady Turbulence based on Large Scale Turbulence Structures
conference_papers.summary: This study presents a relationship between values of model constants of two sub-grid scale (SGS) models, the Smagorinsky and Vreman models, in large-eddy simulation (LES). This relationship, already presented in the previous study, is examined using a statistically steady isotropic turbulence field. A value of the model constants can be varied to the spatial scale of the external force field that maintains turbulence. The present values of the two model constants for each condition are calculated by calibrating with those obtained using a spectral method with identical turbulence field conditions. A functional form of the relationship between these values of the two model constants agreed with that of the previous study. However, obtained values of the coefficient of it were significantly different. The present study considers that this result implies that a value of the coefficients in the relationship between the model constants may depend on in turbulence fields.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: LES Analysis on the Impact of Mass Conservation Uncertainty on the Static Pressure Fluctuation in Spatially Periodic Steady Turbulence
conference_papers.summary: This study investigates the effect of mass-conserving uncertainty on the static pressure fluctuation characteristics in incompressible isotropic steady turbulence. The mass conservation uncertainty can be produced by relaxing the convergence of the Poisson equation solved in the fractional stages. This mass-conserving uncertainty may often be found acceptable in fluid analysis. In incompressible flows, the mass conservation uncertainty is quantified as the spatial variation RMS of the velocity divergence. The analysis is analyzed as a large-eddy simulation, and the SGS components are modelled using the Smagorinsky and coherent structure models. First, the steady-state turbulence generated in the case without mass-conserving uncertainty is tested to be independent of the differences between these SGS models. Then the spatial fluctuation RMS of the velocity divergence is validated to be significant.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Kinematics Analysis and Trajectory Planning of UR5 Robot
conference_papers.summary: With the expansion of the application scope of robot technology, the technical requirements are getting higher and higher. In order to achieve the precise control and trajectory planning of the robot, the kinematics and dynamics problems need to be studied. In this paper, the forward and reverse kinematics equations of UR5 robot are established by D-H method. The dynamics of the manipulator are analyzed using the Lagrange method. Utilizing the cubic polynomial interpolation method, the trajectory of linear motion is planned, and the linear motion trajectory is jointly simulated and analyzed based on ADAMS and MATLAB. The curves of angle, angular velocity, angular acceleration and torque with time are obtained. These findings establish the theoretical groundwork for future research on the precise control of the manipulator.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Kinematic Analysis of 6-RSS Parallel Robot Designed for Assisting Cervical Laminectomy
conference_papers.summary: Cervical laminectomy is a kind of clinical surgery mainly used for decompression of a cervical vertebrate. Because of the limited space of the cervical vertebrate, this surgery requires surgeons to operate in a higher degree of accuracy. A robot-assisted surgery can always achieve good accuracy by virtue of precise positioning and operation of the robot, and a parallel robot can perform better accuracy due to its mechanism feature. A 6-RSS has a more concise structure and lower mass of moving parts than other types of parallel robots, thus it performs better in human-machine interaction which could guarantee precise operations of surgeons. But kinematic analysis of a 6-RSS parallel robot is normally more complicated than other types. In this paper, the theoretical mechanism model of the 6-RSS parallel robot was built and coordinates were defined. The kinematic model was derived based on the closed-loop kinematic chain. The dexterity indices were analyzed to facilitate the design process of the robot.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: IoT-Based Automation for Spray Painting in Aerospace Manufacturing
conference_papers.summary: The use of industrial automation has seen a rise in the manufacturing industries in recent years. Spray painting is one of the tasks suitable for industrial automation implementation as it is a task that requires a steady repetitive motion during execution. This paper aims to design an automated spray painter system to be used in the aerospace manufacturing industry, as well as to further automate the environment the automated spray painter works in to create an integrated automated environment which can function with minimal human support. With the proper design, devices and communication protocol, an automated environment with collaborative robots can be achieved within an aerospace manufacturing facility.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Investigating the 5G Handover in Autonomous Mobile Robotic Applications
conference_papers.summary: In industrial automation, Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) applications have been widely integrated into facilities to improve manufacturing, productivity, and flexibility of productive areas. These advancements are largely attributed to wireless connectivity such as 5G or Wi-Fi. The unlicensed networks such as Wi-Fi, currently face performance issues due to elec-tromagnetic interferences from other overlapping neighboring networks and therefore cannot guarantee reliability or scalability for such a mission-critical task. This raises the question of whether 5G could be the wireless technology to drive the expected digital transformation. To ensure the stability of connectivity for seamless operations, it is crucial to investigate whether the handover in 5G, which differs significantly from traditional Wi-Fi procedures, is suitable for the productive environment. The handover in mobile networks such as 5G is understood to be the transfer of the connection from one cell to another. For example, in productive environments, the handover is required when the AMR moves between different halls with multiple small cells and needs to be reconnected to another cell for a better signal quality. This paper addresses this issue and presents an exemplary investigation, in which the handover is monitored for an AMR application. Our results show that the handover process is completed without any detectable delay or packet loss during the data transmission. The results also indicate that the use of a 5G campus network could be a key enabler for the implementation of mission-critical tasks and give insights into the potential of 5G for AMR applications in industrial automation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Monitoring Technology for the Impact of Deep Foundation Pit Excavation on Adjacent Facilities
conference_papers.summary: Selecting a typical archaeological construction field, based on water system and hydrogeololgy conditions on the site, monitoring technology and numerical calculation were used to simulate the foundation settlement and deformation values of existing buildings during the excavation construction process. This research concluded that the settlement differences did not exceed the standard limit. It also showed that the monitoring values are consistent with the numerical calculation values. The purpose is to detect construction safety and ensure the normal use of adjacent buildings after the completion of archaeological projects. The research can provide construction reference for the restoration of ancient city, moat dredging, relics excavation and urban infrastructure.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Innovative Approaches to Tourism Demand Prediction: A Genetic Algorithm Perspective
conference_papers.summary: This paper emphasizes the importance of tourism demand forecasting, particularly in the context of sustainable development. It uses AI tools and machine learning to explore linear regression models and their optimization using Genetic Algorithms (GAs). In spite of the fact that GAs have been applied in a wide range of fields, their application in tourism research still needs to be explored. The primary objective of this study involves a comparative analysis of three distinct methodologies: LR-GA, linear regression implemented using SPSS Statistics, and linear regression implemented using SASe This comparative evaluation aims to provide insights into the efficacy of these methods in addressing challenges relevant to the field of tourism. Additionally, the study seeks to investigate the potential contributions of genetic operators, namely the blend crossover and elitism selection mechanisms, in enhancing the predictive accuracy and overall performance of LR-GA. The results showcase the superior performance of the LR-GA algorithm, highlighting its potential for generating accurate predictive outcomes and facilitating informed decision-making in the tourism sector. The comprehensive presentation of the research methodology, findings, and their implications serves to advance the field's predictive capabilities and decision-making processes, fostering sustainable and data-driven practices within the tourism industry.
institutions: University of Technology and Applied Sciences-Suhar
University of Technology and Applied Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Indoor Following Model Based on TDOA Positioning and Q-Learning Algorithm
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents an indoor tracking algorithm model designed specifically for the unique scenario of supermarkets. Firstly, the UWB positioning technology is utilized to replace the RFID radio frequency positioning due to its superior performance in all aspects. Additionally, to account for the vast area of supermarkets, the TDOA algorithm is employed to cluster and combine all UWB positioning base stations, thereby reducing non-line-of-sight errors and improving the overall positioning accuracy. Furthermore, the supermarket is abstracted into a two-dimensional plane with insurmountable obstacles, and the Q-learning algorithm and its improved version are utilized to obtain the optimal and suboptimal paths between two points in the supermarket, which can be used to determine the general direction of travel. In the event of obstacles along the travel path, the DWA algorithm is employed to perform local dynamic obstacle avoidance, ultimately achieving the goal of shopping cart tracking.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Improvement and Application of a Fire Alarm Method for Building
conference_papers.summary: The current building fire intelligent alarm system relies on single point abnormal signal analysis to generate alarm behavior, which is often affected by signal interference, resulting in low efficiency. This paper proposes an optimized and improved method for building fire alarms. carries out sensor beam collection on the sensing information, and test the connectivity of the sensing information of the building's intelligent fire alarm system; sort the sensing beam signals through spectrum decomposition and feature separation, and extract the accurate feature quantity of the transmission signals of the building intelligent fire alarm system; uses multidimensional wavelet decomposition method for transmission signal identification, in combination with joint tracking and detection of the sensor information to realize fire alarm. The experimental results show that the accuracy of using the improved method for building fire alarms is between$90{\mathrm{\% }}$and$98\%$, and the signal processing capacity is significantly enhanced compared with before the improvement, and the overall has application advantages.
institutions: Inner Mongolia Technical University of Construction

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Improved Mapping Technique Based on ORB-SLAM2 in Dynamic Scenes
conference_papers.summary: At present, in the simultaneous localization and map construction (SLAM) algorithm, the more mature technology is the map construction in the static environment. However, there are currently moving objects in most environments, which will affect the accuracy and integrity of slam mapping. In this paper, we propose an improved vision SLAM based on ORB-SLAM2 that adds an independent parallel target detection thread to effectively filter low dynamic objects in the scene. Finally, we conduct an experimental evaluation using the TUM dataset, and the results show that our algorithm has a great improvement over ORB-SLAM2 in positioning accuracy and running time.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Implementation of a Wireless Mesh Network for Orienteering Monitoring
conference_papers.summary: Characterized by complex organization on crucial terrains for the numerous competitors, Orienteering activities are facing formidable safety challenges during training and competitions sessions. A robust communication network is crucial need for Orienteering organization progress management and control, timely emergency treatment, and comprehensive data analysis. Referring to the Longley-Rice model, theoretical calculations for equipment selection and network coverage capacity of a Wireless Mesh Network were conducted. Feasibility of a two-tiered backbone-access network structure was validated through network design and communication capability test. The safety management level of the Orienteering events was enhanced obviously through Orienteering monitoring on the structure of a self-configuring Wireless Mesh Network. The athletics abilities of Orienteering candidates were improved significantly with the support of the data analysis obtained through Wireless Mesh Network.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Human Behavior Analysis in Virtual Environment for Human-Robot Collaboration
conference_papers.summary: With the rapid development of robot technology, there will be more and more opportunities for humans and robots to work together in the future. In order to enable robots and humans to better complete collaborative tasks, the analysis of human behavior is very important. Robots should make up for the lack of human work ability. weak parts, thereby helping humans complete tasks quickly and efficiently. This article designed three tasks of different difficulty through the VR simulation system and recorded the behavioral patterns of a single operator, thereby analyzing the tendency of people to ignore corners and other obscure locations during the search task, and to analyze the range that they have already inspected. Lack of clarity and subjective judgments are too obvious and lead to mission failure. At the same time, we compared the different performances of human behavior in human-machine collaborative tasks, and compared and analyzed various data, and concluded that robots are of little help to humans in simple tasks, robots can help to a certain extent in general tasks, and robots in difficult tasks will compensate for humans. Subjective thinking defects lead to higher task completion.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Green Time Extension Method of Transit Signal Priority Control for Phase Overlapping Intersection
conference_papers.summary: Aiming at the transit priority control problem under the existence of phase overlapping constraints at signalized intersection, this paper proposes a green time extension method based on non-linear programming. On the basis of the traditional ring-barrier, an improved phase signal timing structure is proposed to address the issue of overlapping. Further, a non-linear programming model for green time extension is presented, in which the objective function aims to optimize the transit priority effect while minimize the adjustments required for non-transit phases, and the constrains include minimum green time, maximum green time, overlapping rules and migration of coordinated phase. The numerical analysis results indicate that under the constraint of a fixed overlapping duration of 4 seconds and the existence of phase coordination, the proposed method can extend the green time for transit priority phases by 166.7% more than the traditional timing scheme. Moreover, the standard deviation of green time adjustments for non-transit phases is reduced by 43.1% compared to the traditional timing scheme under the same extension effect.
institutions: Shandong University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Grasping Control of Planar Mechanical Claw
conference_papers.summary: The topic of our research is the grasping strategy of a planner two-joint mechanical claw. Our inspiration comes from a paper on the grasping strategy of soft things by a rigid mechanical hand. If we can get the force sensor's accurate data, how can we process these data to grasp an object correctly? In order to achieve our goal, we built a model of a mechanical hand on Matlab with two joints for each finger. We calculate many functions to process the data and simulate the model. With this model, we get our results. We get the evaluation of parameters alpha1 and alpha2, L, and tau. We increase the robustness of the entry of L. The mechanical claw can grasp a ball steadily and reach the stable point faster.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Gaussian and Non-Gaussian Information Based Hydraulic Component Internal Leakage Fault Diagnosis
conference_papers.summary: Internal leakage is primary fault mode of hydraulic components, typically caused by seal failure or damage. However, the fluid inside hydraulic components exhibits complex motion characteristics, and its external vibration signals often have intricate distributions, making fault diagnosis challenging. This paper focuses on the internal leakage of hydraulic directional valve and proposes a fault diagnosis method based on Gaussian and N on-Gaussian information. First, time and frequency domain features are extracted from the vibration signals of the hydraulic directional valve. Then, the correlation between internal leakage and signal features is analyzed. Finally, Gaussian and Non-Gaussian information is extracted based on the correlated signal features, and these are used to construct statistics for detecting the presence of internal leakage. In complex data distribution scenarios for fault diagnosis, this method offers a novel solution without requiring a large number of fault samples or complex parameter optimization. Experimental studies validate the performance of this method, demonstrating that it outperforms several classical fault diagnosis methods in terms of robustness and accuracy. This research provides an effective approach for detecting internal leakage faults in hydraulic directional valves.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Functional Safety Fault Diagnosis Strategy for Electric Vehicle VCU Based on Random Forest and Hidden Markov Model
conference_papers.summary: In order to solve the frequent occurrence of road vehicle functional safety problems and the imperfect fault diagnosis mechanism of electric vehicle controller, this paper proposes a vehicle control unit (VCU) functional safety fault diagnosis strategy based on Random Forest and Hidden Markov Model. The vehicle operation process is described as a Hidden Markov stochastic process, and feature screening is carried out with the help of Random Forest. The implicit relationship model between the functional safety fault of the VCU and the change of the characteristic signal under the vehicle fault state is established and the fault diagnosis is solved. Using the constructed HIL simulation test environment, the diagnosis and verification of six functional safety faults of accelerator pedal to ground short circuit, accelerator pedal opening signal is not accurate, brake pedal to ground short circuit, brake pedal opening signal is not accurate, application layer software logic fault and MCU power supply abnormal are realized. The results show that the proposed diagnostic strategy has an average diagnostic rate of 90.1%, which can effectively diagnose different types of functional safety faults.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Framework for Evaluating Path Accuracy in UAV Indoor Operations
conference_papers.summary: In recent years, there has been an increased focus on using UAV s indoors. Businesses and academic institutions are now developing UAV s for a variety of purposes, such as inspection, security, inventory management, and transporting small goods. The publication presents a framework designed to evaluate path accuracy in indoor UAV operations. The framework uses open-source platforms, integrates a motion capture system, and makes use of advanced communication methods such as Wi-Fi 6 and 5G. It was developed in ROS2 for its robust tools and low-latency advantages. Additionally, it employs Gazebo for flight simulation and features a customized graphical interface for UAV control. The study also highlights the lack of standardized measuring techniques for position and path accuracy in UAV operations. The aim is to contribute to the evolution of UAV technology by analyzing the possibility of creating performance criteria for UAV s, similar to the standards established in industrial robots. Furthermore, the paper provides a detailed explanation of the system's architecture, hardware components, and software implementation. Validation tests are presented to assess the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed framework.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Formulation of the Necessary Conditions for Optimality for a Parameter Dependent Optimal Control Problem Evolving on a Principal Fibre Bundle
conference_papers.summary: The main objective of this research is the presentation of a maximisation of payload haulage by use of UAV for payload spraying purposes of a pesticide in a regular field. Optimal control from principles of calculus of variations is applied to formulate the maximisation problem. The variable payload models the parameter dependant UAV. The system evolves on a principle fibre bundle on a SE(3) x S2manifold necessitating a from principles calculus of variations optimal formulation which is the key contribution of this paper. An illustrative spraying example is used to demonstrate a maximal pesticide spraying problem. Future work will include the formulation of optimal control problems on the semi-direct function Manifold

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Fluid-Structure Coupling Simulation of the Main Drive Seal in Shield Machine
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents a fluid-structure coupling simulation (FSC) method for the main drive seal in a shield machine. The method is based on the simulation of hyper-elastic material deformation and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). It involves obtaining the fluid field model using predefined pressure and obtaining actual pressures through CFD simulations. The method iteratively updates the fluid field model based on the actual pressures to determine the final clearance of the seal ring under actual working conditions. The calculated results show that the opening pressure of the seal ring is 0.043 MPa, and the opening clearance of the seal ring under the working conditions is 0.2 mm. This analysis provides a reference to guide the lubricant dosage, verify the seal ring shape and structure, and assess the feasibility of achieving an effective seal for the main drive.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Fish Detection and Classification Based on Improved ViT
conference_papers.summary: It is crucial for marine researchers and preservationists to routinely evaluate the relative abundance of fish species in their environments and monitor changes in their populations. Different automated computer-based fish sampling systems in underwater videos have been offered instead of arduous hand sampling. However, no ideal solution exists for automated fish identification and species classification. This is mainly because of the challenges involved in filming underwater, such as varying light levels, fish concealment, changing backgrounds, murky water, limited resolution, intricate backgrounds, fish shape distortions, obstruction from other water bodies, and subtle differences among specific fish species. The proposed method uses an improved vision transformer (IMViT) for detection and classification. To capture the inductive bias information from images, the traditional ViT model incorporates the convolutional and residual units of ResNet to improve the architecture of the ViT model when working with a small-scale dataset. Our results reveal that deep learning (DL) models can detect and classify species using underwater fish images and obtain considerable results. “Fish-Dataset” is used for evaluations. This method corroborates significantly more discrimination accuracy ameliorations than the previously proposed techniques. The proposed model may be used for various underwater objects in light of the experimental findings.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Feature Decoupled of Deep Mutual Information Maximization
conference_papers.summary: In deep learning, supervised learning techniques usually require a large amount of expensive labeled data to train the network, and the feature representations extracted by the model usually mix multiple attributes, resulting in feature representations that are difficult to decouple and are non-interpretable, which restricts the application and development of deep learning techniques, and for this reason, it is particularly important to study decoupled feature representation methods for unsupervised learning. Although the Learning deep representations by mutual information estimation and maximization (DIM) method achieves excellent results in unsupervised learning, the feature representations learned by the DIM method still suffer from the problem of difficult decoupling. decoupling problem. To address this problem, we minimize the mutual information between the intermediate layer feature representations learned by the hidden layer of the encoder during the encoder training process, so that the features learned by each filter are as uncorrelated as possible, thus realizing feature decoupling, and our method is called FP-DIM. Finally, the effectiveness of the FP-DIM method is verified on the CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Fashion-MNIST datasets. The experiments show that our proposed FP-DIM method is more significant for the learned decouplable middle layer feature representation. Finally, we also propose a reflection of future research for the FP-DIM method, aiming to provide a research idea and direction for solving unsupervised interpretable machine learning and to lay a solid theoretical and application foundation for machine learning fields such as image classification and migration learning.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Evaluation of Vibrotactile Glove and Handheld Controller in a Visuo-Haptic VR Space Station
conference_papers.summary: Using virtual reality technology, we can simulate the microgravity environment of the outer space for popularizing the space science. Compared with handheld controllers, we expect using a glove with localized vibrotactile feedback might be more efficient and natural for simulating grasping gestures for space roaming and 3D-objects manipulating, however, quantitative and qualitative effects remain unknown. Thus, this study developed a science popularization orientated visuo-haptic VR space station for elucidating the difference between the two interaction devices. We used the number of times of trying to grasp, success grasping rate, and total time of completing the roaming task to objectively describe the interacting efficiency. The results of subjective rating showed better motion intuitiveness and vibrotactile fidelity using the vibrotactile glove, however, quantitative results showed using the glove was less efficient as compared to using the handheld controller. So, analyses of the underlying reasons were performed in aspects of both hardware and software. The findings may provide suggestions for designing VR interacting devices for space science popularization.
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Virtual Reality Technology and Systems

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Evaluation of Global Sizes and Cylindricity Errors Based on fminimax Optimization Function
conference_papers.summary: Based on the evaluation definitions of minimum circumscribed, maximum inscribed and minimum zone methods for global sizes and cylindricity errors of cylinder, the optimization objective function of the axis parameters of the reference cylindrical surfaces and the evaluation models of global sizes and cylindricity errors were built. The subprograms for the optimization objective functions of the axis parameters of the reference cylindrical surfaces and the evaluation of global sizes and cylindricity errors were written by using Matlab language. The roundness profiles of four cylindrical samples were extracted, and their global sizes and cylindricity errors were evaluated based on least square, minimum circumscribed, maximum inscribed and minimum zone methods. The evaluation results of the optimization characteristic values of fminimax optimization function were compared with those evaluated by using other optimization methods, and it turned out that the accuracy of the optimization objective characteristic values of fminimax optimization function are higher or equal to those evaluated by other optimization methods, which is suitable to the application in the evaluation of global sizes and cylindricity errors.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Evaluation and Optimization Design of Road Traffic Markings Based on Understanding
conference_papers.summary: The proper implementation of traffic marking is crucial for ensuring traffic safety. Insufficient comprehension of marking is a major contributing factor to frequent road traffic accidents. This study aims to clearly define and evaluate the understandability of traffic marking from a design perspective, taking into account both driver characteristics and the design itself. The Q-type clustering method of cluster analysis and SPSS software were employed to obtain clustering analysis results. Through an intra-group homogeneity test, the understanding level of traffic marking was ultimately categorized into three levels: A, B, and C. Additionally, this paper summarizes the relevant indicators, principles, and guidelines for graphic symbol design. By conducting an importance evaluation using factor analysis methodology, three types of design factors (layout rationality, visualization, and appearance style) comprising a total of 12 indicators were identified. The weightage for each factor was calculated in order to determine their relative importance in optimized design factors. Based on these findings regarding the factors influencing the understandability of traffic marking designs, an optimization design approach for traffic markings is proposed herein. Finally, by utilizing examples such as tide lane lines and no-turn markings, optimization designs are implemented with subsequent effect evaluations demonstrating significant improvements in the understanding level of traffic markings after optimization – thus validating the effectiveness of this proposed method.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Equivalence Among PID and Several Robust Control Methods with Application to Motor Control
conference_papers.summary: This paper explores the equivalence among proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control and several robust control methods, including an adaptive backstepping control, an improved backstepping control, “P+PI” control and a quasi-sliding mode control, in time domain. It can be concluded that all the discussed robust control methods can be reconstructed in PID form. Experimental results of a servo motor control system verify the equivalence among PID and the discussed robust control methods.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Ensemble Deep Learning NARX for Estimating Time Series of Earthquake Occurrence
conference_papers.summary: Predicting earthquake occurrences in time series data remains a challenging task in seismology. NARX (Nonlinear Autoregressive with eXogenous input) neural networks have recently shown promise for accurate predictions. While previous research has demonstrated NARX's effectiveness in estimating earthquake frequencies, the architecture still relies on several pre-determined parameters. These parameters include the number of hidden layers, number of neurons, and delay time. This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of Ensemble Deep Learning NARX neural networks in predicting time series of earthquakes. The proposed ensemble model integrates multiple NARX neural networks, each trained on a distinct subset of earthquake data. This approach aims to enhance prediction accuracy and bolster model robustness. The dataset consists of time series records detailing earthquake occurrence frequencies and magnitudes. The results show performance evaluation metrics in terms of Mean Square Error (MSE) values. For training frequency data, the MSE is 4.10e-26, and for testing, it is 6.05e-22. Regarding training magnitude data, the MSE is 2.86e-21 for training and 3.17e-19 for testing. This study makes a valuable contribution to the advancement of earthquake prediction techniques, underscoring the potential of Ensemble Deep Learning NARX neural networks for precise time series estimation in seismology.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Enhancing Electromechanical Coupling: A Modified Model for Studying Uterine Myometrial Contraction
conference_papers.summary: The mechanism of uterine electromyographic signals and mechanical contractions is a significant research topic. In this study, we propose a novel electromechanical model that utilizes the FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) model to simulate the enhanced excitability of uterine cells influenced by hormones, leading to the successful generation of pacemaker behavior upon the introduction of small perturbations. Furthermore, we observe that as pregnancy progresses, enhanced gap junction, anchoring junction, and electromechanical coupling activity contributes to global mechanical contraction synchronization. Our research results also demonstrate a considerable level of synchronization between electrical and mechanical signals, providing robust theoretical support for the practical application of electrical signals. These findings deepen our understanding of electromechanical coupling effects and offer new perspectives for research and applications in related fields.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Efficient Semantic-Aware TSDF Mapping with Adaptive Resolutions
conference_papers.summary: Mapping unknown environments based on vision sensors is a key step for robot planning. Existing methods usually adopt a fixed resolution to store the occupancy information. A high resolution consumes excessive computational resources while a low one results in unbearable information loss of specific user-interested regions that require precise representation. To address these challenges, we develop an efficient semantic-aware Truncated Signed Distance Function (TSDF) mapping system with adaptive resolutions. Our map representation consists of multiple layers with different voxel sizes. Meanwhile, with the assistance of semantic segmentation or object detection models, we identify key objects in the scene and use higher resolutions for their reconstruction. Semantic information can guide the selection of map resolution and also potentially provide valuable insights for more complex user-defined navigation tasks. By leveraging our lightweight implementation, our system achieves real-time computation and less memory consumption than existing frameworks.
institutions: Shanghai Key Laboratory of Navigation and Location Based Services

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: EEG Based Imagined Word Recognition Using CNN-Bi-GRU
conference_papers.summary: A notable advancement in brain-computer interface (BCI) for the benefit of the speech-impaired community based on EEG led many insights for imagined speech. This study addresses challenges in translating brain-computer interface (BCI) advancements for speech-impaired individuals using EEG. Existing neural speech decoding methods, despite progress, face classification accuracy issues. The proposed solution combines a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) and a bi-directional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) for improved classification. The systematic approach includes EEG signal preprocessing with bandpass and notch filters, power spectral density analysis, and coherence analysis for cognitive speech task-related EEG topography. The integrated CNN and Bi-GRU enhance memory capacity and classification. Simulation results show the system effectively detects four words with an 88 % recognition rate, surpassing previous performance benchmarks.
institutions: Cochin University of Science and Technology
Kerala University of Digital Sciences, Innovation and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Occupancy Grid Map Update Method using Camera and LiDAR Object Detection for Autonomous Driving
conference_papers.summary: For safe autonomous driving, cameras are widely utilized to detect and classify objects, whereas light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides accurate distance information for objects. In this study, we employed cameras and LiDAR to obtain three-dimensional (3D) bounding box information, such as class information, and the position and orientation of the objects using deep learning-based recognition techniques. Among various methods for representing the surrounding environment, the dynamic occupancy grid map (DOGM) has the advantage of representing the dynamic and static states of each object. However, utilizing only the DOGM increases the difficulty of considering the class information of each object. Herein, we utilized 3D bounding box information as input values to construct DOGM, including semantic information. Specifically, we applied the Dempster-Shafer theory of evidence-based combination rules to update the semantic information of the grid cell. Additionally, the developed methods are verified using the nuScenes public data sets, including camera and lidar measurements.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Dynamic Characteristics of Flow Limiting Valve for Hydrogen Fuel Cell Vehicles
conference_papers.summary: In the hydrogen supply system of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles, flow limiting valves play a crucial role in preventing significant hydrogen leakage in the event of accidents, greatly enhancing safety. This study established a mathematical model that considers changes in port opening, to analyze the dynamic characteristics of the flow limiting valve. A slope signal is used to simulate pressure changes in the valve when pipe ruptures occur, and the initial pressure value is obtained from Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation results. It is found that the structural parameters are closely related to its design indexes. Specifically, when the downstream pressure remains the same, an increase in the cone angle of the spool, valve body diameter, and damping orifice diameter enhances the valve's flow capacity, leading to a larger closure flow rate, but results in a decreased response speed. Changes in the conical valve structure have a more pronounced impact on the operational characteristics of the flow limiting valve.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Dual-Path Neural Networks Enabled Fetal ECG Extractions From Abdominal Electrohysterograpgy
conference_papers.summary: Fetal heart monitoring is crucial for the early detection of potential risks to fetal health conditions. However, the non-invasive fetal heart monitoring technology using maternal abdominal electrocardiography (AECG) is susceptible to interference from maternal electrocardiography (MECG) and multi-source noise. To address the above challenge, we propose a novel Dual-path Encoder-Decoder Model to extract fetal electrocardiography (FECG) signals from maternal abdominal recordings. It can effectively separate and remove MECG interference to obtain FECG. Additionally, a Feature Augmentation Module based on attention-guided is introduced to optimize the quality of the remaining features after MECG removal. Finally, the optimized features are fed into a decoder with external skip connections to reconstruct the FECG signal. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves outstanding performance on two public datasets, providing an effective solution for fetal health monitoring and assisting physicians in diagnosing fetal abnormalities.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: DiversityScanner-360°: An Automated System for Digitizing Invertebrate Bulk Samples
conference_papers.summary: Digitization of natural history collections opens many opportunities for research. Some of the data and information stored in the physical collections are made accessible without the need to move fragile specimens. In addition, digi-tized specimens allow for automated analysis, for example, with machine learning methods. Despite the enormous advantage of digitization, most specimens in natural history collections (e.g., insects) remain undigitized. One of the reasons is that the existing techniques for digitization are very time-consuming and labor-intensive, especially for small objects such as invertebrates and in particular for small specimens less than three millimeters in size. They have to be imaged with high-resolution cameras from multiple angles to capture important morphological features. Therefore, we developed the DiversityScanner-360°, which allows for the automated imaging of invertebrates from multiple directions. These images can then be used for taxonomic work or as training data for machine learning applications. Multiple focal planes can be imaged and processed into one image to obtain in-focus images of the specimens. The number of perspectives and focal planes is set by the user and adapted to individual cases. In particular, the DiversityScanner-360° offers a new way for digitizing invertebrates preserved in ethanol, leading to new discoveries and a deeper understanding of the world's biodiversity.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Discrimination of the Near-Fault Pulse-Like Seismic Motions Based on Convolutional Neural Network
conference_papers.summary: Identification of near-fault pulse-like seismic motions are an important part of engineering seismic design. In recent years, the rapidly developing deep learning algorithm, with its powerful data feature mining and image recognition ability, can quickly and accurately constrain the attributes of earthquake events. By inputting seismic wave data and seismic time-frequency data, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to obtain the waveform and spectral features of the seismic events, thereby constructing an automatic classification network model based on the CNN algorithm for near-fault pulse-like earthquakes and non-near-fault pulse-like earthquakes. Based on the observed data of near-fault pulse earthquakes and non-near-fault pulse-like earthquakes recorded in the NGA-West2 strong-motion database, a deep learning training model is constructed and the model is trained to determine known near-fault pulse earthquakes. The results show that the CNN based on time-frequency data has a high recognition accuracy, with a recognition rate of up to 91.59%.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Digital Process Design and Simulation of Slush Molding Based on Tecnomatix
conference_papers.summary: In the product development process, manufacturing flexibility requirements continue to increase, and with the emergence and development of digital twin technology, virtual scenes can be created to observe, analyze, and predict data. Compared with traditional models, the risk is lower and the investment cost is lower. The slush molding process is one of the important processes in the production of automotive interiors, and the difficulty of improving the process is particularly prominent. Based on the Tecnomatix Plant Simulation software, this paper digitally designed the slush molding process, built the corresponding simulation model and logic program, and carried out the production scheduling simulation according to the production work order; then used the simulation experiment method to optimize the process parameters, and after comparing the simulated production capacity data with the actual production capacity, the accuracy of the model is verified, and finally, the production capacity prediction under different production requirements can be realized, which can effectively reduce the cost of process improvement.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Diet Planning Models Based on Linear Programming Theory for Catering Problems
conference_papers.summary: As residents attach more and more importance to healthy diet, the catering problem has garnered widespread public attention. Nutrient-based dietary planning can give viable dietary recommendations for the above problems. In this paper, this study establishes a dietary planning model to find the minimum dietary expenditure under the condition that the daily nutritional requirements of diabetic patients are met and the upper limit of nutrient intake is not exceeded. Employing a dependable mathematical model, we make viable planning for diverse social groups and varied food materials, so as to give viable recommendations to the greatest extent.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Detecting Communities in Signed Networks based on Structural Balance Theory and Graph Convolution Network
conference_papers.summary: Singed networks describe the positive and negative interactions between components in real complex systems, contain rich information and are helpful to comprehensively and deeply mine connection patterns between individuals. It is a challenging task to detect the community structure accurately and quickly in a signed network. In this paper, we propose a community detection algorithm based on convex non-negative matrix factorization and graph convolutional neural network to extract communities from signed networks, which combines the aggregation process of graph convolutional networks with structural balance theory to make better use of the positive and negative connections, and designs a loss function combining the relaxed modularity and graph regularization to train the model in an end-to-end fashion. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by experiments on artificial networks and real networks.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of a Vehicle-level Test System for In-vehicle Emergency Call System
conference_papers.summary: The in-vehicle emergency call system has the ability to decrease the waiting time for assistance following a car crash, resulting in a decreased fatality rate for road accidents. According to domestic and international regulations, it is necessary for the system to undergo comprehensive testing to ensure its reliability prior to being utilized in vehicles. The whole vehicle triggering characteristics serve as the final evaluation in the certification process, requiring strict testing and verification to guarantee the technology's maturity and dependability. This paper presents a vehicle-level test system designed to meet vehicle-level test requirements. The system was tested from four perspectives, including in-vehicle system (IVS) triggering characteristics, minimum set of data (MSD) correctness, positioning accuracy, and voice call quality. The experimental results indicate that the testing system effectively tests the whole vehicle triggering characteristics of the in-vehicle emergency call system, thereby confirming its efficacy. The testing system can offer a budget-friendly and productive emergency call (eCall) certification testing solution to automobile companies. Additionally, it can provide substantial technical and data support for the creation of mandatory standards in China. Consequently, it promotes the expansion of related domains in China.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of a System for Near-Infrared Composite Spectral Image Acquisition and Information Processing
conference_papers.summary: The NIR camera is a device that captures images within the near-infrared spectral range, typically operating wavelengths from 700nm to 2500nm. The camera can possess exceptional penetrating capability and achieve multi-functions, making it a prominent subject of research and application in the industrial sector. The paper provides the system for near-infrared composite spectral image acquisition and information processing which is based on the Alvium 1800 U-130 VSWIR camera by Allied Vision. The system leverages QT Creator to establish an efficient and robust software platform with a user-friendly interface, facilitating NIR image acquisition and information processing across wavelengths ranging from 400 nm to 1700 nm. It is also equipped with narrow band filters for 940 nm, 1450 nm, and 1550 nm. The system effectively tackles challenges regarding the prevention of illegal copying, counterfeiting and infringement areas, detection of water content, differentiation of similar objects, and penetrability. Moreover, it offers practical applications in areas such as anti-counterfeiting measures, food safety assurance, and industrial processes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design of a Drone that Applies Multisensor Information for the Early Detection of Forest Fires
conference_papers.summary: The article focuses on the design and development of a drone equipped with advanced technology for the early detection of wildfires, a major threat to the environment, human life and property. Early detection is essential for effective response. This drone has multiple advanced sensors, including thermal cameras, high-resolution cameras and gas sensors, allowing it to continuously and accurately monitor forest areas. Its autonomous and programmable operation capability makes it an efficient tool for regular patrols over critical areas. The fire detection system is based on real-time analysis of thermal and high-resolution images captured by the drone. Computer vision algorithms process these images to identify early signs of fire, such as changes in temperature, smoke or presence of fire. When a potential fire is detected, the drone notifies authorities immediately. The advanced technology applied in this drone has the potential to save lives, reduce property damage and preserve the environment. This innovative approach to early wildfire detection shows great potential for the protection of vulnerable ecosystems and the safety of communities.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of a Drone System for Large Thermal Power Boiler Inspection
conference_papers.summary: Drones virtually immune to human survival and physiological limitations and physical injuries, and are capable of performing its intended tasks properly in dangerous, contaminated environments. We propose a drone localization and navigation system in the thermal power boiler. Multiple sensor fusion algorithms, such as UWB, lidar, and IMU, are used to locate and establish maps. The system has outstanding advantages in dusty, dark and vertical feature degradation thermal power boiler drone inspection missions. Moreover, considering that there are no complex and dense obstacles within the boiler, this system only designs a local planner to implement autonomous cruise control within the boiler, which supports initial coordinate system calibration and real-time heading control. Finally, we built a simulation platform to test several performances of the system and compared with traditional localization algorithms. The experimental results verify the feasibility of the multi-sensor fusion algorithm and the reliability of the trajectory planning navigation algorithm.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design of Universal Integrated Robot Joint and Its Applications in Multiple Fields
conference_papers.summary: This article mainly focuses on the design and prototype development of a universal integrated joint, and analyzes the design of the joint and the motor used. By verifying and optimizing weak materials such as enameled wires, heat shrink tubes, and lead wires, and applying them to the entire product, core components such as motors and rotary transformers can have a longer lifespan in complex environments. At the same time, universal interfaces are designed for joints to ensure that integrated joints can be widely used in various fields such as rehabilitation, medical exoskeletons, and nuclear industrial robots. Finally, practical use cases are provided in the article.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design of Enhanced Rotation Scheme for Dual-Axis Rotational Inertial Navigation System
conference_papers.summary: Dual-axis rotational inertial navigation system (RINS) compensates system error by rotating the inertial measurement unit (IMU) with two-axis. Reasonable rotation scheme properly removes the system errors caused by inertial sensors error without other additional error by the rotation. Therefore, rotation scheme is a dominant factor of RINS's performance. In this paper, we propose the enhanced rotation scheme, which consists of 24-position rotations. The performance of the proposed method is verified by a simulation for long term and compared to the conventional 16-position dual-axis rotation scheme as wells.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Verification of An Avalanche Photodiode Device for Rare Earth Fluorescence Detection
conference_papers.summary: The gain and spectral response range of photodiodes are very important for rare earth fluorescence detection. However, traditional photodiodes do not have internal gain, which cannot meet the requirements of the above fields. Therefore, an avalanche photodiode is designed and manufactured based on 0.18 μm CMOS process in this paper. N+/P-Well forms the avalanche multiplication region of the device, which is used for the detection of external photons. N-Well is used as the guard ring of the device to prevent the breakdown of the side junction of N+/P-Well. In addition, the principle of the device is verified based on Technology-Computer-Aided-Design (TCAD) simulation. The test results show that the avalanche breakdown voltage of the device is 11.7 V. When the reverse bias voltage is 11.7V, the dark current of the device is 9.8 × 10-9A, and the photocurrent of the device is 3.8 × 10-6A. The current after the avalanche breakdown of the device is 1 mA. The spectral response range of the device is 400 nm-1000 nm, the peak is 470 nm, and the responsivity is 6.7 A/W.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Design and Simulation of a 3-DOF Dexterous Joint Actuator Based on Multi-Drive Hierarchical Output and Spherical Rotation Mechanism
conference_papers.summary: Series-type and ball-and-socket are currently two typical architectures of hip joint actuators. However, they either rely on advancements and applications in materials science or compromise on structural design, failing to accurately mimic the motion of the human hip joint. Therefore, we designed a three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) dexterous joint actuator based on multi-drive hierarchical output and spherical rotation mechanism for better kinematics performance, high power density, and high load-withstand capability. Three identical motors were installed in parallel on the motor mounting frame, with two motors coupled and controlled a pair of differential bevel gears, while another motor transmitted torque through two spherical gears, coupled with a secondary frame mounted on a large bevel gear, ultimately achieving spherical rotation with a fixed point as the center. 3D simulations demonstrated that this new design could achieve a 120-degree rotation range across three degrees of freedom, with high load-withstand capability, successfully meeting project expectations and demonstrating its usability. This design closely approximated the overall performance of the human hip joint in terms of driving performance, motion characteristics, and control logic. It provides theoretical support for addressing existing engineering bottlenecks in joint actuators and has promising potential for various robotic applications.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of Yipai App Based on Artificial Intelligence Technology
conference_papers.summary: With the increasing popularity and upgrading of mobile phone cameras, the pixel, sensor, aperture, lens and software algorithms of mobile phone cameras are constantly iterative. Taking photos and sharing life has been integrated into our lives, but there are still many people who cannot master the photography skills proficiently and are at a loss in the face of taking photos, so the market demand for photo systems is large. “Yipai APP based on artificial intelligence technology” is a photo APP that guides users to take photos and provides booking and requesting photos. Its front-end is mainly developed by the system program using Java language, the back-end uses SQLite to store and manage data, and realizes artificial interaction by using natural language processing technology. Intelligent guidance is provided to users, and AI intelligent matching copy is performed on the photos taken. When the user does not want to take a selfie, this system also provides appointment service, of course, the photographer user can also publish help to take a post, looking for customers. Mobile phone photo APP has a broad prospect, and the function of easy APP is relatively rare in the photo market, which brings great opportunities and markets to the development of easy APP.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of Traffic Vehicle Image Recognition Module
conference_papers.summary: Due to the economic growth, the number of cars increased, the current urban congestion, traffic accident handling, vehicle parking management and other social pressure is greater. Under this social background, the research on traffic vehicle recognition has become one of the most popular research objects. How to effectively identify vehicle information is an important part of modern traffic management and safety, and the combination of OpenMV hardware and software module Micropython has brought more efficient and flexible solutions for the development of vehicle identification technology. OpenMV and Micropython can be used to build a vehicle identification system, which can recognize the appearance, model and color of the car in real time. Using OpenMV and Micropython can also realize real-time tracking and statistics of vehicles, providing more accurate and practical data support for traffic flow analysis and urban traffic management. The purpose of this design is to complete the collection and identification of vehicle information through OpenMV, complete the judgment of vehicle signals, determine whether it is a car, a bus or a bicycle, and realize the recognition function of vehicles. The combination of OpenMV hardware modules and Micropython brings a more efficient and flexible solution for the development of vehicle identification technology, which will play an important role in the future of intelligent transportation.
institutions: Chongqing College of Finance and Economics

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of Coal Mine Equipment Management System
conference_papers.summary: There are many types of mechanical and electrical equipment in coal mines, and the management tasks are heavy. In order to improve the management level and utilization efficiency of equipment, this paper analyzes the main requirements of coal mine electromechanical equipment management, designs a business process for cross-departmental full-cycle equipment management, and uses the software layered architecture design method to develop a coal mine equipment management system based on ASP.NET and MySQL database. The system realizes the dynamic management of equipment information, and provides reliable technical support for the online management and efficient maintenance of equipment.
institutions: China Coal Technology and Engineering Group Corp (China)

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: DADN: Data Augmentation-Driven Dual Network Framework for Node Classification
conference_papers.summary: Node classification is an important task in graph neural networks (GNNs), aiming to predict the category of nodes in the graph according to their neighbours and their own characteristics. Current methods mainly focus on one level of data augmentation, ignoring huge potential in other underlying levels. Furthermore, existing models cannot fully exploit the information contained in the existing data, which undermines the performance of node classification. In order to solve the above problems, we propose a novel Data Augmentation-driven Dual Network (DADN) framework. Specifically, we first design a composite data augmentation module that comprehensively considers the local neighborhood level, the node level, and the edge level to augment the original features. Then, we copy the original features and the augmented features into the dual network framework with dropout for model training to capture the innermost features. Finally, we experimentally evaluate our method on three real-world public datasets, and the results show that our method outperforms the baseline models in the node classification task, except for individual metrics.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Cylinder-Wheel Coupled Robot with Buttocks-Support Mechanism for Lower-Limb Rehabilitation Training
conference_papers.summary: Rehabilitation robot plays an increasingly important role in the treatment of spinal cord injuries for reducing the human surgeons' workload and meeting the rapidly growing clinical demands. However, extant treadmill-based rehabilitation robot presents challenges due to complicated gait generation mechanism and human-machine interaction mismatch. Hence, we designed a cylinder-wheel coupled medical robot for lower-limb rehabilitation training. The robot used a motorized track and two electric cylinders in each limb to match the patient's three joints rotation, and generated gait motion through the coordination of the left and right limbs. The robot employed a dynamic buttocks-support mechanism to reduce the patient's impedance torque during training, avoiding the use of a complex body weight support (BWS) system commonly used in existing rehabilitation robots. 3D simulation results demonstrated the high usability of this novel design in gait generation, showing promising potential to solve the bottlenecks that emerged in treadmill-based rehabilitation robots.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Cracking Causes of Dissimilar Steel Butt Joint of a High Temperature Superheater Tube in a Power Plant
conference_papers.summary: A T91/TP347H dissimilar steel butt joint of high temperature superheater tube of a 630 MW power plant unit was found cracked after 100,000 hours of operation. The reasons of cracking were analyzed by macroscopic examination, chemical composition analysis, metallographic examination, hardness test, scanning electron microscope (SEM) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) analysis. The results show that the misuse of welding materials is the root cause of the cracking. The excessive protrusion of the weld root and abnormal carburizing layer near the fusion line are the direct causes of the cracking. In view of the causes of cracking, it is suggested to strengthen the supervision of welding process, improve the welding quality and strictly control the heat treatment process.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (RAAI)
conference_papers.title: Coverage Area-Based Weighted Mean Yielding Position Exploration Method for Resolving Deadlocks Among Autonomous Robots
conference_papers.summary: When introducing multiple autonomous service robots, collision avoidance, and deadlock resolution among robots are crucial for efficient navigation. In situations where robots are entirely deadlocked, assigning priority among robots and performing yielding maneuvers is necessary to allow other robots to exit. Previously, for such yielding actions, static waiting positions were pre-set, or collision-free avoidance positions were dynamically calculated based on the relative speeds of robots. However, pre-setting, fixed waiting positions could lead to increased installer fatigue as it depends on the spatial structure of the operating environment, and considering the other robot's speed was ineffective in narrow and long corridors. This paper introduces an algorithm that identifies potential yielding positions within the coverage area and dynamically generates an appropriate yielding position by considering their weighted average. This reduces the need for manual configuration of static positions and ensures effective yielding maneuvers, even in long, narrow corridors where only one robot can navigate.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
conference_papers.title: Construction Strategy of Machine Learning Sample Database for Intersection Signal Timing Optimization Based on VISSIM Simulation
conference_papers.summary: The optimization of intersection signal timing based on artificial intelligence has emerged as a prominent research area in ITS. However, traditional surveys for obtaining sample data of intersection signal timing schemes suffer from issues such as low efficiency, lack of comprehensiveness, and difficulty in evaluation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sample database construction strategy of machine learning for intersection signal timing optimization based on the VISSIM simulation method. Firstly, a Python-VISSIM simulation platform is established using the COM interface provided by VISSIM. Further, taking a typical crossroad as an example, the optimal timing scheme is simulated under different traffic flow scenarios to generate an initial sample data set, where the optimal scheme is evaluated by the average queue length of all approaches. Finally, the Webster model is employed to validate the rationality of the initial sample set, thereby constructing a machine learning sample database for signal timing optimization. The proposed strategy comprehensively considers various scenarios and adopts an automated approach, offering advantages such as high efficiency, comprehensive and diverse data, and ease of evaluation compared to traditional surveys.
