conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Vision-Based Cooperative Surrounding and Fault-Tolerant Control for Heterogeneous Robotic Swarms with Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance
conference_papers.summary: In heterogeneous robot swarm encirclement missions, the presence of malfunctioning robots (which act as dynamic obstacles) and high energy consumption present significant challenges. This paper proposes a novel vision-based coordination strategy to address these issues. Specifically, we introduce the YOLO-AlignNet model, which enables robots to accurately identify malfunctioning peers in real-time for effective collision avoidance. Concurrently, a visual attention mechanism is employed to selectively focus on key neighboring robots, thereby optimizing communication paths and significantly reducing energy consumption. Furthermore, the traditional artificial potential field method is enhanced by integrating these visual cues, allowing the swarm to dynamically and efficiently encircle moving targets while avoiding both static and dynamic obstacles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy not only maintains stable encirclement formation but also achieves a substantial reduction in overall energy expenditure, validating its effectiveness and practicality for intelligent swarm control systems.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Target Recognition and Precision Strike with Intelligent FPV Drones
conference_papers.summary: Intelligent FPV (First-Person View) drones, as novel unmanned platforms with autonomous perception and decision-making capabilities, demonstrate significant potential in the field of time-sensitive target strikes. Addressing the precision strike requirements of intelligent FPV drones, this paper designs a complete system integrating target recognition and terminal guidance. The system utilizes YOLOv8 and DeepSort algorithms to achieve rapid target recognition and stable tracking, and designs a terminal guidance algorithm based on the proportional navigation law. Through practical flight tests, the drone successfully accomplished the entire mission profile from autonomous takeoff and route tracking to terminal attack. The strike accuracy against the target was better than 0.5 meters, effectively proving the system's good performance in terms of real-time capability, accuracy, and reliability, providing key technical support for the practical application of intelligent unmanned platforms.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Road Continuity-Aware Network for Road Extraction from High-resolution Remote Sensing Images
conference_papers.summary: Automated road extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery holds significant application value for navigation and geographic information system (GIS) updates. However, extracting accurate and complete roads remains a considerable challenge due to the complex road topology and various background interferences. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Road Continuity-Aware Network (RCANet) for complete and continuous road extraction. The RCANet generally adopts an encoder-decoder architecture. Firstly, the encoder is based on the ResNet-34 backbone to learn road features from original high-resolution remote sensing images. Secondly, for the skip connection between the encoder and decoder, an Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) block is devised with channel and spatial attention mechanisms to dynamically select and fuse features from different levels and effectively mitigate the semantic gap between them. In addition, the road continuity-aware decoder module integrates deformable convolution and criss-cross attention mechanism for accurate road feature decoding. The deformable convolution adaptively captures local directional context of roads, while the attention mechanism efficiently models global dependencies to reconnect broken road segments. Experiments on the public CHN6-CUG dataset demonstrate that RCANet significantly outperforms existing methods in F1-score, Intersection over Union (IoU), and mean IoU (mIoU), generating more complete and topologically continuous road extraction results.
institutions: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Research on Sea Ice Image Segmentation Algorithm Based on Improved PSPNet
conference_papers.summary: The rapid melting of Arctic sea ice and the scarcity of high-resolution hydrological data pose significant challenges to the safety of navigation and construction for key vessels, such as dredging ships, operating along the Arctic route. Traditional sea ice monitoring methods often struggle with low segmentation accuracy and blurred edges in complex polar environments. To address these limitations, this paper introduces an enhanced sea ice segmentation algorithm based on PSPNet, incorporating an attention mechanism. The proposed model employs a lightweight backbone network constructed with depthwise separable convolutions, which substantially reduces computational complexity and improves deployment efficiency on resource-limited platforms, without compromising feature extraction performance. Furthermore, a dual-path attention mechanism, encompassing both channel and spatial attention, is integrated to enhance the model's focus on critical sea ice features, thereby refining environmental perception for dredging operations. Experimental validation on a shipborne floating ice image dataset demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach: the improved model achieves a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 97.8% in floating ice segmentation, surpassing the original PSPNet by 5.8 percentage points. Edge detection accuracy is improved by 20.3%, and the model exhibits strong robustness in challenging scenarios prevalent in dredging operations, such as broken and thin ice. This method provides a core technological foundation for developing high-precision hydrological monitoring and prediction platforms, ultimately supporting dredging enterprises in achieving refined sea ice forecasting, ensuring navigational safety, and optimizing operational windows for engineering vessels in the Arctic, thus contributing to the development of the "Polar Silk Road."

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation Based on Text Guidance and Pseudo-label Optimization
conference_papers.summary: Medical image segmentation is a key technology in computer-aided diagnosis and surgical navigation, and its accuracy directly affects the reliability of clinical diagnosis and treatment. In abdominal CT imaging, due to the limited grayscale differences between adjacent organs and imaging noise interference, boundary blurring often occurs, leading to misclassification and missed classification of the segmentation model in the edge regions of organs. This issue has become a core bottleneck restricting segmentation accuracy and clinical application value. Despite significant progress in automatic segmentation methods based on deep learning, there are still problems of insufficient recognition and limited robustness in dealing with boundary blurring. To address this, this paper proposes a method combining text guidance and pseudo-label optimization based on the MedSAM large model. Firstly, logical relationship cues are designed for the shape, position, and proximity of the target organs to enhance the model's understanding of the structural semantics between organs. Subsequently, the CLIP pre-trained model is used to encode the cues and integrate them into MedSAM for model fine-tuning, enabling text information to more accurately guide the localization of blurry boundary regions. Finally, a pseudo-label optimization strategy is introduced to effectively alleviate the label noise problem caused by blurry edges, thereby improving the quality of pseudo-labels and segmentation robustness. Experimental verification on the public abdominal CT dataset LiTS shows that, compared to the baseline model, the proposed method improves the Dice coefficient by 2.65% and reduces the ASSD metric by 0.12 cm, significantly enhancing segmentation accuracy under boundary blurring conditions. The research results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively alleviate boundary blurring in abdominal medical image segmentation and show potential application value in improving clinical practicality.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: MTC-CycleGAN: A Masked Text Collaborative Guidance-Based Data Augmentation Algorithm for Magnetic Tile Surface Defects
conference_papers.summary: Magnetic tiles are the core magnetic components of electric motors, and surface defects affect equipment performance. However, industrial visual inspection faces two major bottlenecks: the high cost of obtaining defect samples and the scarcity of training data, as well as a long-tail distribution of samples. To address this, this paper proposes the MTC-CycleGAN defect image generation algorithm, based on a mask-text collaborative guidance approach. This algorithm designs a dual-modal guidance mechanism to achieve controllable defect generation and introduces a Balanced Channel Space Attention Module to enhance detail representation. Experiments show that the defect images generated by MTC-CycleGAN have clearer textures and more precise localization, with a 12.74% reduction in the average FID compared to CycleGAN and a 6.26% reduction in LPIPS. Validation on three models, including YOLOv11-seg, demonstrates that this algorithm can effectively solve the data imbalance problem and improve detection accuracy.
institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: MFOV: Multi-Dimensional Feature Optimization for Failure Detection and Reasoning in Robotic Manipulation
conference_papers.summary: Recent advances have demonstrated that robots can leverage Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to detect the outcomes of action executions and provide corresponding explanations when failures occur. However, methods relying heavily on data collection and model fine-tuning face significant limitations. In particular, when transferring fault detecting and reasoning capabilities to new scenarios with large domain discrepancies, model performance often degrades substantially. To address this issue, this paper explores an alternative approach that enhances the fault detecting and reasoning capabilities of VLMs without requiring additional data collection or fine-tuning. We propose a multidimensional feature enhancement method that optimizes spatial, semantic, and temporal features of the input images to improve the detecting and reasoning performance of VLMs. Experiments conducted on the RoboFail dataset demonstrate that, without any model fine-tuning, our method improves the task success rate by 16%.
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Fault Diagnosis of New Energy Vehicle Motor Controllers Based on Machine Learning Algorithms
conference_papers.summary: The global penetration rate of new energy vehicles continues to rise. As a central component of the power system, the motor controller is responsible for the conversion of DC-AC electrical energy and the control of motor speed and torque. Its reliability directly affects the safe operation of the vehicle. Therefore, optimizing the fault diagnosis algorithm has become a key issue. To address the pain points of existing algorithms in the fault diagnosis of motor controllers, this paper proposes the APO-Transformer classification algorithm. Firstly, a correlation analysis is conducted, and then multiple machine learning algorithms are introduced for comparative experiments. The results show that APO-Transformer performs the best in various evaluation indicators. The accuracy rate, recall rate, precision rate and F1 value all reach 99.1%, and the AUC is as high as 99.9%, which is significantly better than other models. The core indicators of Random Forest and ExtraTrees were both 98.2%, and the AUCs were 99.4% and 98.2% respectively, performing second. The AUC of XGBoost and GBDT is both 98.7%, with the rest of the indicators ranging from 95% to 96.3%. The AUC of CatBoost is between 95.9% and 96%, with an AUC of 97.9%. The AUC of the decision tree is 93.2%, with an AUC of 95.7%. However, the core classification indicators of SVM are only 74.2% to 78.3%, and the overall performance gap is the largest. This algorithm provides a high-precision solution for the fault diagnosis of motor controllers and has significant practical value in enhancing the reliability of the power system of new energy vehicles and ensuring driving safety.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Enhancing Stereo Matching with Multi-Scale Selective Attention Aggregation
conference_papers.summary: Stereo matching is a fundamental task in computer vision, enabling applications such as robotics, autonomous systems, and augmented reality to gain depth understanding. Currently, the design and development of an accurate and efficient stereo matching model have remained an active area of research with significant potential for advancement. In this work, we introduce a high-performance stereo matching model that improves the conventional cost-volume-based pipeline by integrating a Selective Attention (SA) module into the 3D aggregation block. SA leverages a dual-branch structure with two distinct kernel sizes to capture multi-scale contextual information. It effectively fuses fine-grained spatial details from initial features with broader contextual cues in the 3D aggregation block. The module employs a dynamic selection mechanism to adjust kernel weights adaptively, enhancing the model’s capability to handle occlusions, textureless regions, and varying object scales. The source code will be publicly available at https://github.com/M2219/StereoSA.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Diffusion-based Evidence-Anchored Purification for Adversarially Robust Image Manipulation Localization
conference_papers.summary: When adversarial noise is injected into a manipulated image, the resulting perturbations distort the subtle cues that image manipulation localization (IML) relies on, making the IML task markedly harder. Although generic adversarial purification can remove such perturbations, it often removes manipulation-related evidence at the same time, degrading IML performance. We introduce Diffusion-based Evidence-Anchored Purification (DEAP), a defense that turns diffusion purification into an evidence-aware procedure. The Evidence Subspace Projector (ESP) learns an orthonormal basis that captures manipulation-relevant variation and yields a compact evidence embedding. Evidence-Anchored Energy Guidance (EAEG) anchors each diffusion state to a robust ESP-derived evidence embedding and performs energy guidance by injecting the negative gradient of an anchor-and-smoothness energy into every reverse step. Experiments show that DEAP consistently raises robustness against strong, adaptive attacks while maintaining clean-image localization, demonstrating that diffusion purification can be made evidence-preserving rather than merely noise-averse.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Underwater Target Detection Based on Enhanced YOLOv9 Model
conference_papers.summary: Underwater target detection is crucial for ocean exploration, yet Traditional ground target detection method struggle under harsh underwater conditions. Issues such as inconsistent lighting, low contrast, and physical obstacles can obscure targets, making it particularly difficult for conventional approaches to accurately detect low-resolution images and small targets, which are further compromised by ambient noise and variable target sizes. These challenges impede accurate feature extraction and slow the detection process. Consequently, advanced detection technologies are imperative to overcome these obstacles and drive progress in marine environmental engineering. In light of the aforementioned challenges, we present an improved iteration of YOLOv9, named the enhanced YOLOv9 model, tailored to bolster detection precision for images of low resolution and minute targets. This upgraded model provides the capacity to fine-tune parameters and modify the shapes of convolutional kernels, leading to a decrease in the computational burden on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Such optimization notably enhances the efficacy of target detection in complex underwater settings, effectively tackling inherent obstacles and fortifying the model's overall resilience. Ablative experiments on Underwater Robot Picking Contest (URPC) and Underwater Object Detection (UOD) datasets and comparative analysis of current mainstream detectors show that this model demonstrates clear superiority in both detection capability and efficiency.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Tightly-coupled Lidar-Visual-Inertial SLAM for Mobile Robot
conference_papers.summary: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) enables robots to perform localization and mapping in unknown environments. Currently, mainstream single-sensor Lidar SLAM (Visual SLAM) tends to diverge and fail when faced with unstructured or textureless scenes. To address this issue, this paper proposes a robust tightly-coupled Lidar-Vision-Inertial Odometry framework (LRI-LVIO) that achieves high-precision and robust SLAM. LRI-LVIO consists of two subsystems: a visual-inertial system and a lidar-inertial system. These two subsystems are tightly coupled through an error-state iterative Kalman filter, allowing one subsystem to maintain stable operation even if the other fails, thus enhancing the robustness of SLAM in textureless and featureless environments. Additionally, the depth of visual feature points is recovered using lidar point cloud information, improving the algorithm's efficiency and accuracy. Finally, LRI-LVIO incorporates loop closure detection based on lidar point cloud keyframes, further reducing cumulative errors and enhancing localization precision. Experiments conducted in various indoor and outdoor environments show that by combining the advantages of each sensor, LRI-LVIO achieves higher accuracy and stronger robustness compared to single-sensor SLAM.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: MMFA-Net: Multi-Modal Feature Learning and Multi-Head Fuse Attention for Image Manipulation Detection and Localization
conference_papers.summary: With the advent of various advanced image processing techniques and the increasingly low manipulation threshold, Image Manipulation Detection and Localization (IMDL) has become a complex and challenging task. Previous studies have shown the importance of manipulation artifacts in the IMDL problem. However, existing methods often struggle to capture effective artifacts when addressing with refined forgery (post-processed forgery). In this paper, we introduce MMFA-Net, a novel approach for IMDL. We extract RGB features, Laplacian high-frequency features, Bayar statistical anomaly features, and manipulation imprint from the image through the Multi-modal Feature Extractor module, concatenating them as multi-modal feature inputs to capture manipulation edge artifacts, which are increasingly difficult to detect in image manipulation. In addition, we propose an innovative Multi-head Fuse Attention (MFA) module. Building on the backbone network's ability to model inconsistencies between original and tampered regions at coarse-to-fine granularities, the MFA module can more effectively capture contextual dependencies in the spatial dimensions and inter-channel correlations for more precise localization. The performance on several public datasets demonstrates that the proposed network outperforms existing SOTA models and remains robust against refined forgery.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Fast Correction and Stitching Algorithm for Fisheye Images
conference_papers.summary: Fisheye cameras, with their ultra-wide-angle field of view, can capture a larger scene in a single shot compared to traditional lenses. This capability makes them highly valuable in areas such as security surveillance, panoramic photography, autonomous driving, and robot navigation. However, building an efficient and accurate visual system is crucial for realizing these applications. This paper proposes an improved algorithm based on fisheye image correction and stitching. First, a fast fisheye image distortion correction method is introduced to eliminate the severe distortion caused by the fisheye lens. Then, the o-FAST algorithm is used for feature point detection, ensuring rotational invariance of the feature points, and the KNN algorithm is employed for initial matching. On this basis, the PROSAC algorithm is applied to remove incorrect matches and compute the homography matrix between images. Finally, seamless image stitching is achieved using a gradual weighted fusion method. The research results demonstrate that this method significantly improves both image quality and computational efficiency, making it effective for generating and processing panoramic images. Experimental results further confirm that the method enhances stitching accuracy while also increasing processing speed, showcasing its high practical value.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Enhanced YOLOv8 Model for Drug Detection in Compound Robot System
conference_papers.summary: The sudden emergence of the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) has had a catastrophic impact on global populations, with healthcare workers (HCWs) facing unprecedented challenges due to the high infection rate among this group. The deployment of composite robots, which combine the functions of fast movement and flexible grasping, can potentially address the shortage of HCWs and facilitate the delivery of essential medical supplies and other tasks in isolation environments. This paper presents a key technology for composite robots to perform the function of picking up and delivering medicines. The identification and detection of medicines is a crucial aspect of this technology. To enhance the accuracy and real-time performance of composite robots in detecting medicines, a target detection algorithm based on the improvement of YOLOv8 for medicines boxes is proposed. Firstly, a global attention mechanism (GAM) is incorporated into the backbone network to enhance the network's focus on crucial information through cross-latitude information interaction and to retain channel and spatial information to a greater extent, thereby improving the ability of the backbone network to extract features. Secondly, the weighted bidirectional feature pyramid network(BiFPN) is integrated into the neck network, which facilitates multi-scale feature fusion by assigning appropriate weights to each input feature and refining the feature fusion process. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an average detection accuracy (mAP) of 99.20%, a recall of 98.90%, and an F1 score of 99.05%, while maintaining a detection speed of 158.73 FPS. In comparison to YOLOv6, YOLOv8n, and YOLOv8s, the proposed model exhibits the highest accuracy index and satisfactory overall performance, aligning with the requirements of composite robots for rapid and precise identification of medicines. The model enables the composite robot to accurately detect and identify medicines in real time within an isolated ward environment.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Cross-modal Frequency-aware Transformer for Multimodal Medical Image Fusion
conference_papers.summary: Fusing multimodal medical images seeks to amalgamate their unique informational strengths, thereby enhancing the precision of clinical diagnostics and the accuracy of surgical navigation. The resulting image quality in multimodal fusion is contingent upon the characteristics derived from individual modalities and the strategies employed for integrating this diverse data. Nevertheless, current deep learning-driven fusion techniques, although adept at harnessing the semantic aspects of each imaging mode, struggle to differentiate between the beneficial low-frequency and high-frequency details within each modality. This limitation hinders their ability to capture comprehensive global insights and to achieve dynamic, context-aware fusion. To address these issues, we introduce an innovative fusion framework that utilizes Fourier transforms and incorporates a cross-modal frequency-aware transformer. This framework includes a frequency-aware cross-attention mechanism for adaptive feature fusion across modalities by exchanging keys and queries between spatial and frequency domains. It also computes cross-attention scores to facilitate the integration of spatial and frequency data. Additionally, we employ a hybrid approach of gradient preservation and transformers for feature extraction, capturing both local specifics and global information. Our model surpasses existing methods assessments, markedly improving fused image quality.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Advanced Object Detection and Pose Estimation with Hybrid Task Cascade and High-Resolution Networks
conference_papers.summary: In the field of computer vision, 6D object detection and pose estimation are critical for applications such as robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. Traditional methods often struggle with achieving high accuracy in both object detection and precise pose estimation simultaneously. This study proposes an improved 6D object detection and pose estimation pipeline based on the existing 6D-VNet framework, enhanced by integrating a Hybrid Task Cascade (HTC) and a High-Resolution Network (HRNet) backbone. By leveraging the strengths of HTC’s multi-stage refinement process and HRNet’s ability to maintain high-resolution representations, our approach significantly improves detection accuracy and pose estimation precision. Furthermore, we introduce advanced post-processing techniques and a novel model integration strategy that collectively contribute to superior performance on public and private benchmarks. Our method demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art models, making it a valuable contribution to the domain of 6D object detection and pose estimation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: A Method for Nuclear Power Pipeline Weld Seam Recognition Based on Structured Light Multidimensional Information Fusion
conference_papers.summary: This paper presents an automated method for precise pipeline weld identification and measurement using autonomous robots in nuclear power environments. It addresses challenges related to initial shooting exposure, camera angle, and distance from the environment by employing adaptive data collection techniques. These methods adjust exposure based on statistical brightness information from color images captured by a structured light camera. By detecting the pipeline model in threedimensional point cloud data, optimal camera positions and postures are determined for high-quality data acquisition. Geometric features are extracted from the point cloud data to create a geometric feature response map projected onto a twodimensional image, which is fused with color features to generate a grayscale fusion map. Image recognition algorithms identify weld areas, enabling precise three-dimensional measurements. Experimental results confirm the method’s effectiveness in improving data quality and achieving accurate weld seam identification and measurement.
institutions: Research Institute of Nuclear Power Operation

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: 3D Reconstruction of Large-scale Head Surface with a Binocular Camera in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Navigation
conference_papers.summary: In image-guided TMS navigation, markerless registration methods use the head surface to match the tracking system space with the image space. Large-scale head surface is beneficial for improving registration accuracy. Currently, most 3D cameras have a limited view field and cannot reconstruct large-scale head surface with a single shot. Extra tracking devices are needed to stitch several single-shot 3D surfaces into a large-scale one. To simplify the above point cloud stitching process, an automatic 3D reconstruction method for awake TMS patients is proposed to obtain head surfaces without extra tracking devices. Experimental results show the accuracy of the reconstruction can reach 1.39 mm and registration is quicker and simpler in repeated TMS treatment sessions.

conference_papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
conference_papers.title: Retraction Notice: Rice Impact Illness Acknowledgment Employing a Profound Convolutional Neural Arrange

conference_papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
conference_papers.title: Marine Debris Detection Model with Custom Dataset Using Instance Segmentation
conference_papers.summary: Object detection and instance segmentation are fundamental task in computer vision with applications ranging from autonomous driving to robotics. In this study, presented a custom dataset implementation on Mask R-CNN model, for object detection and instance segmentation. Our dataset images acquired from Motobu beach, Okinawa, Japan. Used to CV AT (Computer Vision Annotation Tool) for annotation. Containing a diverse range of objects of interest. Coastal debris affects marine ecosystem. The standard responses set in SGDs projects involve cutting down plastic waste at the source, beach cleanups, use of the circular economy, recycling, education, and a reduction in packaging, among other solutions. We fine-tuned the Mask R-CNN architecture using transfer learning techniques, initializing the model with weights pretrained on a large-scale dataset. Our proposed model is based on instance segmentation Mask R-CNN and SIFT (Scale invariant features transform) matching deep learning neural network. The results showed successfully recognize seven categories of marine debris, using a specific custom dataset. Marine debris global environmental issue and debris detection challenging, because of weather condition like (cloud, shine, and sunset), occulated and small size object, long distance from fix camera. Debris issues not only beaches but also under water and any localization. when the flood affects any area in the world, garbage is accumulated into deep sea. We developed a deep learning-based Mask R-CNN project for the marine environment auto-clean and multi-class classification process of marine debris detection from (Kakaxi fixed camera) images.

conference_papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
conference_papers.title: Exploring the Frontier of Object Detection: A Deep Dive into YOLOv8 and the COCO Dataset
conference_papers.summary: The field of computer vision has recently widened to incorporate object identification, which has significant impacts in areas such as autonomous vehicles, robotics, security, and healthcare. This research review and analysis look at how well YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once), the latest version of the popular object recognition model, does on the COCO data set. The purpose of this research is to learn about the YOLOv8 architecture, its improvements over previous versions, the COCO data set's make-up and evaluation metrics, and their strengths and weaknesses. From its first version through YOLOv8, the paper discusses the YOLO architecture's core features and enhancements. To establish a benchmark, the YOLOv8 model is compared to other top-tier object detection models as Faster R-CNN, SSD, and EfficientDet. The COCO data set is investigated in detail, including an overview of its pictures, annotations, item categories, data collection, and annotation procedure, and the evaluation criteria used to test object identification algorithms on this data set. The study also discusses YOLOv8 architecture and performance limits and COCO data set biases, data distribution, and annotation quality. Discussing the difficulties of generalizing YOLOv8 for diverse object detection tasks. YOLOv8 and the COCO data set are useful in real-world applications and case studies. The study concludes by offering possible enhancements for the YOLOv8 architecture, ideas for extending the COCO data set and assessment metrics and analysing upcoming trends in object identification research and their implications for YOLOv8 and COCO. This comprehensive review analysis helps object detection researchers, practitioners, and industry professionals choose models, datasets, and evaluation methods for their applications.

conference_papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
conference_papers.title: A Review on Anti-Spoofing : Face Manipulation and Liveness Detection
conference_papers.summary: The latest developments in deep generative networks have greatly improved the quality of generating life-like fake face videos. Face digital manipulation such as DeepFakes, FaceSwap, and Face2Face are critical issues for automated face recognition systems as it detrimentally affects their performance. To tackle this difficulty, face anti-spoofing is utilized which is a task to prevent unauthorized entry by breaching facial recognition systems using a mask, photo, video or another substitute for a legitimate person's face. The review paper examines the problems and solutions explored in the domain of digital face manipulation, as well as the notion of liveliness detection and numerous aspects and cues that can be used to determine the authenticity of a face. The review is organized into sections, discussing face manipulation techniques, liveness detection using eye blinking, and finally a hybrid system is proposed that considers both face manipulation and liveness detection to strengthen existing solutions. It aims to enhance the security and reliability of facial recognition technology in various applications.
institutions: Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: YOLO-Substation: Inspection Target Detection in Complex Environment Based on Improved YOLOv7
conference_papers.summary: Substations play a vital role in the field of electrical power production. In order to efficiently inspect substation equipment in complex environment using inspection robots, an target detection model based on YOLOv7, named YOLO-Substation, is proposed. To tackle the problem of feature degradation during training, a deformable convolution module is integrated into the backbone network, adapting to features of varying shapes and sizes. Furthermore, AAM is introduced to selectively emphasize crucial information from the input, improving the model’s performance in complex and dynamic backgrounds. The experiments demonstrate that the YOLO-Substation model can achieve accurate detection of inspection targets, with an mAP of 82.7%, an F1 score of 87.6%, and a recognition accuracy of 97.5%, surpassing other mainstream object detection models.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: TransGait: Vision Transformer Based Gait Recognition Network
conference_papers.summary: Gait, the distinctive walking pattern of an individual, stands out as a human modality that can be effortlessly captured even with low-resolution cameras from a considerable distance. Gait patterns are unique to each individual and hard to fake. Gait recognition is a cutting-edge biometric technology that focuses on identifying individuals based on their distinctive walking patterns. Therefore, its fields of application span a number of domains, encompassing healthcare, robotics, automation, as well as security and access control. The origin of this investigation stems from challenges faced by high school and college residents contending with forgotten identification credentials, compounded by the intricacies of facial recognition in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, especially in instances involving mask-obscured facial features. This paper proposes Transformer based Gait Recognition Network (Occlusion-TransGait), which combining temporal Vision Transformer (VIT) and Swin Transformer based structure and occlusion masked datasets. Utilizing the Swin Transformer model, the study achieved enhanced precision, with improvements of 0.4% for NM, 1.0% for BG, and 1.4% for CL. Furthermore, this paper presents a novel open-set detection technique for recognizing potential threats arising from unidentified individuals. Finally, this research embraces an inventive strategy that integrates human detection, tracking, and segmentation to create an end-to-end pipeline well-suited for implementation on the NVIDIA Jetson platform. This research promises a transformative impact on gait recognition systems, enhancing their effectiveness and security, and paving the way for stronger and more efficient biometric solutions.
institutions: NSF NCAR Computational & Information Systems Laboratory

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Research on indoor robot navigation algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning
conference_papers.summary: Highly intelligent robot is the trend in the new round of development, and it is also the ultimate goal of robot navigation technology research.The ability to learn is an important embodiment of robot intelligence.Autonomous navigation is the basic function of indoor mobile robots[1]and it is the premise and key technology to realize the autonomy and intelligence of robots.With the continuous development of robot-related technologies and the continuous expansion of application scope, the tasks faced by robots are more challenging, and the work scenes are increasingly complex and diversified, which puts forward new requirements and challenges for navigation technology. Indoor robot navigation systems need not only to maintain accuracy and stability in fixed scenes, but also to be able to handle dynamic changes in the environment, and to take into account safety and the impact on human comfort in an environment that coexists with humans.This paper takes the indoor mobile robot platform as the research object[2], introduces the machine learning algorithm based on neural network into the navigation task[3], utilizes the existing research achievements in the field of deep learning to build a robot navigation system based on different learning modes, and endows the robot with intelligent perception ability and navigation strategy learning ability[4].

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: Research on Warehouse Object Detection for Mobile Robot Based on YOLOv5
conference_papers.summary: In view of the lack of public datasets for object detection in warehouse environment, a large number of images containing cargos, trays and forklifts in real warehouse environment is collected and annotated by cameras, creating a warehouse object dataset. At the same time, in view of the low detection accuracy of traditional object detection algorithms in warehouse environment, the YOLOv5 series models are applied to warehouse environment, and the models are trained and optimized on the warehouse object dataset created by ourselves, achieving accurate detection of warehouse object. The mAP@50 of the YOLOv5 series models has reached more than 99%. Among them, the mAP@50-90 of the YOLOv5l model and YOLOv5x model is about 92%, which is better than other models. The YOLOv5m model is also deployed on the self-designed mobile robot, realizing the automatic detection of warehouse object. The experimental results show that YOLOv5m has achieved a satisfactory warehouse object detection effect, and it has certain practical value in the field of warehouse object detection.
institutions: Guiyang Institute of Humanities and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
conference_papers.title: A Generic LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration Method base on Lightweight SAM
conference_papers.summary: In the domains of autonomous driving and robotic vision, camera and LIDAR, as core sensors, played an imperative roles where the precise fusion of their data had a significant impact on environmental perception. Accordingly, the accurate calibration of external parameters to achieve data fusion emerged as a crucial step to enhance system performance. This paper proposed a zero-shot, target-less and rapid method for calibrating the external parameter of the LiDAR-Camera, based on the distillation of the large model, Segment Anything Model (SAM). Initially, the SAM model was distilled, resulting in a lightweight image segmentation model that could rapidly segment objects in any scene and obtain a mask for each object. Subsequently, a process for handling LiDAR point cloud data was designed, which could obtain the attributes of each point cloud and adaptively acquire the weights of each attribute based on the scene. After processing the image and point cloud data, the external parameter from the LiDAR to the camera was optimized by maximizing the consistency of the point cloud projection to the segmented image mask. The proposed method was evaluated on numerous public datasets and self-built datasets, and compared with other advanced methods. The results indicated that our method exhibited higher accuracy and speed in different scenes.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Vision-Enhanced System For Human-Robot Disassembly Factory Cells: Introducing A New Screw Dataset
conference_papers.summary: Waste from electrical and electronic equipment is exacerbating the global environmental crisis. There is an urgent need to build a robust infrastructure capable of providing effective e-waste disposal options. In this work, a novel hybrid human-robot and system-agnostic application for relevant waste disassembly and recycling has been developed. Working on cells, collaborative robots, enhanced with state-of-the-art computer vision capabilities, can achieve near-real-time performance and high precision in the disassembly process. Additionally, a new screw dataset suitable for three separate computer vision tasks, namely instance segmentation, object detection, and semantic segmentation, is introduced to facilitate future research, which can be utilized almost for any screwing/unscrewing application beyond the current disassembly topic. Experiments demonstrating the robustness of the visual object detection and robotic 3D deprojection modules, which are the core aspects of the proposed architecture, have been conducted.
institutions: Centre for Research and Technology Hellas

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Research on Ship’s Officer Behavior Identification Based on Mask R-CNN
conference_papers.summary: The negligence and inattention of the navigators on duty are the main causes of ship accidents. Based on the CCTV records of the bridge, the identification on human behaviors on duty has high value and significance. In this paper, a human behavior recognition method based on Mask R-CNN and a knowledge-based model is proposed. At the very beginning, the images of bridges collected by the camera are used as the input, the keypoints are extracted through a convolution neural network. Subsequently, the feature distribution of the keypoints of the k-nearest neighbor algorithm is then analyzed by clustering, which realizes the real-time online recognition of common behaviors such as walking, standing, sitting, steering and looking through the mobile phone, looking out and napping. At the final step, the proposed method was validated on the samples of the ferry ship from Zhoushan, Zhejiang, China. In the validation, the one-time recognition accuracy of this method was 82%, and the rolling recognition rate had reached almost 99%, which might significantly improve the safety of navigation.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Research on Mobile Robot Localization and Mapping Method for Underground Long-Narrow Tunnels
conference_papers.summary: The underground roadway scene has few features, which is a typical degraded scene. The commonly used GPS localization methods on the ground can not be directly applied, which brings great challenges to the localization and mapping of mobile robots. This paper proposes to build a laser-UWB fusion slam system to realize the localization and mapping of underground environment to solve the problems. The EKF based method was used to fuse IMU observation information to construct UWB pseudo GNSS localization system. The localization constraints provided by UWB localization system were added to the pose optimization constraints using the graph optimization-based framework and provide a reliable initial estimate for scan matching. Then using the original point cloud preprocessing method, i.e., de-distortion, radius filtering, and voxel grid filtering, combines the optimized pose for accurate pose estimation and mapping. Finally, the field experiment shows that the proposed method is closer to the actual trajectory and there is no cumulative error. The odometer error in the X direction has been effectively controlled. Compared with the general slam method, it has a higher ability to resist degradation.
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Coal Mine Safety Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Recognising Known Configurations of Garments For Dual-Arm Robotic Flattening
conference_papers.summary: Robotic deformable-object manipulation is a challenge in the robotic industry because deformable objects have complicated and various object states. Predicting those object states and updating manipulation planning is time-consuming and computationally expensive. In this paper, we propose learning known configurations of garments to allow a robot to recognise garment states and choose a pre-designed manipulation plan for garment flattening.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Minimize Collision Risk Global Planner Based Voronoi Graph for Mobile Robot
conference_papers.summary: Ensure safe, reliable, fast and stable robot navigation which requires stable and efficient motion planning algorithm support. In order to reduce the collision risk during robot navigation, we propose minimize collision risk global planner for mobile robot, based on voronoi graph to extract Tyson polygon vertices. Using multiple vertices to form a planning search graph, the collision risk of each edge is calculated i.e. the integral of the distance to the obstacle is used as the weighted value of the edge, and the search is performed using A* to obtain the planning path with the lowest collision risk globally at the current moment. In order to make the planned path more consistent with robot kinematics, we designed the collision and smooth cost function to optimize the path using gradient descent, and the searched path is passed to the local planner after path smooth. The test results on the actual robot show that the robot can effectively avoid narrow areas and effectively reduce the collision rate and replanning times in dynamic environments.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Markerless Visual Servoing Using Virtual Face Tag and Image Moment Invariants
conference_papers.summary: A novel normalized-centered image moment invariant-based visual servoing scheme is presented. A fresh combination of the moments invariants is proposed for planar symmetrical objects that are parallel to the image plane at the desired position. The output of the face detection module in the image plane, that is a rectangle around the face is used as a virtual target, treated as a planar symmetrical object which always remains parallel to the image plane. The proposed method completely decouples the DoF and is 2D translation, rotation, and scaling invariant. It was experimentally validated on a real robotic arm using a haar cascade-based face detection system to accomplish visual servoing tasks for both 2D printed faces and actual 3D faces. Unlike traditional deep learning based visual servoing schemes, the proposed markerless visual servoing technique does not require a 3D model of the face or a reference image/pose at the desired position and it can also work with unfamiliar faces without prior training .
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Robotics and Systems
Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
NED University of Engineering and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Learning to Walk on Low Friction Terrain by Reinforcement Learning
conference_papers.summary: Locomotion control of legged robots has been an important topic in the field of robotic research. Its practical application in complex terrain environment is the focus and difficulty of research. In order to overcome the nonlinear dynamic characteristics of the legged robots walking on low friction terrain and obtain robustness, adaptability, the traditional controller design is too complex. We solve these problems by Reinforcement Learning (RL). Firstly, we make robot learn to walk on ordinary terrain by RL. And then with the usage of curriculum training, our robot can maintain balance on low friction terrain and adapt to terrains with the different friction coefficients. At last, we conduct a series of physical experiments on UnitreeA1 to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Intelligent Flower Detection System Based on YOLOv5s
conference_papers.summary: In order to quickly and accurately identify the flowers that meet the picking requirements by using the flower picking robot in the natural environment, an intelligent flower detection system based on YOLOv5s was proposed. In this study, the collected data sets of roses in different flowering periods are taken as the object. Aiming at the problems of fuzzy pictures, easy omission of small targets and large model size, which are difficult to be applied to embedded devices, the YOLOv5s model is improved by adding transposed convolution module, changing the weighted NMS mode to DIOU_NMS, and compressing the model through channel pruning. The experimental results show that the mAP values of four flowering periods can reach 86.6% when verified on rose data sets with different flowering periods, and the small target detection effect is significantly improved, the model size is compressed to 2.15MB, and the model parameters are reduced by 86%. And that detection effect of the flower pic robot can be effectively improved.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Design and Implementation of ROS-based 5G Operation and Maintenance Center Inspection Robot Navigation System
conference_papers.summary: To realize the intelligent navigation and safe obstacle avoidance of the intelligent inspection robot in the complex environment of the 5G operation and maintenance centers, and build an accurate environment map, This paper designs an autonomous navigation system for 5G operation and maintenance center inspection robots based on the robot operating system ROS. During the navigation process of the inspection robot in a known environment, The A* algorithm with a new heuristic function is used for global path planning, and the improved DWA algorithm is used for local path planning. Based on the traditional DWA algorithm, a new distance evaluation function is added to optimize the obstacle avoidance effect of the inspection robot. It enables the robot to reach the target point faster and safer, and conduct related simulation experiments and real-environment experiments. The experimental results show that the method can realize the real-time dynamic obstacle avoidance of the robot in complex environments and reach the endpoint, and it can be closer to the global path planned by the A* algorithm. Guarantee the global optimal route.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Deep Learning Based Binocular Detection and Localization Method for Roses
conference_papers.summary: Aiming at the problems that interfere with the distance detection of flowers, such as light changes and occlusion of branches and leaves in rose plantations, this paper proposes a deep learning-based binocular vision detection and localization method for roses in complex scenes. Firstly, the attention mechanism Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is added to the neck layer of YOLOv5 (You Only Look Once) to improve the convergence speed and detection accuracy of the model. Secondly, the Efficient Intersection over Union (EIOU) loss function is used to calculate the length and width of the target frame separately, which solves the problem of large errors in the horizontal and vertical directions. Finally, the Oriented Fast and Rotated Brief (ORB) algorithm is used for matching the feature points and the Hamming distance is added to discriminate the similarity between the descriptors, and then the target detection results are used to constrain the feature points. At the same time, the optimal feature point pair in the flower area is extracted to obtain effective parallax and realize real-time target ranging. The experimental results show that compared with the previous algorithm, the improved algorithm has a 3% increase in accuracy and a 10fps increase in speed. Within a certain range, the average relative error between the measured distance and the actual distance is less than 2%, which meets the flower detection and distance detection requirements of picking robots in rose plantations.

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: An Efficient and Accurate 3D SLAM Method for Dynamic Environment
conference_papers.summary: LiDAR-based 3D SLAM has always been one of the hotspots in the field of self-driving and mobile robots in the recent years. But how to build a robust and accurate map for a complex dynamic environment is still a challenging task, which attracts more and more attention in this community. In this paper, we proposed an efficient and accurate 3D SLAM method for complex dynamic environment, which mainly includes two stages. In the first moving object detection stage, an end-to-end full convolution semantic segmentation network (FCNN) is exploited to segment the potential moving objects accurately. Then the left point cloud is forward to the static SLAM module, which is based on direct point cloud registration method, the map is managed efficiently with the incremental kd-tree data structure. Additionally, an independent thread of the loop closure detection (LCD) based on the framework of multi-factor graph is adopted to further improve the accuracy and robustness of final outputs. With the elaborately design of the whole framework, the proposed method can work efficiently. The performance of the proposed method is validated with the benchmark dataset KITTI, the results show that by removing the dynamic objects, the stability and accuracy of SLAM can be greatly improved.
institutions: CRRC Qingdao Sifang Rolling Stock Research Institute (China)

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: Adaptive Model-free Control with Supervising Switching Technique for Robotic Manipulator with Actuator Failure
conference_papers.summary: This paper proposes a time-delay estimator-based adaptive model-free controller with supervising switching technique for robotic manipulator with actuator failure. The proposed method based on ultra local model is composed of timedelay estimator (TDE), proportion-differential control (PDC), supervising switching technique (SST) and auto-tuning algorithm based on Nussbaum function. The TDE is adopted to estimate the lumped disturbance, while PDC is designed to stabilize the closed-loop system. For better control performance when actuator failure occurs, the SST and variable adaptive gain are introduced to suppress error induced by TDE and realize fast convergence. To validate the effectiveness and superiority of the referred strategy, compared simulations are conducted via Matlab/ Simulation. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller owns high accuracy, fast convergence and less chattering in dealing with actuator failure problem.
institutions: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

conference_papers.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Computer Vision (ICRCV)
conference_papers.title: A Visual Contour-based Detection Method for Orthodontic Archwire during Robotic Bending
conference_papers.summary: With the development of robot technology, the bending of orthodontic archwire is becoming automated. Online visual measurement of archwire parameters during bending is beneficial for guaranteeing high robotic bending precision. The traditional feature point detection method is unsuitable for the visual detection of the archwire due to the lack of texture features. Aimed to realize the visual detection of this kind of tiny curved object, this paper proposes a measurement method based on contour positioning and binocular vision. Firstly, the stereo correction was performed on the original archwire image. Then the thinning algorithm was used to extract the archwire skeleton. A multi-layer contour detection method was developed to extract the bending point of the archwire. Lastly, the normalized cross-correlation coefficient is used to obtain parallax information and complete the parameter measurement. The experimental results showed that the detection method successfully extracted all feature points while the SIFT algorithm and literature [15] method did not make it. Maximum measurement error not more than 0.4mm, which is practicable for justifying the bending quality and close-loop controlling the robotic bending precision.

journal_papers.title: Ultra-wideband radar to measure in vivo muscle forces
journal_papers.summary: Accurate measures of muscle forces are critical for engineers, clinicians, and biomechanists, yet direct measurement is highly invasive, and current estimation methods remain limited in accuracy. Here, we demonstrate the application of ultra-wideband radar sensors to noninvasively estimate muscle forces by measuring changes in the electromagnetic properties of contracting muscles, in muscles with different structural properties, during various static and dynamic conditions, and in the presence of fatigue. First, we show that ultra-wideband radar scans of muscle can reliably track isometric force in a unipennate knee extensor (vastus lateralis) and a bipennate ankle dorsiflexor (tibialis anterior). Next, we integrate radar signals in machine learning and linear models to estimate muscle forces during fatiguing isometric and dynamic knee extension contractions, with exceptional accuracy. Last, we identify radar frequency-dependent effects of the relationship between muscle forces and ultra-wideband radar signals, with these effects being independent of physiological and structural features known to influence muscle force. Together, these findings establish ultra-wideband radar as a noninvasive sensor capable of quantifying in vivo muscle forces, with the potential for wearable assistive technologies, biomechanics, and rehabilitation.

journal_papers.title: Multilevel dynamics of the brain, hormones, mind, and behavior in social human-robot interaction
journal_papers.summary: As robots enter homes, workplaces, and health care settings, sustaining trust during social interaction becomes a central challenge for human-robot interaction. However, relatively little is known about how humans integrate signals across the brain, hormones, mind, and behavior when robots violate expectations or display social expressiveness. Addressing this gap, we examined how robot performance (congruent versus erroneous) and expressiveness (animated versus stationary) shape multilevel human responses during face-to-face decision-making with an embodied humanoid robot. Participants engaged with the robot in person while neural activity was monitored using functional near-infrared spectroscopy, alongside salivary oxytocin assays, self-reported trust, and behavioral influence measures. Robot errors, implemented as cooperative norm violations, reliably reduced trust and influence, establishing performance reliability as the foundation of trust. Expressiveness amplified these effects: Animated robots elicited stronger prefrontal engagement and cross-level neural-hormonal coupling. Elevated oxytocin was most strongly linked to reduced trust during expressive robot errors, alongside diminished behavioral influence. This pattern is consistent with a context-sensitive vigilance response, indicating that oxytocin in human-robot interaction may heighten sensitivity to norm violations rather than reliably promote bonding. Validation analyses provided small, directionally consistent support for this pattern under counterbalanced order and improved temporal separation. Together, these findings establish a multilevel framework for studying trust in human-robot interaction and reveal a critical design trade-off: Expressive design enhances engagement but can make robot errors disproportionately damaging to trust. These insights identify a biologically grounded boundary condition for oxytocin's role in social interaction and inform the design of socially effective and trustworthy robots.

journal_papers.title: Advances, challenges, and opportunities for legged robots
journal_papers.summary: Humanoid and quadrupedal robots have the potential to revolutionize the way we work, interact, and coexist with intelligent machines. To understand their effects on society and how they can enable scientific discovery, we assess the current capabilities of these systems along hardware, locomotion, autonomy, data, and applications. We identify recent advances and key open challenges that must be overcome to enable widespread adoption and new use cases for legged robots. Last, we provide an outlook on the future of legged robots, exploring their ethical considerations, economic potential, policy implications, and broader societal effects.

journal_papers.title: Performant robotic manipulation with real-world reinforcement learning
journal_papers.summary: Real-world robotic manipulation in homes and factories demands reliability, efficiency, and robustness that approach or surpass skilled human operators. We present a real-world reinforcement learning (RL) framework, RL-100, for achieving complete task success under a predefined evaluation protocol built on diffusion visuomotor policies. RL-100 unifies imitation and RL under a single clipped proximal policy optimization surrogate objective applied in the denoising process, yielding conservative, stable improvements across offline and online stages. To meet deployment latency, a lightweight consistency distillation compresses multistep diffusion into a one-step controller for high-frequency control. The framework is task, embodiment, and representation agnostic and supports both single-action and action-chunking control. We evaluated RL-100 on eight diverse real-robot tasks, from pushing and bowling to pouring, cloth folding, unscrewing, multistage juicing, and long-horizon box folding. Under our predefined protocol, RL-100 achieved 100% success in the evaluated trials (1000 of 1000 episodes), including up to 250 of 250 consecutive trials on one task. It matched or surpassed expert teleoperators in time to completion. Without retraining, a single policy attained ∼90% zero-shot success under environmental and dynamics shifts, adapted in a few-shot regime to substantial task variations (86.7%), and remained robust to human perturbations (about 96%). Our juicing robot served customers continuously for about 7 hours without failure when deployed zero-shot in a shopping mall. These results suggest a potential path to deployable robot learning by starting from human priors, aligning training objectives with human-grounded metrics, and reliably extending performance beyond human demonstrations.
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

journal_papers.title: Bioinspired multimodal robotics
journal_papers.summary: To survive in dynamic and unstructured environments, animals have developed extraordinary multimodal locomotion capabilities. This biological insight drives the innovation of bioinspired multimodal robots, which are defined as robotic systems integrating and transitioning between two or more distinct modes of bioinspired locomotion. This Review explores the historical progression, key design considerations, and current challenges faced in the realm of multimodal robotics. We highlight recent advancements in robotic body design, including the integration of soft materials, innovative structure repurposing strategies, and the deployment of multirobot systems. These advancements facilitate seamless mode transitions through both active and passive structural reconfigurations. In the realm of path planning and motion control, the paradigm is progressively shifting from traditional graph-based approaches and discrete controllers to learning-based frameworks. To address the current void of standardized benchmarks in this field, we propose five performance metrics-number of modes, marginal cost of modality, component repurpose percentage, transition cost, and performance improvement-that provide a quantitative framework for evaluating multimodal robots in terms of design effectiveness and operational performance. Last, we delineate a strategic roadmap for the future that advocates for the integration of physical and computational intelligence in multimodal robotics, arguing that this convergence is crucial for enabling real-time behavioral adaptations to complex environmental stimuli and thereby enhancing the robustness and functionality of multimodal robotic systems.

journal_papers.title: Allocentric teleoperation for variable perspective multirobot coordination
journal_papers.summary: The human brain can process spatial action through either egocentric (self-centered) or allocentric (environment-centered) perspectives. Despite this cognitive ability, teleoperation of robotic systems has been predominantly egocentric, wherein operators control a single robot from an inside-out perspective with limited situational overview. This paper proposes a scalable paradigm for simultaneously teleoperating multiple robotic systems from an allocentric perspective that enables a single operator to solve complex collaborative tasks. The perceptual information of all robots is fused into a joint virtual environment, which the operator can view from a top-down perspective to control the robots similar to puppets. We investigated differences between egocentric and allocentric multirobot teleoperation using both simulated and real robots. In the simulation study, study participants ( n = 15) reported a higher sense of embodiment over robot bodies when using egocentric control, enabling them to perform more precise manipulation after initial training. Using allocentric control, participants achieved speed increases of 84% in a parallelizable locomotion task and 50% in a situational overview task compared with egocentric control. Participants reported improved system usability and overview with allocentric control, and no significant differences in sense of agency were measured. These results were validated in a real-world study with two physical robots ( n = 6) and underscore the effectiveness of our allocentric teleoperation framework as a complementary approach to egocentric robotic teleoperation. Interfaces that support smooth switching between allocentric and egocentric control therefore enable operators to leverage the advantages of both paradigms depending on their specific task.

journal_papers.title: Agile perceptive multiskill locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild
journal_papers.summary: Enabling quadrupedal robots to traverse complex terrains, from rugged outdoor environments to urban landscapes, requires seamless integration of multiple motor skills, smooth transitions between gaits, and high-speed perceptive locomotion using only onboard sensors. We present APT-RL (action pretrained transformer-based reinforcement learning), a unified framework that enables multiskill locomotion to achieve high-speed traversal in complex environments through autonomous skill transitions using only onboard perception and computation. Our approach generates large-scale, feature-rich two-dimensional (2D) motion datasets through trajectory optimization with simplified dynamics. These datasets enable training of diverse, reusable locomotion skills that transfer effectively to a real quadruped robot operating on complex uneven terrains. The resulting high-quality skills serve as strong priors for efficient learning of complex downstream tasks and extend naturally to 3D environments, enabling smooth, high-speed multiskill locomotion in deployed policy. Real-world experiments demonstrate the framework's capabilities: The robot performed agile maneuvers through complex indoor obstacles and outdoor wild environments, including dynamic drop-down maneuvers that reached instantaneous peak speeds of up to 6 meters per second. A single onboard policy enabled robust traversal of diverse obstacles, including stairs, hurdles, stepping stones, gaps, and fallen branches, demonstrating the versatility and effectiveness of our approach.

journal_papers.title: A high-endurance DNA origami snap-through switch for functional nanoscale control
journal_papers.summary: Switchable elements are central to both technological devices and biological machines because they enable controlled and reversible transitions between distinct functional states. Here, we present a DNA origami-based, mechanically bistable snap-through mechanism that can be electrically controlled. This nanoscale switching mechanism exhibits long-term stability in both states in the absence of external stimuli while achieving millisecond-scale switching times upon application of an electric field. Individual devices sustain hundreds of thousands of switching cycles over several hours and remain functional for actuation over several days, offering a powerful platform for systematically studying the endurance and failure mechanisms of biomolecular nanoswitches. As a nanoscale electromechanical interface, our device enables applications in molecular information processing, optical nanodevices, and the dynamic control of chemical reactions. We demonstrate that functionalization with gold nanorods facilitates polarization-dependent optical modulation, establishing direct application in plasmonics. We further show that controlling the accessibility of a molecular binding site allows electrical regulation of reaction kinetics, thereby directly coupling mechanical switching to biochemical function.
